examples.translation: běi jīng de qiū tiān hěn měi tiān qì bù lěng bú rè fēi cháng shū fú — Autumn in Beijing is beautiful; the weather is neither cold nor hot, and very comfortable.

examples.text: 北京冬天的天气很冷，有时候下雪，北京人可以滑雪。
examples.translation: běi jīng dōng tiān de tiān qì hěn lěng yǒu shí hòu xià xuě běi jīng rén kě yǐ huá xuě — The winter weather in Beijing is very cold. Sometimes it snows and people in Beijing can ski.

examples.translation: dé zhōu de xià tiān hěn rè dōng tiān hěn shǎo xià xuě — Summer in Texas is very hot, and it rarely snows in winter.

lessons.title: 131. The book’s examples: 哪个, 怎么样 and 为什么
lessons.subtitle: 哪个同学是你们的班长？ · 你爸爸的身体怎么样？ · 为什么中国东部人口多？

explanations.title: A. 哪个 + noun, “which”
explanations.body: 哪个 is used to express “which”: 哪个 + noun?

examples.text: 哪个同学是你们的班长？
examples.translation: nǎ ge tóng xué shì nǐ men de bān zhǎng — Which student is your class leader?

examples.text: 你最喜欢哪个季节？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì xǐ huān nǎ ge jì jié — Which season do you like the best?

examples.text: 你在哪个城市出生的？
examples.translation: nǐ zài nǎ ge chéng shì chū shēng de — In which city were you born?

examples.text: 你妈妈在哪个医院工作？
examples.translation: nǐ mā mā zài nǎ ge yī yuàn gōng zuò — Which hospital does your mother work in?

explanations.title: B. Subject + 怎么样？, “how is …?”
explanations.body: 怎么样 asks how something is or what it is like, like “How is …?”

examples.text: 你老家的天气怎么样？
examples.translation: nǐ lǎo jiā de tiān qì zěn me yàng — How is the weather in your hometown?

examples.text: 你哥哥的工作怎么样？
examples.translation: nǐ gē gē de gōng zuò zěn me yàng — How is your elder brother’s job?

examples.text: 那个电脑公司怎么样？
examples.translation: nà ge diàn nǎo gōng sī zěn me yàng — How is that computer company?

examples.text: 你爸爸的身体怎么样？
examples.translation: nǐ bà bà de shēn tǐ zěn me yàng — How is your father’s health?

explanations.title: C. 为什么, “why”
explanations.body: 为什么 can be placed before or after the subject: Subject + 为什么 + predicate?

examples.text: 你为什么喜欢夏天？
examples.translation: nǐ wèi shén me xǐ huān xià tiān — Why do you like summer?

examples.text: 你妹妹为什么学中文？
examples.translation: nǐ mèi mèi wèi shén me xué zhōng wén — Why does your younger sister study Chinese?

examples.text: 为什么你弟弟没去上大学？
examples.translation: wèi shén me nǐ dì di méi qù shàng dà xué — Why didn’t your younger brother go to college?

examples.text: 为什么中国东部人口多？
examples.translation: wèi shén me zhōng guó dōng bù rén kǒu duō — Why is there a large population in eastern China?

explanations.title: Practice questions (Activities 1 and 2)
explanations.body: Ask and answer: 1. 你的老家在美国哪个州？ 2. 你是在哪个城市出生的？ 3. 你在哪个城市长大的？ 4. 你老家哪个季节最好？ 5. 你最喜欢美国哪个城市？ Then ask questions about pictures with 怎么样, as in the book’s example: Student A: 你爸爸的工作怎么样？ Student B: 很好，他是一个工程师。

examples.text: 你的老家在美国哪个州？
examples.translation: nǐ de lǎo jiā zài měi guó nǎ ge zhōu — Which state of the U.S. is your hometown in?

examples.text: 你是在哪个城市出生的？
examples.translation: nǐ shì zài nǎ ge chéng shì chū shēng de — In which city were you born?

examples.text: 你在哪个城市长大的？
examples.translation: nǐ zài nǎ ge chéng shì zhǎng dà de — In which city did you grow up?

examples.text: 你老家哪个季节最好？
examples.translation: nǐ lǎo jiā nǎ ge jì jié zuì hǎo — Which season is best in your hometown?

examples.text: 你最喜欢美国哪个城市？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì xǐ huān měi guó nǎ ge chéng shì — Which city in the U.S. do you like best?

examples.text: 你爸爸的工作怎么样？
examples.translation: nǐ bà bà de gōng zuò zěn me yàng — How is your father’s job?

examples.text: 很好，他是一个工程师。
examples.translation: hěn hǎo tā shì yí gè gōng chéng shī — Very good. He is an engineer.

Which asks “Which hospital does your mother work in?”

lessons.title: 132. The book’s examples: 最喜欢, 因为…所以, 不…也不… and 可以
lessons.subtitle: 最喜欢 · 最不喜欢 · 因为 · 所以 · 不冷也不热 · 可以

explanations.title: The superlative 最 + 喜欢
explanations.body: 最 can also precede verbs that express emotion, as in what one “most likes” or “most hates”: 最 + 喜欢 + object; 最 + 不喜欢 + object.

examples.text: 大卫最喜欢夏天，因为夏天很热，他可以游泳。
examples.translation: dà wèi zuì xǐ huān xià tiān yīn wèi xià tiān hěn rè tā kě yǐ yóu yǒng — David likes summer the most because it is very hot and he can swim.

examples.text: 方老师最喜欢北京，因为那儿是他的老家。
examples.translation: fāng lǎo shī zuì xǐ huān běi jīng yīn wèi nàr shì tā de lǎo jiā — Professor Fang likes Beijing the most because it is his hometown.

examples.text: 李丽最不喜欢她老家的冬天，因为那儿的冬天非常冷。
examples.translation: lǐ lì zuì bù xǐ huān tā lǎo jiā de dōng tiān yīn wèi nàr de dōng tiān fēi cháng lěng — Li Li dislikes the winter in her hometown the most because the winter there is extremely cold.

examples.text: 我最不喜欢我老家的夏天，因为那儿的夏天很闷热。
examples.translation: wǒ zuì bù xǐ huān wǒ lǎo jiā de xià tiān yīn wèi nàr de xià tiān hěn mēn rè — I dislike the summer in my hometown the most because the summer there is very hot and stuffy.

explanations.title: Practice with 最喜欢 (Activities 4 and 5)
explanations.body: Ask and answer, giving a reason with 因为: 你最喜欢什么语言？ 我最喜欢中文，因为…… 你最喜欢什么工作？ 我最喜欢……，因为…… 你最不喜欢什么季节？ 我最不喜欢……，因为…… Then ask at least two classmates what they like most and least, and why, and report to the class (Activity 5, a two-minute survey).

examples.text: 你最喜欢什么语言？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì xǐ huān shén me yǔ yán — Which language do you like the most?

examples.text: 我最喜欢中文，因为……
examples.translation: wǒ zuì xǐ huān zhōng wén yīn wèi — I like Chinese the most, because … (finish with your own reason)

examples.text: 你最喜欢什么工作？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì xǐ huān shén me gōng zuò — What job do you like the most?

examples.text: 你最不喜欢什么季节？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì bù xǐ huān shén me jì jié — Which season do you like the least?

explanations.title: The 因为 … (所以) construction
explanations.body: The construction connects two correlative clauses and expresses cause and result. A. 因为 by itself gives the cause (Reason, 因为 + result). B. 所以 gives the result, “so, therefore” (Reason, 所以 + result). C. Both can be used: 因为 reason, 所以 result.

examples.text: 因为我爸爸是个军官，我们都住在德州的一个军事基地。
examples.translation: yīn wèi wǒ bà bà shì gè jūn guān wǒ men dōu zhù zài dé zhōu de yí gè jūn shì jī dì — Because my father was a military officer, we all lived on a military base in Texas.

examples.text: 因为蒙特雷很少下雪，我们不能滑雪。
examples.translation: yīn wèi méng tè léi hěn shǎo xià xuě wǒ men bù néng huá xuě — Because it rarely snows in Monterey, we cannot ski.

examples.text: 我的老家冬天下雪，所以我们可以滑雪。
examples.translation: wǒ de lǎo jiā dōng tiān xià xuě suǒ yǐ wǒ men kě yǐ huá xuě — It snows in my hometown in winter, so we can ski.

examples.text: 蒙特雷的夏天很冷，所以我们不能游泳。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de xià tiān hěn lěng suǒ yǐ wǒ men bù néng yóu yǒng — Monterey is very cold in summer, so we cannot swim.

examples.text: 因为我的老家冬天下雪，所以我们可以滑雪。
examples.translation: yīn wèi wǒ de lǎo jiā dōng tiān xià xuě suǒ yǐ wǒ men kě yǐ huá xuě — Because it snows in my hometown in winter, we can ski.

examples.text: 因为蒙特雷的夏天很冷，所以我们不能游泳。
examples.translation: yīn wèi méng tè léi de xià tiān hěn lěng suǒ yǐ wǒ men bù néng yóu yǒng — Because Monterey is very cold in summer, we cannot swim.

explanations.title: Game (Activity 6)
explanations.body: Two groups take turns making sentences with “因为……，所以……”, “因为……，……” and “……，所以……”. A larger dice roll goes first, the teacher keeps time (five minutes in all) and the group with the most sentences wins.

explanations.title: The construction 不 … 也不 …
explanations.body: 不 … 也不 … negates two verbal or adjectival expressions, like “neither … nor …”: Subject + 不 + adjective/verb + 也不 + adjective/verb.

examples.text: 北京的秋天不冷也不热，非常舒服。
examples.translation: běi jīng de qiū tiān bù lěng yě bú rè fēi cháng shū fú — Autumn in Beijing is neither cold nor hot; it is very comfortable.

examples.text: 我的电脑不大也不小，我很喜欢。
examples.translation: wǒ de diàn nǎo bú dà yě bù xiǎo wǒ hěn xǐ huān — My computer is neither big nor small. I like it very much.

examples.text: 我妈妈是一个家庭妇女，不工作也不上大学。
examples.translation: wǒ mā mā shì yí gè jiā tíng fù nǚ bù gōng zuò yě bú shàng dà xué — My mother is a housewife; she neither works nor goes to college.

examples.text: 我爸爸不是医生也不是工程师，他是海军军官。
examples.translation: wǒ bà bà bú shì yī shēng yě bú shì gōng chéng shī tā shì hǎi jūn jūn guān — My father is neither a doctor nor an engineer. He is a naval officer.

explanations.title: The modal verb 可以
explanations.body: 可以 is placed before a verb and can be used to make suggestions: 可以 + verb. Activity 8 asks you to finish: 今天的天气真热，可以…… 我老家的冬天下雪，可以…… 你妈妈是中文老师，她可以…… 你爸爸是海军军官，他可以…… 我的手机号码是 831 252 7635，你可以……

examples.text: 德州的夏天很热，可以游泳。
examples.translation: dé zhōu de xià tiān hěn rè kě yǐ yóu yǒng — It is very hot during the summer in Texas, and you can swim.

examples.text: 今年的春节在星期六，你可以和你的家人一起过春节。
examples.translation: jīn nián de chūn jié zài xīng qī liù nǐ kě yǐ hé nǐ de jiā rén yì qǐ guò chūn jié — This year the Spring Festival falls on Saturday, so you can celebrate it with your family.

exercises.prompt: What does 最不喜欢 mean?
Why does David like summer the most?
options: It is hot and he can swim

exercises.prompt: Why does Professor Fang like Beijing the most?
Why does Li Li dislike the winter in her hometown the most?

options: Because the father was a military officer

exercises.prompt: Why can’t they ski in Monterey?

Which part of 因为…所以 gives the cause?
What does 我爸爸不是医生也不是工程师 say?
options: My father is not an engineer.
My father is both a doctor and an engineer.
My father is neither a doctor nor an engineer.
exercises.explanation: 不是 A 也不是 B.

options: My computer is neither big nor small.
My computer is big and small.

exercises.prompt: What does 可以 do in 德州的夏天很热，可以游泳？

exercises.promptTranslation: David likes summer the most.

exercises.prompt: 因为蒙特雷很少下雪，我们不___滑雪。
exercises.promptTranslation: Because it rarely snows in Monterey, we cannot ski.

exercises.prompt: 我的老家冬天下雪，___以我们可以滑雪。
exercises.promptTranslation: It snows in my hometown in winter, so we can ski.

exercises.promptTranslation: My mother is a housewife; she neither works nor goes to college.

lessons.title: 133. Two readings: Changchun and San Francisco
lessons.subtitle: 长春的冬天很长 · 国际滑雪节 · 旧金山没有四个季节

explanations.title: Passage 1: 长春 (Changchun)
explanations.body: Group A reads this passage. New words: 长 (cháng, long), 国际 (guójì, international). 暖和 (nuǎnhuo) is warm.

examples.text: 王老师的老家在吉林省长春市。
examples.translation: wáng lǎo shī de lǎo jiā zài jí lín shěng zhǎng chūn shì — Teacher Wang’s hometown is Changchun in Jilin Province.

examples.text: 吉林省在中国的东北，长春是吉林的省会。
examples.translation: jí lín shěng zài zhōng guó de dōng běi cháng chūn shì jí lín de shěng huì — Jilin Province is in the northeast of China, and Changchun is the capital of Jilin.

examples.text: 长春一年有四个季节。
examples.translation: cháng chūn yì nián yǒu sì gè jì jié — Changchun has four seasons a year.

examples.text: 春天很暖和，但是常常有风，四月的风最多。
examples.translation: chūn tiān hěn nuǎn huo dàn shì cháng cháng yǒu fēng sì yuè de fēng zuì duō — Spring is warm but often windy, and April has the most wind.

examples.text: 夏天不太热，很凉快，有时候下雨。
examples.translation: xià tiān bú tài rè hěn liáng kuài yǒu shí hòu xià yǔ — Summer is not too hot but cool, and sometimes it rains.

examples.text: 秋天也很凉快，是一年最舒服的季节。
examples.translation: qiū tiān yě hěn liáng kuài shì yì nián zuì shū fú de jì jié — Autumn is also cool and is the most comfortable season of the year.

examples.text: 长春的冬天很长，风很大，天气非常冷，常常下雪。
examples.translation: cháng chūn de dōng tiān hěn zhǎng fēng hěn dà tiān qì fēi cháng lěng cháng cháng xià xuě — Winter in Changchun is long and windy, the weather is extremely cold, and it often snows.

examples.text: 王老师很喜欢冬天，因为长春的冬天有国际滑雪节，王老师可以和朋友一起滑雪。
examples.translation: wáng lǎo shī hěn xǐ huān dōng tiān yīn wèi cháng chūn de dōng tiān yǒu guó jì huá xuě jié wáng lǎo shī kě yǐ hé péng yǒu yì qǐ huá xuě — Teacher Wang likes winter very much, because Changchun has an international ski festival in winter, and Teacher Wang can ski with friends.

explanations.title: Passage 2: 旧金山 (San Francisco)
explanations.body: Group B reads this passage. 旧金山 is Jiùjīnshān (San Francisco); 珍妮 is Zhēnnī (Jenny).

examples.text: 珍妮的老家在美国旧金山。
examples.translation: zhēn nī de lǎo jiā zài měi guó jiù jīn shān — Jenny’s hometown is San Francisco, U.S.

examples.text: 旧金山在美国的西部。
examples.translation: jiù jīn shān zài měi guó de xī bù — San Francisco is in the west of the U.S.

examples.text: 旧金山没有四个季节，大部分的天气很凉快，只有九月和十月很暖和，九月和十月有几天很热。
examples.translation: jiù jīn shān méi yǒu sì gè jì jié dà bù fèn de tiān qì hěn liáng kuài zhǐ yǒu jiǔ yuè hé shí yuè hěn nuǎn huo jiǔ yuè hé shí yuè yǒu jǐ tiān hěn rè — San Francisco does not have four seasons. Most of the weather is cool; only September and October are warm, and a few days in September and October are hot.

examples.text: 十一月开始下雨，十二月和一月常常下雨，一月的雨最多。
examples.translation: shí yī yuè kāi shǐ xià yǔ shí èr yuè hé yī yuè cháng cháng xià yǔ yī yuè de yǔ zuì duō — It begins to rain in November, it often rains in December and January, and January has the most rain.

examples.text: 旧金山的冬天不太冷，但是不下雪。
examples.translation: jiù jīn shān de dōng tiān bú tài lěng dàn shì bú xià xuě — Winter in San Francisco is not too cold, but it does not snow.

examples.text: 春天雨很少，有时候有风。
examples.translation: chūn tiān yǔ hěn shǎo yǒu shí hòu yǒu fēng — In spring there is little rain and sometimes wind.

examples.text: 旧金山的夏天不热，很凉快，有时候很冷，还常常下雾。
examples.translation: jiù jīn shān de xià tiān bú rè hěn liáng kuài yǒu shí hòu hěn lěng hái cháng cháng xià wù — Summer in San Francisco is not hot but cool, sometimes very cold, and often foggy.

examples.text: 因为旧金山的夏天很冷，冬天不下雪，珍妮在旧金山不可以游泳也不可以滑雪。

explanations.body: Activity 1. You are at the Chinese New Year party of the Chinese Association in Monterey and a guest greets you in Chinese. Take notes in a table, then report. Activity 2. You and your classmates plan to travel to China over a ten-day Christmas break. You can choose only three of five cities: Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Xi’an and Chengdu. explanations.title: Before you read (Getting Started)
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss: A. How is the weather in Monterey? Do you like it and why? B. What do you know about Chongqing? Where is it located? C. Is the weather in Chongqing the same as it is in Monterey?

explanations.title: Presentation 3: 重庆 (Chongqing)
explanations.body: The book prints a number in digits (43, 7); they are written out here so that every word has its pinyin. 山城 is a mountain city; 平均 is “on average”; 左右 is “about”.

examples.text: 重庆在中国西南部，是一个山城。
examples.translation: chóng qìng zài zhōng guó xī nán bù shì yí gè shān chéng — Chongqing is in the southwest of China and is a mountain city.

examples.text: 重庆一年四季大部分是阴天，很少有晴天。
examples.translation: chóng qìng yì nián sì jì dà bù fèn shì yīn tiān hěn shǎo yǒu qíng tiān — Chongqing is mostly cloudy all year round, and rarely has sunny days.

examples.translation: chóng qìng de chūn tiān jīng cháng xià wù — In spring it often fogs in Chongqing.

examples.translation: xià tiān hěn rè zuì gāo qì wēn sì shí sān shè shì dù — Summer is very hot, with a highest temperature of 43 degrees Celsius.

examples.text: 秋天经常下雨，有时候刮风。
examples.translation: qiū tiān jīng cháng xià yǔ yǒu shí hòu guā fēng — In autumn it often rains and sometimes the wind blows.

examples.text: 冬天跟春天一样，也常常下雾，可是很少下雪。
examples.translation: dōng tiān gēn chūn tiān yí yàng yě cháng cháng xià wù kě shì hěn shǎo xià xuě — Winter is the same as spring: it is often foggy too, but it rarely snows.

examples.text: 重庆的气候没有蒙特雷这么好，夏天没有蒙特雷凉快，冬天比蒙特雷冷，平均最低气温七摄氏度左右。
examples.translation: chóng qìng de qì hòu méi yǒu méng tè léi zhè me hǎo xià tiān méi yǒu méng tè léi liáng kuài dōng tiān bǐ méng tè léi lěng píng jūn zuì dī qì wēn qī shè shì dù zuǒ yòu — Chongqing’s climate is not as good as Monterey’s: summer is not as cool as Monterey’s, winter is colder than Monterey’s, with an average lowest temperature of about 7 degrees Celsius.

examples.text: 重庆有很多好玩的地方、好吃的东西，是一个很有意思的城市。
examples.translation: chóng qìng yǒu hěn duō hǎo wán de dì fāng hǎo chī de dōng xī shì yí gè hěn yǒu yì si de chéng shì — Chongqing has many fun places and delicious things, and is a very interesting city.

explanations.title: Reading (Activity 2): 上海 (Shanghai)
explanations.body: Read the passage and answer the questions: What is the passage about? What is the weather like in spring and summer in Shanghai? What is said about autumn and winter? What is said about the uniqueness of Shanghai?

examples.text: 上海在中国的东南部，一年有四个季节，春天很暖和，夏天很闷热，平均最高气温三十二摄氏度。
examples.translation: shàng hǎi zài zhōng guó de dōng nán bù yì nián yǒu sì gè jì jié chūn tiān hěn nuǎn huo xià tiān hěn mēn rè píng jūn zuì gāo qì wēn sān shí èr shè shì dù — Shanghai is in the southeast of China and has four seasons. Spring is very warm and summer is hot and stuffy, with an average highest temperature of 32 degrees Celsius.

examples.translation: shàng hǎi de qiū tiān hěn liáng kuài yǒu shí hòu xià yǔ kě shì hěn shǎo xià wù — Autumn in Shanghai is cool; sometimes it rains, but it is rarely foggy.

examples.text: 冬天天气阴冷，很少有晴天，常常下雨，刮风，可是很少下雪。
examples.translation: dōng tiān tiān qì yīn lěng hěn shǎo yǒu qíng tiān cháng cháng xià yǔ guā fēng kě shì hěn shǎo xià xuě — In winter the weather is cloudy and cold, there are few sunny days, it often rains and the wind blows, but it rarely snows.

lessons.title: 136. The book’s patterns: 跟…一样, and the Zhao Ming dialog
lessons.subtitle: NP1 跟 NP2 一样 + adjective · 不一样 · 一样吗？ · 一样不一样？

explanations.title: 跟 … 一样: patterns
explanations.body: 跟…一样 shows that two things or persons are identical when compared. Patterns: NP1 跟 NP2 一样 + adjective; NP1 跟 NP2 一样 + VP (verbs of emotion, like 喜欢, 想). Negative: NP1 跟 NP2 不一样 + adjective. Questions: NP1 跟 NP2 一样 + adjective 吗？ and NP1 跟 NP2 一样不一样 + adjective？

examples.text: 我弟弟跟我一样高。
examples.translation: wǒ dì di gēn wǒ yí yàng gāo — My younger brother is as tall as I am.

examples.text: 李先生跟王先生一样喜欢学生。
examples.translation: lǐ xiān shēng gēn wáng xiān shēng yí yàng xǐ huān xué shēng — Mr. Li loves his students just the same as Mr. Wang does.

examples.text: 这个教室跟那个教室不一样大。
examples.translation: zhè ge jiào shì gēn nà ge jiào shì bù yí yàng dà — This classroom and that classroom are not the same in size.

examples.text: 今年夏天跟去年夏天一样热吗？
examples.translation: jīn nián xià tiān gēn qù nián xià tiān yí yàng rè ma — Is this summer as hot as last summer?

examples.text: 今年夏天跟去年夏天一样不一样热？
examples.translation: jīn nián xià tiān gēn qù nián xià tiān yí yàng bù yí yàng rè — Is this summer as hot as last summer? (verb-not-verb form)

explanations.title: Activity 1: a conversation between two Chinese students
explanations.body: In the book you highlight the 跟…一样 patterns, write translations and role-play. 习惯 (xíguàn) means “to be used to”.

examples.text: 甲：赵明，你习惯这儿的天气吗？
examples.translation: jiǎ zhào míng nǐ xí guàn zhèr de tiān qì ma — Zhao Ming, are you used to the weather here?

examples.text: 乙：习惯。我们老家的天气跟这儿的一样，冬天不冷，夏天不热。
examples.translation: yǐ xí guàn wǒ men lǎo jiā de tiān qì gēn zhèr de yí yàng dōng tiān bù lěng xià tiān bú rè — Yes. The weather in our hometown is the same as here: winter is not cold and summer is not hot.

examples.text: 甲：我们老家的天气跟这儿的不一样，所以我不太习惯。
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ men lǎo jiā de tiān qì gēn zhèr de bù yí yàng suǒ yǐ wǒ bú tài xí guàn — The weather in our hometown is different from here, so I am not quite used to it.

examples.text: 乙：你们老家是不是冬天很冷，夏天很热？
examples.translation: yǐ nǐ men lǎo jiā shì bú shì dōng tiān hěn lěng xià tiān hěn rè — Is it that winter is very cold and summer is very hot in your hometown?

examples.text: 甲：对。
examples.translation: jiǎ duì — Yes.

explanations.title: Activity 2: short dialogs (from pictures)
explanations.body: The book shows pictures and asks you to complete the answers in pinyin. Dialog 1: a gym compared with your school’s gym. Dialog 2: winter in your hometown compared with New York. Dialog 3: two aircraft, 强击机 (qiángjījī, attack aircraft) and 轰炸机 (hōngzhàjī, bomber).

examples.text: 这个体育馆跟你们学校的体育馆一样吗？
examples.translation: zhè ge tǐ yù guǎn gēn nǐ men xué xiào de tǐ yù guǎn yí yàng ma — Is this gym the same as your school’s gym?

examples.text: 你们老家的冬天跟纽约的冬天一样冷吗？
examples.translation: nǐ men lǎo jiā de dōng tiān gēn niǔ yuē de dōng tiān yí yàng lěng ma — Is the winter in your hometown as cold as the winter in New York?

examples.text: 强击机跟轰炸机不一样。
examples.translation: qiáng jī jī gēn hōng zhà jī bù yí yàng — An attack aircraft is not the same as a bomber.

explanations.title: Activity 3: same and different
explanations.body: Write three weather phenomena of your hometown and of Monterey that are the same and different, for each season, and exchange the information with a classmate.

lessons.title: 137. The book’s patterns: 比, 没有 and 有 … 这么/那么
lessons.subtitle: NP1 比 NP2 + adjective · NP1 没有 NP2 · NP1 有 NP2 那么 + adjective

explanations.title: 比: patterns
explanations.body: 比 indicates different degrees of comparison between two things or persons. Basic: NP1 比 NP2 + adjective; NP1 比 NP2 + VP (of mental verbs). Negative: NP1 没有 NP2 + VP; NP1 不比 NP2 + VP. Interrogative: NP1 有没有 NP2 + VP？ NP1 比 NP2 + VP？ NP1 有 NP2 + VP 吗？ In the book some words are in brackets because they may be left out, such as the repeated noun after 比.

examples.text: 重庆的雾天比蒙特雷多。
examples.translation: chóng qìng de wù tiān bǐ méng tè léi duō — Chongqing has more foggy days than Monterey.

examples.text: 我老家的冬天比北京暖和。
examples.translation: wǒ lǎo jiā de dōng tiān bǐ běi jīng nuǎn huo — Winters in my hometown are warmer than in Beijing.

examples.text: 我比大卫喜欢夏天。
examples.translation: wǒ bǐ dà wèi xǐ huān xià tiān — I like summer more than David does.

examples.text: 他比我们想家。
examples.translation: tā bǐ wǒ men xiǎng jiā — He misses home more than we do.

examples.text: 蒙特雷的风没有纽约大。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de fēng méi yǒu niǔ yuē dà — The wind in Monterey is not as strong as in New York.

examples.text: 他不比小王高。
examples.translation: tā bù bǐ xiǎo wáng gāo — He is not taller than Xiao Wang.

examples.text: 今年的春天风有没有去年的大？
examples.translation: jīn nián de chūn tiān fēng yǒu méi yǒu qù nián de dà — Is the wind this spring as strong as last year’s?

examples.text: 今天的气温比昨天的高吗？
examples.translation: jīn tiān de qì wēn bǐ zuó tiān de gāo ma — Is today’s temperature higher than yesterday’s?

examples.text: 你老家的夏天有上海热吗？
examples.translation: nǐ lǎo jiā de xià tiān yǒu shàng hǎi rè ma — Is summer in your hometown as hot as in Shanghai?

explanations.title: 有: the same degree, with a high standard
explanations.body: Unlike 跟 … 一样, which also shows identical comparison, NP1 有 NP2 (这/那么) + adjective suggests the speaker regards the degree of NP2 as high. Basic: NP1 有 NP2 (这/那么) + adjective. Negative: NP1 没有 NP2 (这/那么) + adjective. Questions: … 吗？ and … 有没有 …？

examples.text: 纽约的夏天有华盛顿的夏天那么热。
examples.translation: niǔ yuē de xià tiān yǒu huá shèng dùn de xià tiān nà me rè — Summer in New York is as hot as summer in Washington.

examples.text: 我有我妹妹那么爱看书。
examples.translation: wǒ yǒu wǒ mèi mèi nà me ài kàn shū — I like reading as much as my younger sister does.

examples.text: 上海的冬天没有北京的冬天那么冷。
examples.translation: shàng hǎi de dōng tiān méi yǒu běi jīng de dōng tiān nà me lěng — Winter in Shanghai is not as cold as winter in Beijing.

examples.text: 上海的冬天有北京的冬天那么冷吗？
examples.translation: shàng hǎi de dōng tiān yǒu běi jīng de dōng tiān nà me lěng ma — Is winter in Shanghai as cold as winter in Beijing?

examples.text: 上海的冬天有没有北京的冬天那么冷？
examples.translation: shàng hǎi de dōng tiān yǒu méi yǒu běi jīng de dōng tiān nà me lěng — Is winter in Shanghai as cold as winter in Beijing? (verb-not-verb form)

explanations.title: Activities 4 to 8 in the book
explanations.body: Activity 4: listen to two brothers talk about the weather and fill in their opinions and reasons; the new word is 锻炼 (duànliàn, exercise). Activity 5: interview a classmate with at least five questions about how their hometown differs from Monterey in size, population and weather, e.g. 你的老家人口比蒙特雷多吗？, then write a short paragraph beginning …在美国的…部/…州。…有…人口，比蒙特雷…。 Activity 7: complete five sentences with comparison constructions: 今天的气温…昨天的气温差不多。 今天早上的风…昨天早上的风…。 今天晚上的天气…今天早上的天气…。 今天早上的风…今天晚上的风…。 晚上的气温…早上的气温…。 Activity 8: use a weather report to finish eight sentences beginning 上海的气温比…, 西安的气温没有…, 北京的气温跟…, 台北的气温比…, 香港跟北京一样…, 南京的天气一样都有小雨, 香港的气温不一样, 西安的气温…高。

lessons.title: 138. The book’s notes: 可是, 好 + verb and temperature conversion
lessons.subtitle: 蒙特雷不太大，可是很美 · 好说 好学 好听 · 摄氏度 华氏度

explanations.title: The conjunction 可是
explanations.body: 可是 is like “but” and connects two clauses: Clause 1 + 可是 + Clause 2.

examples.text: 我老家的冬天很冷，可是可以滑雪。
examples.translation: wǒ lǎo jiā de dōng tiān hěn lěng kě shì kě yǐ huá xuě — Winter in my hometown is very cold, but you can ski.

examples.text: 蒙特雷不太大，可是很美。
examples.translation: méng tè léi bú tài dà kě shì hěn měi — Monterey is not very big, but it is very beautiful.

explanations.title: Activities 9 and 10: 可是 practice
explanations.body: Activity 9: write the opposite idea after 可是: 蒙特雷的风景很美，可是…… 我很喜欢中文，可是…… 纽约是美国最有名的城市，可是…… 加州的天气很好，可是…… Activity 10: one partner says five negative things about Monterey and life here, for example 中文很难。 The other answers with the positive side after 可是, for example 可是，中文很有用。

examples.text: 蒙特雷的风景很美。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de fēng jǐng hěn měi — The scenery in Monterey is very beautiful.

examples.text: 纽约是美国最有名的城市。
examples.translation: niǔ yuē shì měi guó zuì yǒu míng de chéng shì — New York is the most famous city in the U.S.

examples.text: 中文很难。
examples.translation: zhōng wén hěn nán — Chinese is hard.

examples.text: 可是，中文很有用。
examples.translation: kě shì zhōng wén hěn yǒu yòng — But Chinese is very useful.

explanations.title: “好 + verb” as an adjective
explanations.body: 好 and a verb can form an adjective meaning “pleasant to …” or “easy to …”. 好看 means pleasant to look at, good-looking; 好说 means easy to say. Activity 11 asks for the meanings of 好说, 好学, 好听, 好玩, 好吃.

explanations.title: Skill Integration: temperatures in two scales
explanations.body: In the book you listen to a dialog about today’s temperature in Monterey and Xi’an in Fahrenheit and Celsius. Here is the conversion from Activity 2. °F = °C × 1.8 + 32 and °C = (°F − 32) ÷ 1.8. Read 1.8 as 一点八 (yī diǎn bā). For example, 30 °C: 30 × 1.8 = 54, 54 + 32 = 86, so 30 °C is 86 °F. Practice: 海南省夏天最高气温有三十五点九摄氏度。三十五点九摄氏度是多少华氏度？ 35.9 × 1.8 = 64.62, 64.62 + 32 = 96.62, so it is 96.62 °F. Common conversions: 0 °C = 32 °F; 37 °C = 98.6 °F; 38 °C = 100.4 °F; 39 °C = 102.2 °F; 40 °C = 104 °F; 100 °C = 212 °F.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Using Chinese in Context): the coffee shop
explanations.body: You are studying at a coffee shop in downtown Monterey and a Chinese tourist is drinking coffee next to you. Greet the person and ask how they like the weather in Monterey compared with the weather in their hometown. Share your impression too. Pair up and exchange: your hometown; the weather in your hometown; the highest temperature in summer; the lowest temperature in winter; a comparison with the weather in Monterey. Use the table in the book to note your partner’s information (你老家的天气和气温与蒙特雷的比较 and 中国游客老家的天气和气温与蒙特雷的比较), then summarize and report it to the class.

explanations.title: Activity 2: a field trip
explanations.body: Your class plans a field trip to a Chinese community in the Bay Area. Your teacher asks you to find the temperature and weather in San Francisco and San Jose and to recommend a destination. Group A prepares a weather report on San Francisco and Group B one on San Jose. Discuss: how many seasons; the weather in different seasons; which season is best and which is not good; the high temperature in the day and the low temperature at night; a comparison with the other city; and good places to eat and have fun. Write a group report, present it, and let the class and the teacher vote for the best place.

lessons.title: 145. Area studies: China’s territorial and administrative divisions
lessons.subtitle: 中华人民共和国 · 23 provinces, 5 autonomous regions, 4 municipalities, 2 special administrative regions

explanations.title: The People’s Republic of China (中华人民共和国)
explanations.body: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is situated in East Asia on the western rim of the Pacific Ocean. It has a total area of 9.6 million square kilometers. Its north-to-south length is 5,500 kilometers and it stretches 5,200 kilometers from east to west. Its entire national border is 22,800 kilometers long. China is bordered by North Korea to the east; Mongolia to the north; Russia to the northeast; and Kazakhstan to the northwest. It is bordered by Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, and Pakistan to the west; India, Nepal, and Bhutan to the southwest; and Burma (Myanmar), Laos, and Vietnam to the south. Across the seas to the east and southeast are South Korea, Japan, the Philippines, Brunei, Malaysia, and Indonesia. The Chinese mainland is flanked by the Bohai Sea (渤海), the Yellow Sea (黄海), the East China Sea (东海) and the South China Sea (南海). China’s coastline is 32,000 kilometers long, with 18,000 kilometers of mainland and 14,000 kilometers of island coastline.

explanations.title: The South China Sea
explanations.body: China claims sovereignty over the South China Sea (南海) and its numerous islands, atolls, and reefs. However, Southeast Asian nations like Vietnam and the Philippines also have territorial claims in this resource-rich region with strategic sea lanes. Because it is one of the world’s busiest shipping routes, the U.S. and other Pacific nations insist the South China Sea remains open international waters.

explanations.title: Administrative divisions
explanations.body: Due to China’s sizeable population and territory, it has governed the nation with tightly organized and integrated administrative divisions since ancient times. China’s administration is currently based on a three-level system dividing the nation into administrative units of three different sizes: provinces, counties and townships. The entire nation is divided into: 23 provinces (the PRC also considers Taiwan 台湾 a province, as it does not recognize the island as a sovereign nation); 5 autonomous regions: Tibet 西藏, Xinjiang 新疆, Inner Mongolia 内蒙古, Ningxia 宁夏 and Guangxi 广西, where the predominant ethnic minority has a degree of legislative power; 4 municipalities: Beijing 北京, Tianjin 天津, Shanghai 上海 and Chongqing 重庆; and 2 special administrative regions: Hong Kong 香港 and Macao 澳门.

explanations.title: Prefectures, counties and townships
explanations.body: Currently there are approximately 335 prefectures in China, although the number changes frequently. Of the nation’s almost 3,000 county-level administrative units, about half are counties, while the rest are mostly municipal districts (市辖区). In rural areas, townships are called villages (乡), while in urban areas they are referred to as towns (镇). The book ends with a chart of the structural hierarchy of the administrative divisions and the basic-level autonomies of the People’s Republic of China: provincial level (1st), prefectural level (2nd), county level (3rd), township level (4th) and basic-level autonomy (5th). The chart itself is a large diagram and is not reproduced here.

explanations.title: Review: Meeting People (第六课 单元复习)
explanations.body:
The review lesson is designed to help you review and consolidate what you learned in Lessons 1 to 5. When you have completed it, you will be able to:
1. Better understand conversations between Chinese speakers, and short written passages with basic information on: greetings and introductions; personal identification; birthdate and birthplace; family; hometown.
2. Become familiar with the language and non-language features tied to those topics: core vocabulary and patterns; grammar; socially appropriate terms; embedded cultural knowledge.
3. Use these language features to complete a variety of language exercises and conduct a variety of communicative activities.

explanations.title: Topics and core patterns, Activity 1 (Writing)
explanations.body:
The book asks you to recall the topics and sub-topics of the unit and fill in a table with four sub-topics for each of Self, Family, Hometown and City. The book leaves the table empty, so here is one way to fill it from Lessons 1 to 5:
Self: name, age, birthdate, phone number.
Family: parents, siblings, jobs, how many people.
Hometown: where it is, the population, the weather, the people.
City: location, size, the four seasons, the climate.
Try to say a sentence about each one aloud.

lessons.title: 149. Unit 1 review: key grammar points in a dialog
lessons.subtitle: 贵姓 · 呢 · 叫 · 也 · 日文系 · 都 · 不 · 多少 · 多 · 几 · 位

explanations.title: Vocabulary and Grammar, Activity 4 (Reading and Writing)
explanations.body: The book gives you eleven words (numbered 1 to 11) and an eleven-blank dialog between two students, and you write the number of the word in the blank where it belongs. The word list and the finished dialog are here. (The book’s speakers A and B are written 甲 and 乙.)

examples.text: 甲：请问，您贵姓？
examples.translation: jiǎ qǐng wèn nín guì xìng — Excuse me, what is your surname?

examples.text: 乙：我姓王，叫大力。你呢？
examples.translation: yǐ wǒ xìng wáng jiào dà lì nǐ ne — My surname is Wang, and I’m called Dali. And you?

examples.text: 甲：我叫张英。您是中文系的学生吗？
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ jiào zhāng yīng nín shì zhōng wén xì de xué shēng ma — I’m called Zhang Ying. Are you a student in the Chinese Department?

examples.text: 乙：对。你也是中文系的学生吗？
examples.translation: yǐ duì nǐ yě shì zhōng wén xì de xué shēng ma — Yes. Are you also a student in the Chinese Department?

examples.text: 甲：不，我是日文系的学生。
examples.translation: jiǎ bù wǒ shì rì wén xì de xué shēng — No, I’m a student in the Japanese Department.

examples.text: 乙：你们日文系的学生都是军人吗？
examples.translation: yǐ nǐ men rì wén xì de xué shēng dōu shì jūn rén ma — Are all the students in your Japanese Department military?

examples.text: 甲：不，我们日文系有一个学生不是军人。
examples.translation: jiǎ bù wǒ men rì wén xì yǒu yí gè xué shēng bú shì jūn rén — No, one student in our Japanese Department is not military.

examples.text: 乙：你们日文系有多少学生？
examples.translation: yǐ nǐ men rì wén xì yǒu duō shǎo xué shēng — How many students are there in your Japanese Department?

examples.text: 甲：二十多个。
examples.translation: jiǎ èr shí duō gè — Twenty-some.

examples.text: 乙：你们有几位老师？
examples.translation: yǐ nǐ men yǒu jǐ wèi lǎo shī — How many teachers do you have?

examples.text: 甲：四位。
examples.translation: jiǎ sì wèi — Four.

exercises.explanation: 请问，您贵姓？ asks someone’s surname politely.

exercises.prompt: 甲：我___张英。您是中文系的学生吗？
exercises.explanation: 我叫张英 means “I’m called Zhang Ying”.

exercises.prompt: 乙：对。你___是中文系的学生吗？

exercises.explanation: 日文系的学生 is “a student of the Japanese Department”.

exercises.prompt: 乙：你们日文系的学生___是军人吗？
甲：___，我们日文系有一个学生不是军人。

exercises.explanation: 几位 asks “how many” of people.
日文系 (rì wén xì) means “Japanese Department”.

lessons.title: 150. Unit 1 review: comparing seasons and talking about your family
lessons.subtitle: 跟……一样 · 没有……那么 · 比 · 因为 · 不……也不…… · 可以 · 还是

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Writing and Speaking): compare the four seasons of your hometown with Monterey
explanations.body: Pair up and compare the four seasons of your hometown with those of Monterey. Explain your reasoning by using all of these grammar patterns: 跟……（不）一样, 没有……这么（那么）, ……比……, 因为……, 不……也不……, 可以. Your description should start with: 我的老家在…… (“My hometown is in …”). Here is one example sentence for each pattern.

examples.text: 上海的夏天跟重庆的夏天一样热。
examples.translation: shàng hǎi de xià tiān gēn chóng qìng de xià tiān yí yàng rè — Shanghai’s summer is as hot as Chongqing’s.

examples.text: 蒙特雷的夏天没有重庆那么热。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de xià tiān méi yǒu chóng qìng nà me rè — Monterey’s summer is not as hot as Chongqing’s.

examples.text: 重庆的夏天比蒙特雷热。
examples.translation: chóng qìng de xià tiān bǐ méng tè léi rè — Chongqing’s summer is hotter than Monterey’s.

examples.text: 因为我喜欢滑雪，所以我喜欢冬天。
examples.translation: yīn wèi wǒ xǐ huān huá xuě suǒ yǐ wǒ xǐ huān dōng tiān — Because I like to ski, I like winter.

examples.text: 蒙特雷的春天不冷也不热。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de chūn tiān bù lěng yě bú rè — Monterey’s spring is neither cold nor hot.

examples.text: 夏天可以游泳。
examples.translation: xià tiān kě yǐ yóu yǒng — In summer you can swim.

explanations.title: Activity 6 (Listening, Writing and Speaking): your partner’s family
explanations.body:
A. Pair up and ask for your partner’s family information with all of these patterns (you need not follow the order): ……几……, ……谁, ……做什么？ ……多大？ 在哪儿……？ 是……的……, ……还是…… .
B. Take notes while you ask. Then report your classmate’s family information to the class, starting your description with: …是…… . Here are some question and answer sentences built from those patterns.

examples.text: 你家有几口人？
examples.translation: nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén — How many people are in your family?

examples.text: 你姐姐是老师还是医生？
examples.translation: nǐ jiě jiě shì lǎo shī hái shì yī shēng — Is your older sister a teacher or a doctor?

examples.text: 你哥哥多大？
examples.translation: nǐ gē gē duō dà — How old is your older brother?

examples.text: 你妈妈做什么工作？
examples.translation: nǐ mā mā zuò shén me gōng zuò — What does your mother do?

examples.text: 你爸爸是在哪儿出生的？
examples.translation: nǐ bà bà shì zài nǎr chū shēng de — Where was your father born?

examples.text: 他们住在哪儿？
examples.translation: tā men zhù zài nǎr — Where do they live?

examples.text: 我哥哥是陆军上尉，我姐姐是老师。
examples.translation: wǒ gē gē shì lù jūn shàng wèi wǒ jiě jiě shì lǎo shī — My older brother is an Army captain; my older sister is a teacher.

exercises.prompt: 蒙特雷的夏天没有重庆___热。
exercises.explanation: 没有……那么 means “not as … as”.
A 比 B + adjective means “A is more … than B”.
A 还是 B asks “A or B?”.

exercises.prompt: 蒙特雷的春天不冷___不热。

exercises.explanation: 你家有几口人？ asks how many people are in the family.
没有……那么 means “not as … as”.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern means “A or B?” in a question?
exercises.explanation: 还是 offers a choice in a question.

Using the layout of the board, each student moves the number of spaces equal to the number thrown and answers the question in that square. All answers must be in complete sentences. Some boxes may need more than one sentence. If your die falls on a purple box, you can pick any topic for your response. If it falls on an orange square, your partner may choose any topic for your reply. The board itself is a large picture (not included here); its squares are listed below in order. lessons.title: 152. Unit 1 review: reading 马小文’s passage

explanations.title: Skill Integration, Activity 1 (Reading and Writing)
explanations.body:
A. Read the passage and fill in the table in English with the essential elements of information: the author’s name, age and birthplace, his parents’ birthplace, the main features of the parents’ birthplace, and the main topic of discussion between the author and his parents.
B. Summarize the passage orally.
The passage (the book writes the numbers 17 and 25,000 as digits; they are written out here):

examples.text: 我姓马，叫小文，今年十七岁。
examples.translation: wǒ xìng mǎ jiào xiǎo wén jīn nián shí qī suì — My surname is Ma, I’m called Xiaowen, and I am seventeen this year.

examples.text: 我的家乡在中国山东省。
examples.translation: wǒ de jiā xiāng zài zhōng guó shān dōng shěng — My hometown is in Shandong Province, China.

examples.text: 我的父母都是在山东一个小城市出生的。
examples.translation: wǒ de fù mǔ dōu shì zài shān dōng yí gè xiǎo chéng shì chū shēng de — My parents were both born in a small city in Shandong.

examples.text: 那里人口不多，只有两万五千多人。
examples.translation: nà lǐ rén kǒu bù duō zhǐ yǒu liǎng wàn wǔ qiān duō rén — The population there is not large, only more than 25,000 people.

examples.text: 城里没有大学，只有一所中学和一所小学，我是在美国加州出生的。
examples.translation: chéng lǐ méi yǒu dà xué zhǐ yǒu yì suǒ zhōng xué hé yì suǒ xiǎo xué wǒ shì zài měi guó jiā zhōu chū shēng de — There is no college in the city, only one middle school and one elementary school. I was born in California, U.S.A.

examples.text: 我问我父母：“我是中国人还是美国人？”
examples.translation: wǒ wèn wǒ fù mǔ wǒ shì zhōng guó rén hái shì měi guó rén — I asked my parents: “Am I Chinese or American?”

examples.text: 我父母说：“我们的老家在中国，我们都是中国人。”
examples.translation: wǒ fù mǔ shuō wǒ men de lǎo jiā zài zhōng guó wǒ men dōu shì zhōng guó rén — My parents said: “Our hometown is in China; we are all Chinese.”

examples.text: 我想，我是在美国出生的，我是中国人，也是美国人。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎng wǒ shì zài měi guó chū shēng de wǒ shì zhōng guó rén yě shì měi guó rén — I think: I was born in America; I am Chinese, and also American.

explanations.title: Skill Integration, Activity 3 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Work in groups of three. Read the following conversation and answer the six questions aloud, using Chinese expressions from the conversation when needed to give examples. explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context, Activity 6 (Speaking and Writing): the interrogation
explanations.body:
You are assigned to interrogate illegal Chinese-speaking immigrants who came to the United States by boat. Your supervisor needs some information on those you have interrogated.
A. Work in pairs. Your classmate plays the role of an illegal immigrant. While interrogating your partner, take notes in a table, then exchange roles so each partner plays both parts.
B. The instructor plays your supervisor. Report the information you have obtained.
The table has eight items: 1. Name, 2. Nationality, 3. Hometown, 4. Birthplace, 5. Birth year or age, 6. Profession, 7. Military service, if any, 8. Military rank, if any.
Notes: 1. When asking someone’s military service and rank, these sentences are useful: a. 你是哪个军种的？ or 你是什么军种？ b. 你的军衔是什么？ or 你是什么军衔？ 2. In this activity, each immigrant gets a flash card, made by your instructor, with their background information.
The first two questions below are the book’s; the others are built from the patterns of the unit so that you can cover all eight items.

explanations.title: Activity 7: overheard conversations
explanations.body:
The “overheard conversation” aims at developing your ability to gain the gist of a conversation in which you are not a participant. The language you will hear is quite unrestricted. At your present level you will understand only a small portion of what you hear, but you can also glean information from the speakers’ tone of voice, the speed with which they speak, and the functional vocabulary you have already noted and practiced. This is one of your final learning objectives for the Basic Course.
Overhearing conversations can be great fun. The secret is to maintain your level of attention throughout. If things are said that you don’t follow, ignore them and keep listening. If you make a conscious effort to avoid getting stuck trying to figure out one phrase, or “tuning out”, you will pick up much more. This is not a translation exercise, and you will not be asked to reproduce any of this language. You are listening for any information that could be of use to you.
A. Listen and write the male speaker’s name in pinyin with tone marks (segment 1). B. Listen and write the male speaker’s personal information in English (segment 2). C. Listen again and write any additional information you heard (segment 3). D. Present the information you have gathered to the class in Chinese. (Audio, not included.)

explanations.title: Activity 8: a U.S.–China military conference in Beijing
explanations.body:
You work for the Department of Defense and are attending a U.S.–China military conference in Beijing. During a break you overhear three people exchange their personal information (a SCOLA recording, not included). Listen for information about each person and write notes in a table: name, nationality, military service, military rank, phone number. explanations.title: Getting Started

explanations.title: 第七课 校园生活 Lesson 7 Student Life: objectives
explanations.body: When you finish this lesson you will be able to: ask questions about and state the time of day; ask about and describe daily schedules; ask about and describe simple school activities; ask about and describe simple weekend activities. To do that you must master the vocabulary for these functions, telling time, the time word 以后, the modal verbs 要 and 得, the 又…又… construction, word order for “time when” and “time spent”, the question word 怎么样, the 除了… 还… construction, the complement of degree, the 先…然后… construction and the 有时…有时… construction.

lessons.title: 171. Presentation 1 grammar: telling time

explanations.title: Telling time: from the largest unit to the smallest
explanations.body: The sequence for telling the time in Chinese runs from the largest to the smallest unit: year, month, date, AM/PM, specific time. The book’s example is 1998 年 8 月 20 号 上午 9 点零 5 分; here the numbers are written out.

examples.text: 一九九八年八月二十号上午九点零五分
examples.translation: yī jiǔ jiǔ bā nián bā yuè èr shí hào shàng wǔ jiǔ diǎn líng wǔ fēn — 9:05 a.m., August 20, 1998

explanations.title: The hour, the quarter and the minute
explanations.body: 点 or 钟 (o’clock), 刻 (quarter hour) and 分 (minute) are the hourly units. Because they are also measure words, they come immediately after numbers. 两 is used for 2 o’clock (两点), not 二点. From 1 to 9 minutes past, 零 is put in front (六点零五, “6:05”); from 10 to 59 minutes it is not (七点十分). 过 means “past” and 差 means “short of”. A quarter hour is 一刻, three quarters is 三刻, and the half hour is 半.

bā diǎn wǔ shí wǔ fēn

examples.translation: nǐ jǐ diǎn shuì jiào — What time do you go to bed?

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Listening, Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: Listen to a conversation between Wang Ying and Chen Qiang and fill in Chen Qiang’s daily routine in English (when, and what and where), then ask your partner questions about it in Chinese and check against the script (audio, not included).

exercises.prompt: What time is 七点四十五分?
What time is 九点一刻?
What time is 十点三刻?
What time is 十二点半?
What time is 六点过五分?
What time is 九点差五分?
What time is 差一刻十一点?
What time is 早上六点半?
What time is 下午两点五十?
exercises.explanation: 下午两点五十 is 2:50 p.m..

exercises.prompt: What time is 八点二十?

exercises.explanation: 2 o’clock is 两点: 两 is used with measure words like 点.
From 1 to 9 minutes, 零 comes before the number.
From 10 minutes on there is no 零.
一刻 is 15 minutes; 三刻 is 45.

exercises.prompt: What does 半 mean in 十一点半?
What does 差 mean in 九点差五分?
options: short of: five minutes before nine
exercises.explanation: 差五分九点 and 九点差五分 are both 8:55.

exercises.prompt: What does 过 mean in 六点过五分?
Which period of the day is 中午?
Which period of the day is 晚上?
What is the correct order for a full date and time?
exercises.explanation: From the largest unit to the smallest.

lessons.title: 172. Presentation 1 grammar: the time word 以后
lessons.subtitle: 下课以后 · V/VP/N/NP + 以后 · 以后再说

explanations.title: 以后: after
explanations.body: In the presentation the reporter and Sergeant Gao had this exchange: 下课以后，你们做什么？ — 下课以后，我们要去操场锻炼身体。 下课以后 means “after class”. 以后 expresses “after”: it is used to indicate a time frame that is after something happened, or after a certain time or event. In English, “after” comes before the verb or noun; in Chinese the order is just the opposite: V/VP/N/NP + 以后. The book writes 00 后 and 2000 年 and 911 with digits; they are written out here (零零后, 二千年, 九一一).

examples.text: 每天早上集合以后，我去学校上课。
examples.translation: měi tiān zǎo shàng jí hé yǐ hòu wǒ qù xué xiào shàng kè — Mornings I go to school after formation.

examples.text: 下雪以后，天很冷。
examples.translation: xià xuě yǐ hòu tiān hěn lěng — It is cold after it snows.

examples.text: 习惯以后她很喜欢。
examples.translation: xí guàn yǐ hòu tā hěn xǐ huān — She likes it a lot after getting used to it.

examples.text: 五分钟以后在操场集合。
examples.translation: wǔ fēn zhōng yǐ hòu zài cāo chǎng jí hé — Gather in the field in 5 minutes.

examples.text: “零零后”就是二千年以后出生的人。
examples.translation: líng líng hòu jiù shì èr qiān nián yǐ hòu chū shēng de rén — “Post-00s” are those born after 2000.

examples.text: 九一一以后很多人参军。
examples.translation: jiǔ yī yī yǐ hòu hěn duō rén shēn jūn — After 911, many people joined the military.

explanations.title: 以后 as a noun
explanations.body: 以后 can also be a noun by itself, meaning “later”, “in the future” or “from now on”.

examples.text: 以后再说。
examples.translation: yǐ hòu zài shuō — Let’s talk about it later.

examples.text: 你以后做什么工作？
examples.translation: nǐ yǐ hòu zuò shén me gōng zuò — What job will you do in the future?

examples.text: 我以后要习惯说中文。
examples.translation: wǒ yǐ hòu yào xí guàn shuō zhōng wén — I will get used to speaking Chinese from now on.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. Pair up. Analyze one or two example sentences to discover differences between Chinese and English (word order, and so on). Share your findings with the class. B. Take turns covering up the Chinese examples while orally interpreting the English sentences into Chinese; your partner may look and give hints. C. Do a chain story as a class. The main character is 18 岁的空军马龙 (the 18-year-old Air Force airman Ma Long). The first sentence is 今天马龙五点起床。 Take turns continuing the story with 以后 until everybody has had two turns. While the story is told, each student draws simple pictures of what 马龙 has done; afterward pair up and compare your drawings to see if you got the same information.

examples.text: 今天马龙五点起床。
examples.translation: jīn tiān mǎ lóng wǔ diǎn qǐ chuáng — Today Ma Long gets up at five.

exercises.prompt: In 下课以后, where does 以后 go compared with English “after class”?
options: At the end of the sentence only
After the word: 下课 + 以后
Before the word: 以后 + 下课
It cannot be used with verbs
exercises.explanation: English puts “after” first; Chinese puts 以后 last.

exercises.prompt: What does 下雪以后，天很冷 mean?
options: It is cold after it snows
It snows after it is cold
It is not cold when it snows
exercises.explanation: 下雪以后 = after it snows.

exercises.prompt: What does 五分钟以后在操场集合 mean?
options: Gather in the field in 5 minutes
Gather in the field 5 minutes ago
Do not gather in the field
exercises.explanation: A time span + 以后 = “in … time”.

exercises.prompt: What does “后” mean in 零零后?
exercises.explanation: 零零后 are the “post-00s”, born after 2000.

exercises.prompt: What does 以后再说 mean?
What does 你以后做什么工作？ ask?
options: What job will you do in the future?
What job did you do before?
What job do you have now?
exercises.explanation: 以后 as a noun: “in the future”.

exercises.prompt: 下课___，我们要去操场锻炼身体。
每天早上集合___，我去学校上课。
How do you say “after getting up”?

lessons.title: 173. Presentation 1 grammar: the modal verb 要
lessons.subtitle: 我要做作业 · 我要去火星 · 要小心！ · 不用 · 不想 · 不要

explanations.title: 要: must or need, want, and an order
explanations.body: In this lesson 要 is used before a verb to show that an action is a must or a need: 我要做作业 (I need to do my homework), 我还要值班 (I must be on duty as well). 要 is also commonly used to show desire or want: 我要去火星 (I want to go to Mars). A third common use is an order or command: 要小心！ (Be careful!). Each meaning has its own negative and question forms.

rows: Subject + 要 + V + 吗？ / Subject + 要不要 + V？ / Subject + 想 + V + 吗？ / Subject + 想不想 + V？
你要去火星吗？ / 你要不要去火星？ / 你想去火星吗？ / 你想不想去火星？
Subject + 不用 + V / Subject + 不需要 + V
Subject + 不想 + V / Subject + 不 + V
我不用值班。 / 我不需要值班。
我不想去火星。 / 我不去火星。
tables.title: The modal verb 要 in three meanings

examples.text: 我要做作业。
examples.translation: wǒ yào zuò zuò yè — I need to do my homework.

examples.text: 我还要值班。
examples.translation: wǒ hái yào zhí bān — I must be on duty as well.

examples.text: 我要去火星。
examples.translation: wǒ yào qù huǒ xīng — I want to go to Mars.

examples.text: 要小心！
examples.translation: yào xiǎo xīn — Be careful!

explanations.title: Negative forms and the question forms in detail
explanations.body: For “must or need”, the negative is 不用 (búyòng, no need) or 不需要 (bù xūyào, don’t need): 我不用值班。 我不需要值班。 For “want”, it is 不想 or just 不: 我不想去火星。 我不去火星。 For an order, 不要: 你不要大意！ (Don’t be careless!). The questions: 我要值班吗？ for “must”; and for “want”: 你要去火星吗？ 你要不要去火星？ 你想去火星吗？ 你想不想去火星？

examples.text: 我不用值班。
examples.translation: wǒ bú yòng zhí bān — I don’t have to be on duty.

examples.text: 我不需要值班。
examples.translation: wǒ bù xū yào zhí bān — I don’t need to be on duty.

examples.text: 我不想去火星。
examples.translation: wǒ bù xiǎng qù huǒ xīng — I don’t want to go to Mars.

examples.text: 我不去火星。
examples.translation: wǒ bú qù huǒ xīng — I’m not going to Mars.

examples.text: 你不要大意！
examples.translation: nǐ bú yào dà yì — Don’t be careless!

examples.text: 我要值班吗？
examples.translation: wǒ yào zhí bān ma — Do I have to be on duty?

examples.text: 你要不要去火星？
examples.translation: nǐ yào bú yào qù huǒ xīng — Do you want to go to Mars?

examples.text: 你想不想去火星？
examples.translation: nǐ xiǎng bù xiǎng qù huǒ xīng — Do you want to go to Mars?

explanations.title: When 要 could mean either
explanations.body: When indicating must or need, and want, the affirmative forms are the same, so sometimes you do not know which meaning a speaker is expressing. For example 我要锻炼 could mean “I need to exercise” or “I want to exercise”. You can rely on the context to figure it out, or you can ask for clarification: 你是得锻炼呢，还是你想要锻炼？

examples.text: 我要锻炼。
examples.translation: wǒ yào duàn liàn — I need to exercise / I want to exercise.

examples.text: 你是得锻炼呢，还是你想要锻炼？
examples.translation: nǐ shì děi duàn liàn ne hái shì nǐ xiǎng yào duàn liàn — Do you have to exercise, or do you want to exercise?

explanations.title: Activity 5 and Activity 6 (Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: Activity 5: A. Write down three things you must do this week and share them with a partner, then ask whether they must do the same things, and take notes. B. Write down three things you want to do this Saturday, share them and ask the same. The book’s two examples are 这个星期我要看医生。你这个星期要看医生吗？ and 这个星期六我要去旧金山。你这个星期六要不要去旧金山？ Activity 6: tell a partner what you would say in Chinese for five situations. The book gives them in English; one way to say each follows.

examples.text: 大卫，你今天下午想去游泳吗？
examples.translation: dà wèi nǐ jīn tiān xià wǔ xiǎng qù yóu yǒng ma — Ask if David wants to go swimming this afternoon.

examples.text: 我得做作业，今天下午我不去游泳。
examples.translation: wǒ děi zuò zuò yè jīn tiān xià wǔ wǒ bú qù yóu yǒng — State that he needs to do his homework and will not go swimming this afternoon.

examples.text: 小王还想回老家过春节吗？
examples.translation: xiǎo wáng hái xiǎng huí lǎo jiā guò chūn jié ma — Ask if Xiao Wang still wants to go back to his hometown to celebrate the Chinese New Year.

examples.text: 小王要回老家过春节。这个月他不用值班。
examples.translation: xiǎo wáng yào huí lǎo jiā guò chūn jié zhè ge yuè tā bú yòng zhí bān — State that Xiao Wang wants to return to his hometown to celebrate the Chinese New Year and does not need to be on duty this month.

examples.text: 大家都要谢谢自己的父母。
examples.translation: dà jiā dōu yào xiè xiè zì jǐ de fù mǔ — State that everyone must thank his/her parents.

exercises.prompt: What does 我要做作业 mean?
options: I need to do my homework
I don’t want to do homework

exercises.prompt: What does 我要去火星 mean?
options: I have to go to Mars
I want to go to Mars

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I don’t have to be on duty”?
exercises.explanation: The negative of “must” is 不用 or 不需要; 不要 would be “don’t”.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I don’t want to go to Mars”?
exercises.explanation: The negative of “want” is 不想 or 不.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “Don’t be careless!”?
exercises.explanation: The negative of an order is 不要.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks “Do you want to go to Mars?”?
exercises.explanation: 想不想 is the affirmative-negative form.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a correct question for “want”?
Which question clarifies 我要锻炼?
options: 你是得锻炼呢，还是你想要锻炼？

exercises.explanation: 要不要 is the affirmative-negative question.
不要 is “don’t” in an order.

lessons.title: 174. Presentation 1 grammar: the modal verb 得 (děi)
lessons.subtitle: 我得去学校上课 · 你今天晚上得值班吗？ · 不用 / 不需要

explanations.title: 得 (děi): must
explanations.body: When used as a modal verb, 得 (pronounced děi) expresses the obligation or need to carry out an action, similar to the English “must”: 我得去学校上课。 The negative form is 不用 / 不需要 (xūyào: need). The patterns are: Affirmative: Subject + 得 + Verb + Object. Interrogative: Subject + 得 + Verb + Object + 吗？ Negative: Subject + 不用 / 不需要 + Verb + Object. The book gives the examples without English; the translations here are added. (Do not confuse it with the structural particle 得, pronounced de, in 说得好, which comes later in this lesson.)

examples.text: 我得去学校上课。
examples.translation: wǒ děi qù xué xiào shàng kè — I have to go to school for class.

examples.text: 他得去看医生。
examples.translation: tā děi qù kàn yī shēng — He has to go and see the doctor.

examples.text: 今天晚上我得去学校值班。
examples.translation: jīn tiān wǎn shàng wǒ děi qù xué xiào zhí bān — Tonight I have to go to school for duty.

examples.text: 他们也得去操场集合吗？
examples.translation: tā men yě děi qù cāo chǎng jí hé ma — Do they have to go to the drill field for formation too?

examples.text: 你今天晚上得值班吗？
examples.translation: nǐ jīn tiān wǎn shàng děi zhí bān ma — Do you have to be on duty tonight?

examples.text: 海军今天不用去操场集合。
examples.translation: hǎi jūn jīn tiān bú yòng qù cāo chǎng jí hé — The Navy doesn’t have to go to the drill field for formation today.

examples.text: 海军今天不需要去操场集合。
examples.translation: hǎi jūn jīn tiān bù xū yào qù cāo chǎng jí hé — The Navy doesn’t need to go to the drill field for formation today.

explanations.title: Activity 7 and Activity 8
explanations.body: Activity 7: listen to a dialog and take notes on the activities that must be done (who, when, what); then listen again and fill in the blanks of three sentences: 小张想 (wants to) 今天晚上和老李一起去吃日本饭，____。 小张说明天中午可以吗？老李说____。 老李请小张去他家吃晚饭，小张说____。 (audio, not included). Activity 8: write a paragraph in pinyin about what you plan to do after school today, using the modal verb 得 wherever appropriate, and share it with a partner.

exercises.prompt: How is 得 pronounced when it means “must”?
exercises.explanation: The modal verb 得 is děi.

exercises.prompt: What does 他得去看医生 mean?
options: He went to see the doctor
He doesn’t want to see the doctor
He has to go and see the doctor

exercises.prompt: What does 今天晚上我得去学校值班 mean?
options: Tonight I have to go to school for duty
Tonight I want to go to school
exercises.explanation: 得 = have to; 值班 = be on duty.

exercises.prompt: Which is the negative of 得?
exercises.explanation: The negative of 得 is 不用 or 不需要.

exercises.prompt: What does 海军今天不用去操场集合 mean?
options: The Navy doesn’t have to go to the drill field today
The Navy mustn’t go to the field
The Navy went to the field

exercises.prompt: How do you make 你今天晚上得值班 a question?
options: Add 不: 你不今天晚上得值班？
Add 吗: 你今天晚上得值班吗？
Swap the order: 值班得你今天晚上？
Add 得: 你得今天晚上得值班？
exercises.explanation: Subject + 得 + Verb + Object + 吗？
去操场集合: go to the drill field for formation.
Subject + 得 + Verb + Object + 吗？ — 们 and 呢 do not make this a yes/no question.

exercises.prompt: 海军今天不___去操场集合。

lessons.title: 175. Presentation 1 grammar: the 又…又… construction
lessons.subtitle: 他又工作又上大学 · 又大又好 · 又是老师又是军人

explanations.title: 又…又…: both … and …
explanations.body: The 又…又… construction connects two expressions to show a coordinate relationship. It emphasizes that the situations or qualities in the two expressions exist together. The book’s example is 他又喜欢滑雪又喜欢游泳. It is used to connect two verbal expressions (又 + Verbal Expression 1 + 又 + Verbal Expression 2) or two adjectival expressions (又 + Adjectival Expression 1 + 又 + Adjectival Expression 2). Nouns can be joined with 又是…又是….

examples.text: 他又喜欢滑雪又喜欢游泳。
examples.translation: tā yòu xǐ huān huá xuě yòu xǐ huān yóu yǒng — He likes both skiing and swimming.

examples.text: 他又工作又上大学。
examples.translation: tā yòu gōng zuò yòu shàng dà xué — He both works and goes to college.

examples.text: 今天旧金山又刮风又下雨。
examples.translation: jīn tiān jiù jīn shān yòu guā fēng yòu xià yǔ — Today San Francisco is both windy and rainy.

examples.text: 他又是儿子又是爸爸。
examples.translation: tā yòu shì ér zi yòu shì bà bà — He is both a son and a father.

examples.text: 他又是老师又是军人。
examples.translation: tā yòu shì lǎo shī yòu shì jūn rén — He is both a teacher and a soldier.

examples.text: 我们这儿又舒服又好玩儿。
examples.translation: wǒ men zhèr yòu shū fú yòu hǎo wánr — It is both comfortable and fun here.

explanations.title: Activity 9 and Activity 10
explanations.body: Activity 9: listen to six statements and revise them with 又…又…, then ask a partner a question about each (audio, not included). Activity 10: pair up. Take turns picking two appropriate expressions from the lists below and asking your partner to connect them in a sentence with 又…又…. Each person thinks up and says three sentences aloud, then writes them in a table. The book’s example is 儿子，女儿 → 张老师又有儿子又有女儿。 Then read your partner’s sentences and choose one to read to the class.

examples.text: 张老师又有儿子又有女儿。
examples.translation: zhāng lǎo shī yòu yǒu ér zi yòu yǒu nǚ ér — Teacher Zhang has both a son and a daughter.

exercises.explanation: 又…又… joins two things that are both true.

exercises.prompt: What does 他又工作又上大学 mean?
options: He works, then goes to college
He both works and goes to college

exercises.prompt: What does 今天旧金山又刮风又下雨 mean?
options: Today San Francisco is both windy and rainy
San Francisco is a windy city
Today it is windy, then rainy
Today San Francisco is neither windy nor rainy

exercises.prompt: What does 他又是老师又是军人 mean?
options: He is both a teacher and a soldier
He is a teacher, not a soldier
He was a soldier, then a teacher

exercises.prompt: What does 我们这儿又舒服又好玩儿 mean?
options: It is comfortable but not fun
It is both comfortable and fun here
It is neither comfortable nor fun here

exercises.prompt: What does 张老师又有儿子又有女儿 mean?
options: Teacher Zhang has both a son and a daughter
Teacher Zhang has a son or a daughter

exercises.prompt: 他___喜欢滑雪又喜欢游泳。
我们这儿又舒服___好玩儿。

exercises.explanation: 又是老师又是军人: both a teacher and a soldier.
刮风 and 下雨 both describe weather.

lessons.title: 176. Presentation 1 grammar: “time when” and “time spent”
lessons.subtitle: 早上六点半集合 · 做两个小时 · 差不多

explanations.title: Word order: when something happens and how long it lasts
explanations.body: In Chinese, when telling what time an action occurs, the time word must be before the verb or before the subject. When stating how long an action lasts, the duration must come after the verb. The book’s examples for the time when are below; the duration example is from Presentation 2’s dialog (大卫：差不多要做两个小时).

examples.text: 我们早上六点半集合。
examples.translation: wǒ men zǎo shàng liù diǎn bàn jí hé — We have formation at 6:30 in the morning.

examples.text: 早上七点四十五分我们上课。
examples.translation: zǎo shàng qī diǎn sì shí wǔ fēn wǒ men shàng kè — At 7:45 in the morning we have class.

examples.text: 我做作业差不多要做两个小时。
examples.translation: wǒ zuò zuò yè chà bu duō yào zuò liǎng gè xiǎo shí — I do homework for about two hours.

explanations.title: Putting it together
explanations.body: Time when: Subject + time + verb, or time + subject + verb (我们早上六点半集合 / 早上七点四十五分我们上课). Time spent: verb + duration (做两个小时). The two can go in one sentence: 我早上做作业做两个小时 (“In the morning I do homework for two hours”).

examples.text: 我们早上做作业做两个小时。
examples.translation: wǒ men zǎo shàng zuò zuò yè zuò liǎng gè xiǎo shí — In the morning we do homework for two hours.

exercises.prompt: Where does the time word go for “when an action happens”?
options: At the end of the sentence only
Before the verb or before the subject
exercises.explanation: 我们早上六点半集合 / 早上六点半我们集合.

exercises.prompt: Where does the duration go for “how long an action lasts”?
options: At the start of the sentence
exercises.explanation: 做两个小时: the duration follows the verb.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct for “We have formation at 6:30 in the morning”?
Which sentence is correct for “I do homework for two hours”?
exercises.explanation: Verb + duration, after the verb is repeated.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “At 7:45 we have class”?
options: 七点四十五分我们上课。
我们上课七点四十五分。
上课七点四十五分我们。
我们七点上课四十五分。

exercises.explanation: The time word comes before 集合.

exercises.prompt: 我做作业差不多要做两个___。
exercises.explanation: 小时 means “hour”; 两个小时 is two hours.
差不多 (chà bù duō) means “about, almost”.

lessons.title: 177. Presentation 1 skill integration: two emails
lessons.subtitle: 小山 · 琳达 · 每天早上七点三刻开始上课 · 我已经习惯了

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading, Writing and Speaking): Email A and Email B
explanations.body:
Pair up. Read Email A while your partner reads Email B. Then ask your partner for the main idea of the email they read, and the details about who, what, when, where and any other information about each activity; take notes in pinyin or characters. Finally, based on your notes, write an email in pinyin or characters to answer the two questions at the end of the email your partner read.

explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context, Activity 1: an American middle school’s schedule
explanations.body: Your friend Lao Li is sending his son to America for middle school. You found the school’s class schedule on the Internet and want to share it with Lao Li. A partner plays Lao Li and asks five questions about the schedule; answer them from the daily schedule below. The book’s two examples are in Chinese here (the times are written out):

Daily schedule: Wednesday and Friday

explanations.title: Activity 1 B: the email
explanations.body: Write an email to Lao Li telling him the times his son is supposed to arrive at and leave school on the different days, and share it with your partner.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Speaking, Writing and Reading): calligraphy classes
explanations.body: One of your classmates wants to learn Chinese calligraphy. It is winter break and you have just learned that the East-West Center at the University of Hawaii offers online calligraphy classes. Call your classmate (played by your partner). Before you tell them the good news, find out what their daily schedule during winter break is like and fill in a table in Chinese (time and activity). Then tell your classmate what the class schedule is like from the table below, after looking at the new words first, and discuss which class they should attend. Remember that California is three hours ahead of Hawaii (the book’s note).

tables.title: The class schedule

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Listening, Speaking and Writing): a summer camp in China
explanations.body: Your friend’s daughter wants to attend a Chinese summer camp in China, and you offer to look into the camps. A. You call Mr. Sun, who runs a camp in Hangzhou, to find out what a typical day is like there; he returns your call later and leaves a message (audio, not included), and you take notes in English. Then your friend’s daughter calls Mr. Sun to double-check the schedule and asks about the times of a few other things (the table below). Divide into groups of three to play: 1) Mr. Sun (Chinese only), 2) the daughter (English only), and 3) the interpreter; rotate roles until everyone has interpreted. You can also create your own events and times.

lessons.title: 180. Presentation 2: school life in Taiwan (dialog)

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss with your partner: A. How long does it take students to get used to life at DLI? B. What classes do you take every day? How do you say them in Chinese? C. What kind of tests do you have? How do you say those in Chinese?

explanations.title: Presentation 2: 小文 asks 大卫 about his life in Taiwan
explanations.body: The book also prints this dialog in traditional characters (for example 大衛，你在台灣的學習生活怎麼樣？).

examples.text: 小文：大卫，你在台湾的学习生活怎么样？
examples.translation: xiǎo wén dà wèi nǐ zài tái wān de xué xí shēng huó zěn me yàng — David, how is your school life in Taiwan?

examples.text: 大卫：挺好的。开始不太习惯，现在完全适应了。
examples.translation: dà wèi tǐng hǎo de kāi shǐ bú tài xí guàn xiàn zài wán quán shì yìng le — Quite good. At first I wasn’t used to it, but now I have completely adjusted.

examples.text: 小文：你们每天上几节课？
examples.translation: xiǎo wén nǐ men měi tiān shàng jǐ jié kè — How many classes do you have every day?

examples.text: 大卫：五节课。上午三节，下午两节。
examples.translation: dà wèi wǔ jié kè shàng wǔ sān jié xià wǔ liǎng jié — Five classes. Three in the morning and two in the afternoon.

examples.text: 小文：都有什么课？
examples.translation: xiǎo wén dōu yǒu shén me kè — What classes are there?

examples.text: 大卫：有听力课、阅读课、语法课和说话课。
examples.translation: dà wèi yǒu tīng lì kè yuè dú kè yǔ fǎ kè hé shuō huà kè — There are listening, reading, grammar and speaking classes.

examples.text: 小文：你们每天作业多吗？
examples.translation: xiǎo wén nǐ men měi tiān zuò yè duō ma — Do you have a lot of homework every day?

examples.text: 大卫：还可以。差不多要做两个小时。
examples.translation: dà wèi hái kě yǐ chà bu duō yào zuò liǎng gè xiǎo shí — It’s okay. It takes about two hours.

examples.text: 小文：考试多不多？
examples.translation: xiǎo wén kǎo shì duō bù duō — Are there a lot of tests?

examples.text: 大卫：很多，除了每天的生词考试以外，还有单元和期末考试。
examples.translation: dà wèi hěn duō chú le měi tiān de shēng cí kǎo shì yǐ wài hái yǒu dān yuán hé qī mò kǎo shì — A lot. Besides the daily vocabulary tests, there are also unit tests and final exams.

examples.text: 小文：你学习这么努力，一定考得不错吧？
examples.translation: xiǎo wén nǐ xué xí zhè me nǔ lì yí dìng kǎo de bú cuò ba — You study so hard, so you must do well on tests, right?

examples.text: 大卫：因为老师们教得很好，所以，我差不多每次都得优。
examples.translation: dà wèi yīn wèi lǎo shī men jiāo de hěn hǎo suǒ yǐ wǒ chà bu duō měi cì dōu dé yōu — Because the teachers teach very well, I get an A (优, top grade) almost every time.

examples.text: 小文：太好了。祝贺你！
examples.translation: xiǎo wén tài hǎo le zhù hè nǐ — Great. Congratulations!

examples.text: 大卫：谢谢。
examples.translation: dà wèi xiè xiè — Thank you.

explanations.title: Activities 1 to 3
explanations.body: Activity 1 (Listening): A. Global listening: What kind of information does Xiao Wen want to find out from David? What are the main differences between David’s life in Taiwan and yours at DLI? B. Detailed listening: complete a table about David’s life in Taiwan (life in general, classes, tests, homework, grades). Activity 2 (Writing): in pairs, complete a table of expressions: kinds of classes and tests; asking how something or someone is; being completely used to something; attending five class periods every day; “in addition to …”; “about two hours”; someone does something well. Activity 3 (Listening): a dialog about Wang Zhong’s son: what and where he is studying, what classes he takes, how many classes a day, and how he is doing and why (audio, not included). The questions are practiced below from the text.

explanations.title: Activity 4: rearrange the sentences into a coherent paragraph
explanations.body: A. With a partner, rearrange the five sentences (a to e) to make a paragraph: a. 她每天上午上听力课和说话课，下午上阅读课和语法课。 b. 因为她学习很努力，所以每次考试她差不多都得优。 c. 琳达是今年八月开始在天津大学学中文的。 d. 除了上课，她每天还有很多作业。 e. 她的学习生活很忙，不过她已经适应了。 B.
