lessons.title: 206. Presentation 2 activities: answering the phone and spelling out a name
lessons.subtitle: 喂，您好！ · 林姐饭店 · 木子李 · 陆军的陆 · 孔子的孔

explanations.title: Activity 4: answer the phone as the host
explanations.body: In Chinese, your partner reads out a phone number at random from the list below. On hearing the number, answer the phone as though you were the host or hostess at the corresponding restaurant, and take the reservation; take turns until you have taken reservations for all six numbers. For example, you hear 219-3576 (the Qinglong Restaurant), so you answer: 喂，您好！这里是青龙酒楼. Also use 请问, 您贵姓? and 请问, 您需要 (xūyào, need) 什么帮助 (bāngzhù, help)?

tables.title: The six restaurants and their numbers

examples.text: 喂，您好！这里是青龙酒楼。
examples.translation: wèi nín hǎo zhè lǐ shì qīng lóng jiǔ lóu — Hello! This is the Qinglong Restaurant.

examples.text: 请问，您贵姓？
examples.translation: qǐng wèn nín guì xìng — May I ask, what is your surname?

examples.text: 请问，您需要什么帮助？
examples.translation: qǐng wèn nín xū yào shén me bāng zhù — May I ask, what help do you need?

explanations.title: Activity 5: specifying the characters of a name
explanations.body: Because there are so many homophones in Chinese (for example 陆 lù and 卢 lú, 李 lǐ and 黎 lí), people usually specify the characters in their names. There are three main methods, each with its own formulaic expression: 1. break down the character components (mainly for surnames); 2. cite a commonly known word that contains the character; 3. refer to a famous person who shares the same character.

examples.text: 我姓李，木子李。
examples.translation: wǒ xìng lǐ mù zi lǐ — My surname is Li, the Li made of 木 and 子.

examples.text: 我叫陆明，陆军的陆，明天的明。
examples.translation: wǒ jiào lù míng lù jūn de lù míng tiān de míng — My name is Lu Ming: the lu of 陆军 and the ming of 明天.

examples.text: 我姓孔，孔子的孔。
examples.translation: wǒ xìng kǒng kǒng zi de kǒng — My surname is Kong, the kong of Confucius (孔子).

explanations.title: Activity 5A: use the first method for these surnames
explanations.body: Use the first method (我姓李，木子李) to specify the surnames 张 Zhāng, 陈 Chén, 吴 Wú, 林 Lín, 章 Zhāng, 许 Xǔ, 胡 Hú and 吕 Lǚ. The usual formulas (the key is mine):

tables.title: Spelling out the surnames

explanations.title: Activities 5B, 6 and 7
explanations.body: 5B: specify your full Chinese name using any of the three methods. Activity 6: think of a special occasion for which you might need to make a restaurant reservation and complete the table 我想订一张桌子: 几个人？ 最好什么时间？ Then role-play customer and receptionist with the form: customer name, reservation time, number in party; switch roles and perform for the class. Activity 7: A. Listen to a dialog and write the reservation as if you were the receptionist (number in party, preferred time, reserved time; audio, not included). B. Pair up: Student A is the receptionist, and without showing it to Student B first crosses out a few of the table sizes and reservation times in the form for the Great Wall Restaurant: Lunch 11:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. with tables for 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2 and slots 11:00–12:00, 12:00–1:00, 1:00–2:00, 2:00–3:00; Dinner 4:00–10:00 p.m. with the same table sizes and slots 4:00–5:00, 5:00–6:00, 7:00–8:00, 8:00–9:00, 9:00–10:00. Student B makes a reservation while A takes down the customer name, phone, preferred time, reserved time and number in party, and tells B which tables and times are available. Switch roles and repeat.

exercises.prompt: How does the host answer the phone?
options: 喂，您好！这里是青龙酒楼。
exercises.explanation: 喂 is “hello” on the phone; 这里是 + name says who is speaking.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks for a customer’s surname politely?
exercises.explanation: 贵姓 is the polite way to ask a surname.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks what help the customer needs?
exercises.explanation: 需要什么帮助: what help do you need?

exercises.prompt: Why do people spell out their names in Chinese?
options: There are many homophones in Chinese
exercises.explanation: 陆 lù and 卢 lú sound alike.

exercises.prompt: Which method is used in 我姓李，木子李?
options: Cite a known word with the character

exercises.prompt: Which method is used in 陆军的陆?
options: Cite a commonly known word containing the character

exercises.prompt: Which method is used in 孔子的孔?
options: Refer to a famous person with the same character

exercises.prompt: How would you spell the surname 林 by components?
How would you spell the surname 胡 by components?
How would you spell the surname 吴 by components?
How would you spell the surname 吕 by components?

exercises.explanation: 李 is 木 over 子.

exercises.prompt: 我叫陆明，陆军的陆，明天的___。
exercises.explanation: The word for 明 is 明天.

lessons.title: 207. Presentation 2 grammar: Verb + 一下
lessons.subtitle: 我查一下 · 请等一下 · 你过来一下 · 一点儿 against 一下

explanations.title: Verb + 一下
explanations.body: To convey that an action is carried out briefly or casually, 一下 can be added to the verb. Verb + 一下 can also indicate an attempt to do something. Finally, like (一)点儿, 一下 can be added to soften the tone of a statement. Compare 你过来！(Come over here!) and 你过来一下！(Come over here a second!). Pattern: (Subject) + Verb + 一下 (+ Object). The difference between 一点儿 and 一下 is that 一点儿 refers to quantity, while 一下 refers to action.

examples.text: 你过来！
examples.translation: nǐ guò lái — Come over here!

examples.text: 你过来一下！
examples.translation: nǐ guò lái yí xià — Come over here a second!

examples.text: 我查一下。
examples.translation: wǒ chá yí xià — Let me check.

examples.text: 请等一下。
examples.translation: qǐng děng yí xià — Please wait a moment.

examples.text: 你看一下这本书。
examples.translation: nǐ kàn yí xià zhè běn shū — Take a look at this book.

examples.text: 我查一下地图。
examples.translation: wǒ chá yí xià dì tú — Let me check the map.

explanations.title: Activity 1: add (一)点儿 or 一下 to the sentences
explanations.body: Add (一)点儿 or 一下 to the seven sentences and say them out loud. (New words: 休息 xiūxi, to rest; 介绍 jièshào, to introduce.) One way to do it (the key is mine):

examples.text: 少吃点儿糖。
examples.translation: shǎo chī diǎnr táng — Eat less sugar.

examples.text: 喝点儿茶吧！
examples.translation: hē diǎnr chá ba — Have some tea!

examples.text: 最好先查一下地图。
examples.translation: zuì hǎo xiān chá yí xià dì tú — It’s best to check the map first.

examples.text: 下个周末，你去见一下我父母好吗？
examples.translation: xià gè zhōu mò nǐ qù jiàn yí xià wǒ fù mǔ hǎo ma — Next weekend, would you go and meet my parents?

examples.text: 你想再来点儿米饭吗？
examples.translation: nǐ xiǎng zài lái diǎnr mǐ fàn ma — Would you like some more rice?

examples.text: 先休息一下吧。
examples.translation: xiān xiū xī yí xià ba — Take a rest first.

examples.text: 给你们介绍一下，这位是王老师。
examples.translation: gěi nǐ men jiè shào yí xià zhè wèi shì wáng lǎo shī — Let me introduce you: this is Teacher Wang.

exercises.prompt: What does 一下 add to a verb?
options: It makes the action brief or casual, or softens the tone

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is softer: 你过来！ or 你过来一下！?
What does 我查一下 mean?
exercises.explanation: 查一下: check, take a quick look.

exercises.prompt: What does 一点儿 refer to?
exercises.explanation: 一点儿 refers to quantity; 一下 to action.

exercises.prompt: What does 一下 refer to?
exercises.explanation: 一下 refers to the action.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is right for “Let me introduce you”?
exercises.explanation: 介绍 is an action, so 一下 follows the verb.

exercises.prompt: Which is right for “Eat less sugar” (a quantity)?
exercises.explanation: 糖 is a noun, so 点儿 is the right word.

exercises.prompt: Which is right for “Take a rest first”?
exercises.explanation: 休息 is an action, so 一下.

options: At the end of any sentence
a bit (for quick or brief actions)
exercises.explanation: 一下 (yí xià) means “a bit (for quick or brief actions)”.

lessons.title: 208. Presentation 2 grammar: 最好 as “had better”
lessons.subtitle: 最好晚上六点以后 · 最好十点以前睡觉 · 最好不要…

explanations.title: 最好: “it would be best to” or “had better”
explanations.body: As we have learned, 最好 means “the best”, as in 我老家最好的季节是春天. 最好 can also mean “it would be best to” or “had better”. It is often used when giving advice or even politely making demands, as in the line from Presentation 2, “最好晚上六点以后.” Pattern: (Subject) + 最好 + Predicate.

examples.text: （你）最好十点以前睡觉。
examples.translation: nǐ zuì hǎo shí diǎn yǐ qián shuì jiào — You had better go to bed before ten.

examples.text: 你最好今天给他打一个电话。
examples.translation: nǐ zuì hǎo jīn tiān gěi tā dǎ yí gè diàn huà — You had better call him today.

examples.text: 上课以前，最好预习一下课文。
examples.translation: shàng kè yǐ qián zuì hǎo yù xí yí xià kè wén — Before class, it is best to preview the text.

examples.text: 晚上最好不要喝咖啡。
examples.translation: wǎn shàng zuì hǎo bú yào hē kā fēi — In the evening it is best not to drink coffee.

examples.text: 最好不要吃太多糖。
examples.translation: zuì hǎo bú yào chī tài duō táng — It is best not to eat too much sugar.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Speaking): polite suggestions with 最好
explanations.body: Use 最好 to make polite suggestions aloud for five situations: 1. It’s 12 a.m., but your roommate is still playing a video game. 2. Your roommate has been doing homework for a long time and is very tired. 3. Your friend failed their PT test. 4. Your friend puts too much sugar in his coffee. 5. You are driving with your friend to Chinatown in San Francisco, but you get lost. One possible answer each (the key is mine):

examples.text: 现在已经十二点了，你最好不要玩儿电子游戏了。
examples.translation: xiàn zài yǐ jīng shí èr diǎn le nǐ zuì hǎo bú yào wánr diàn zǐ yóu xì le — It’s 12 a.m., but your roommate is still playing a video game: You had better not play video games any more.

examples.text: 你作业做了很长时间了，最好休息一下。
examples.translation: nǐ zuò yè zuò le hěn zhǎng shí jiān le zuì hǎo xiū xī yí xià — Your roommate has been doing homework for a long time: You had better take a rest.

examples.text: 你最好每天早上锻炼身体。
examples.translation: nǐ zuì hǎo měi tiān zǎo shàng duàn liàn shēn tǐ — Your friend failed the PT test: You had better exercise every morning.

examples.text: 你最好少放点儿糖。
examples.translation: nǐ zuì hǎo shǎo fàng diǎnr táng — Your friend puts too much sugar in his coffee: You had better put in less sugar.

examples.text: 我们最好看一下地图。
examples.translation: wǒ men zuì hǎo kàn yí xià dì tú — You are lost on the way to Chinatown: We had better look at the map.

exercises.prompt: What does 最好 mean in 最好晚上六点以后?
options: it would be best to; preferably
exercises.explanation: As advice or preference, 最好 means “had better”.

exercises.prompt: What does 你最好十点以前睡觉 mean?
options: You had better go to bed before ten
You went to bed at ten
You are the best at sleeping

exercises.prompt: What does 晚上最好不要喝咖啡 mean?
options: In the evening it is best not to drink coffee
In the evening the best coffee is cold
exercises.explanation: 最好不要 + verb: best not to.

exercises.prompt: What does 上课以前，最好预习一下课文 mean?
options: Before class, it is best to preview the text

exercises.prompt: What does 最好 mean in 我老家最好的季节是春天?
exercises.explanation: 最好的季节: the best season.

options: After the subject, before the predicate

exercises.prompt: Which is the right way to say “You had better call him today”?
options: 你给他最好打电话今天。
你今天给他最好打一个电话。
你最好今天给他打一个电话。
最好你给他今天打电话一个。
exercises.explanation: The time word goes after 最好.

exercises.prompt: Which is polite advice for a friend who put too much sugar in his coffee?
上课以前，___预习一下课文。
exercises.explanation: 最好 makes the advice polite.
最好不要: best not to.

options: had better; it would be best
exercises.explanation: 最好 (zuì hǎo) means “had better; it would be best”.

lessons.title: 209. Presentation 2 grammar: 不要 for negative commands
lessons.subtitle: 不要太咸 · 不要放味精 · 上课的时候不要玩儿手机

explanations.title: 不要: negative commands
explanations.body: Negative commands like “don’t” are formed with 不要. Patterns: (Subject) + 不要 + Verb [+ Object] and (Subject) + 不要 + Adjective. The subject is usually omitted, as in English.

examples.text: 不要太咸。
examples.translation: bú yào tài xián — Don’t make it too salty.

examples.text: 最好不要放味精。
examples.translation: zuì hǎo bú yào fàng wèi jīng — It’s best not to put in MSG.

examples.text: 不要说英文。
examples.translation: bú yào shuō yīng wén — Don’t speak English.

examples.text: 上课的时候不要玩儿手机。
examples.translation: shàng kè de shí hòu bú yào wánr shǒu jī — Don’t play with your cell phone during class.

examples.text: 不要太晚睡觉。
examples.translation: bú yào tài wǎn shuì jiào — Don’t go to bed too late.

explanations.title: Activity 3: which commands might apply to you?
explanations.body: A. Which of these seven commands might apply to you? B. Write a few negative commands to remind your classmates of things they shouldn’t do.

examples.text: 上课时不要睡觉。
examples.translation: shàng kè shí bú yào shuì jiào — Don’t sleep in class.

examples.text: 周末不要太晚起床。
examples.translation: zhōu mò bú yào tài wǎn qǐ chuáng — Don’t get up too late on weekends.

examples.text: 每天都要吃早饭。
examples.translation: měi tiān dōu yào chī zǎo fàn — Eat breakfast every day.

examples.text: 不要太晚睡觉。
examples.translation: bú yào tài wǎn shuì jiào — Don’t go to bed too late.

examples.text: 要努力学习，不要玩手机。
examples.translation: yào nǔ lì xué xí bú yào wán shǒu jī — Study hard; don’t play with your phone.

examples.text: 每天都要预习和复习。
examples.translation: měi tiān dōu yào yù xí hé fù xí — Preview and review every day.

examples.text: 不要太晚做作业。
examples.translation: bú yào tài wǎn zuò zuò yè — Don’t do homework too late.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Speaking): eight pictures about health
explanations.body: Based on eight pictures (not included), use 不要 and 最好不要 to make suggestions for maintaining good health. Some of mine (the book leaves the answer open):

examples.text: 不要吃太多糖。
examples.translation: bú yào chī tài duō táng — Don’t eat too much sugar.

examples.text: 最好不要喝太多可乐。
examples.translation: zuì hǎo bú yào hē tài duō kě lè — It’s best not to drink too much Coke.

examples.text: 不要太晚睡觉。
examples.translation: bú yào tài wǎn shuì jiào — Don’t go to bed too late.

examples.text: 最好不要整天坐着玩儿手机。
examples.translation: zuì hǎo bú yào zhěng tiān zuò zhe wánr shǒu jī — It’s best not to sit all day playing with your phone.

examples.text: 每天要多喝水。
examples.translation: měi tiān yào duō hē shuǐ — Drink more water every day.

exercises.prompt: What does 不要太咸 mean?
What does 不要说英文 mean?
What does 上课的时候不要玩儿手机 mean?
options: Play with your phone after class
Don’t play with your cell phone during class

exercises.prompt: What does 每天都要吃早饭 mean?
options: You must eat breakfast every day
exercises.explanation: 要 here means must, not 不要.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a polite “best not to”?
exercises.explanation: 最好不要 softens the order.

exercises.prompt: Why is the subject usually omitted in 不要 sentences?
options: It is rude to say it
As in English commands, the listener is understood

exercises.prompt: Which means “Don’t go to bed too late”?

exercises.explanation: 不要 is the negative command.

lessons.title: 210. Presentation 2 grammar: 才 for “later than expected”
lessons.subtitle: 我四点才下课 · 晚饭以后才做作业 · 十点才起床

explanations.title: 才 + verb
explanations.body: The adverb 才 can be used to indicate that something happened later than expected. Its English equivalent is “not until”. Pattern: Subject + Time + 才 + Verb.

examples.text: 我四点才下课。
examples.translation: wǒ sì diǎn cái xià kè — I don’t finish class until four.

examples.text: 我晚饭以后才做作业。
examples.translation: wǒ wǎn fàn yǐ hòu cái zuò zuò yè — I don’t do homework until after dinner.

examples.text: 我考试前才开始努力学习。
examples.translation: wǒ kǎo shì qián cái kāi shǐ nǔ lì xué xí — I don’t start studying hard until just before the test.

examples.text: 周末他九点才起床。
examples.translation: zhōu mò tā jiǔ diǎn cái qǐ chuáng — On weekends he doesn’t get up until nine.

examples.text: 到了台湾几个月以后，我才适应了这里的生活。
examples.translation: dào le tái wān jǐ gè yuè yǐ hòu wǒ cái shì yìng le zhè lǐ de shēng huó — It was not until a few months after arriving in Taiwan that I got used to life here.

explanations.title: Activity 5: which statements apply to you?
explanations.body: A. Which of these five statements might apply to you? B. Based on your own situation, write three more statements using 才 and read them to the class.

examples.text: 我两个月以前才开始学中文。
examples.translation: wǒ liǎng gè yuè yǐ qián cái kāi shǐ xué zhōng wén — I only began studying Chinese two months ago.

examples.text: 作业太多了！我每天晚上十一点以后才睡觉。
examples.translation: zuò yè tài duō le wǒ měi tiān wǎn shàng shí yī diǎn yǐ hòu cái shuì jiào — There’s too much homework! I don’t go to bed until after eleven every night.

examples.text: 我早上六点以后才起床。
examples.translation: wǒ zǎo shàng liù diǎn yǐ hòu cái qǐ chuáng — I don’t get up until after six in the morning.

examples.text: 星期六和星期天，我十点才起床。
examples.translation: xīng qī liù hé xīng qī tiān wǒ shí diǎn cái qǐ chuáng — On Saturdays and Sundays I don’t get up until ten.

examples.text: 我八岁才上学。
examples.translation: wǒ bā suì cái shàng xué — I didn’t start school until I was eight.

explanations.title: Activity 6: a weekday and weekend table
explanations.body: A. Complete a table with the times you do these activities on weekdays (星期一～星期五) and weekends (星期六～星期天): 起床, 锻炼, 早饭, 午饭, 晚饭, 做作业, 睡觉. B. Your partner asks you in Chinese when you do these activities on the weekends; when applicable, answer using 才.

exercises.prompt: What does 才 show in 我四点才下课?
What is the English equivalent of 才?
exercises.explanation: 我四点才下课: I don’t finish until four.

exercises.prompt: What does 周末他九点才起床 mean?
options: On weekends he gets up at nine, early
On weekends he doesn’t get up until nine

exercises.prompt: What does 我八岁才上学 mean?
options: I didn’t start school until I was eight
I went to school eight times
I started school at eight, very early
After the time word, before the verb

exercises.prompt: Which is right for “I don’t do homework until after dinner”?
Which is right for “I don’t get up until ten”?
Which sentence shows the speaker thinks it is late?
options: 我每天晚上九点就睡觉。
我每天晚上十一点以后才睡觉。

exercises.prompt: 到了台湾几个月以后，我___适应了这里的生活。
exercises.explanation: 几个月以后才: not until months later.

lessons.title: 211. Presentation 2 skill integration: the online form and two reservation stories
lessons.subtitle: 预订时间 · 人数 · 特别要求 · 春节 · 订满了 · 分店

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading, Writing and Speaking): an online reservation form
explanations.body: A. Make restaurant reservations online by highlighting your preferences and completing the table with either characters or pinyin (the web page, with the language and service tabs, is not included). B. In pairs, role-play customer and receptionist to make the same reservation by phone; don’t forget the customary courtesy expressions; switch roles and repeat. The fields of the form:

rows: reservation date (closed Sundays and the first Monday of every month)
name: 姓 (surname) and 名 (given name)
title: 先生 (Mr.) or 女士 (Ms.)
tables.title: 餐桌预订 (table reservation)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Listening and Speaking): two phone dialogs
explanations.body: A. Student A listens to Dialog 1 and Student B to Dialog 2 (audio, not included). Dialog 1: When does the customer want to reserve a table? What times are available? What are the details of the confirmed reservation? Dialog 2: Why did the customer call? What was the misunderstanding? What are the details of the final reservation? B. Compare answers in two groups. C. Return to your partner and convey the important information in Chinese.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading and Speaking): two passages
explanations.body: A. Read the passages and complete the forms: Passage 1 (Reservation Event, Reservation Request, Available Times, Final Result, Special Requests) and Passage 2 (Reservation Event, Preferred Times, Available Times, Final Result). B. Pair up and, based on Passage 1, role-play the phone conversation between customer and receptionist; switch roles and repeat for Passage 2.

examples.text: 春节快到了，我和四个朋友想去一家中国饭店吃晚饭。他们都想吃饺子，还想吃辣子鸡、糖醋鱼、麻婆豆腐。小文说他可以吃辣的，不过不要太辣。我给那家饭店打电话，说我们想订一张这个星期六下午六点的桌子。服务员告诉我，他们只有八点的了。因为春节的时候在饭店吃饭的人太多。最后，我只好订了八点的。
examples.translation: chūn jié kuài dào le wǒ hé sì gè péng yǒu xiǎng qù yì jiā zhōng guó fàn diàn chī wǎn fàn tā men dōu xiǎng chī jiǎo zi hái xiǎng chī là zi jī táng cù yú má pó dòu fǔ xiǎo wén shuō tā kě yǐ chī là de bú guò bú yào tài là wǒ gěi nà jiā fàn diàn dǎ diàn huà shuō wǒ men xiǎng dìng yì zhāng zhè ge xīng qī liù xià wǔ liù diǎn de zhuō zi fú wù yuán gào sù wǒ tā men zhǐ yǒu bā diǎn de le yīn wèi chūn jié de shí hòu zài fàn diàn chī fàn de rén tài duō zuì hòu wǒ zhǐ hǎo dìng le bā diǎn de — The Spring Festival is coming and I and four friends want to go to a Chinese restaurant for dinner. They all want dumplings, and also spicy chicken, sweet and sour fish and mapo tofu. Xiaowen says he can eat spicy food, but not too spicy. I called the restaurant and said we wanted a table for six o’clock this Saturday afternoon. The waiter told me they only had eight o’clock left, because too many people eat in restaurants during the Spring Festival. In the end I had no choice but to book eight o’clock.

examples.text: 今天是我先生的生日。我们想和孩子们一起到九龙饭店吃晚饭。那家饭店的饭菜很好吃，每天人都挺多的。不过我今天太忙了，到下午四点才给饭店打电话。我说，我想订一张五个人的桌子，最好是今天下午五点的，不过，七点以前的都行。可是服务员说，今天的桌子都已经订满了。不过他说，他们在东城有一家分店。我可以给那里打电话。
examples.translation: jīn tiān shì wǒ xiān shēng de shēng rì wǒ men xiǎng hé hái zi men yì qǐ dào jiǔ lóng fàn diàn chī wǎn fàn nà jiā fàn diàn de fàn cài hěn hǎo chī měi tiān rén dōu tǐng duō de bú guò wǒ jīn tiān tài máng le dào xià wǔ sì diǎn cái gěi fàn diàn dǎ diàn huà wǒ shuō wǒ xiǎng dìng yì zhāng wǔ gè rén de zhuō zi zuì hǎo shì jīn tiān xià wǔ wǔ diǎn de bú guò qī diǎn yǐ qián de dōu xíng kě shì fú wù yuán shuō jīn tiān de zhuō zi dōu yǐ jīng dìng mǎn le bú guò tā shuō tā men zài dōng chéng yǒu yì jiā fēn diàn wǒ kě yǐ gěi nà lǐ dǎ diàn huà — Today is my husband’s birthday. We want to have dinner with the children at the Jiulong Restaurant. The food there is delicious and it is quite crowded every day. But I was too busy today and did not call the restaurant until four in the afternoon. I said I wanted a table for five, preferably at five this afternoon, but anything before seven would do. But the waiter said that all the tables today are booked. But he said they have a branch in the east of the city. I could call there.

lessons.title: 212. Presentation 2: using Chinese in context (restaurant brochure, reviews, e-mail)
lessons.subtitle: 长城饭店 · 最新评论 · 你给这家饭店几星？ · 你有什么好主意？

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading and Speaking): six questions
explanations.body: In groups of three, take turns asking each other the following six questions to discuss your experiences making restaurant reservations.

examples.text: 你（你的家人，朋友）上一次订饭店是什么时候？是为什么？
examples.translation: nǐ nǐ de jiā rén péng yǒu shàng yí cì dìng fàn diàn shì shén me shí hòu shì wèi shén me — When was the last time you (your family, friends) reserved a restaurant? Why?

examples.text: 是打电话订的吗？
examples.translation: shì dǎ diàn huà dìng de ma — Did you reserve by phone?

examples.text: 为什么订那家饭店？
examples.translation: wèi shén me dìng nà jiā fàn diàn — Why did you reserve that restaurant?

examples.text: 订的是什么时间？有几个人？
examples.translation: dìng de shì shén me shí jiān yǒu jǐ gè rén — What time did you reserve? How many people were there?

examples.text: 有什么特别的要求吗？
examples.translation: yǒu shén me tè bié de yāo qiú ma — Were there any special requests?

examples.text: 你是和谁一起去的？每人点自己的菜还是大家一起吃？
examples.translation: nǐ shì hé shuí yì qǐ qù de měi rén diǎn zì jǐ de cài hái shì dà jiā yì qǐ chī — Whom did you go with? Did each person order their own dish, or did everyone eat together?

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading and Speaking): a brochure of local Chinese restaurants
explanations.body: A. Read the following brochure and decide which restaurant to have dinner at (the book shows four entries; three of them are labeled 中华园). Fill in your choice of restaurant and the reason for your choice. B. Get together with classmates who chose the same restaurant, list the times each of you wants to go and your special requests. C. Discuss which time works best for everyone, then call the restaurant to make a reservation while a student from another group plays the host or hostess (lunch 11:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. and dinner 4:00–10:00 p.m., tables for 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2, with slots 11:00–12:00, 12:00–1:00, 1:00–2:00, 2:00–3:00; 4:00–6:00, 6:00–8:00, 8:00–10:00). The four entries, and the latest review of each:

examples.text: 长城饭店（四颗星，评论二百零七条）
examples.translation: cháng chéng fàn diàn sì kē xīng píng lùn èr bǎi líng qī tiáo — Great Wall Restaurant (four stars, 207 reviews). Introduction: traditional Chinese food, home-style Sichuan dishes. Specialties: pickled-cabbage fish, boiled fish, sweet and sour fish.

examples.text: 中华园（四颗星，评论一百六十七条）
examples.translation: zhōng huá yuán sì kē xīng píng lùn yì bǎi liù shí qī tiáo — Zhonghua Garden (four stars, 167 reviews). Home-style northern dishes. Specialties: egg-flower soup, sweet and sour shrimp, kung pao chicken, stir-fried three delicacies.

examples.text: 中华园（四颗星，评论二百三十五条）
examples.translation: zhōng huá yuán sì kē xīng píng lùn èr bǎi sān shí wǔ tiáo — Zhonghua Garden (four stars, 235 reviews). Sichuan food and Sichuan snacks. Specialties: mapo tofu, hot pot.

examples.text: 中华园（四星半，评论三百四十一条）
examples.translation: zhōng huá yuán sì xīng bàn píng lùn sān bǎi sì shí yī tiáo — Zhonghua Garden (four and a half stars, 341 reviews). Cantonese food and seafood. Specialties: Cantonese soy-sauce chicken, Cantonese shrimp dumplings, Cantonese-style roast duck.

examples.text: 这是我第一次来这家饭店。这里的菜很好吃，服务员也很友好，听我说中文他很高兴。
examples.translation: zhè shì wǒ dì yī cì lái zhè jiā fàn diàn zhè lǐ de cài hěn hǎo chī fú wù yuán yě hěn yǒu hǎo tīng wǒ shuō zhōng wén tā hěn gāo xìng — This is my first time at this restaurant. The food here is delicious and the waiters are friendly; he was very happy to hear me speak Chinese.

examples.text: 我常常和朋友们到这家饭店吃晚饭。这里的服务员都很好，饭菜也很好。每次在这里吃饭我们都很高兴。
examples.translation: wǒ cháng cháng hé péng yǒu men dào zhè jiā fàn diàn chī wǎn fàn zhè lǐ de fú wù yuán dōu hěn hǎo fàn cài yě hěn hǎo měi cì zài zhè lǐ chī fàn wǒ men dōu hěn gāo xìng — I often have dinner with friends at this restaurant. The waiters here are all very good and the food is good too. Every time we eat here we are happy.

examples.text: 我喜欢这家饭店。饭菜很好吃，又不太贵。饭店很干净。这里的火锅很有特色！
examples.translation: wǒ xǐ huān zhè jiā fàn diàn fàn cài hěn hǎo chī yòu bú tài guì fàn diàn hěn gān jìng zhè lǐ de huǒ guō hěn yǒu tè sè — I like this restaurant. The food is delicious and not too expensive. The restaurant is very clean. The hot pot here is very distinctive!

examples.text: 这家饭店很小，只有五六张小桌子，可是每份菜都挺多。老板也很好，每次去吃饭都给我们免费的小吃！
examples.translation: zhè jiā fàn diàn hěn xiǎo zhǐ yǒu wǔ liù zhāng xiǎo zhuō zi kě shì měi fèn cài dōu tǐng duō lǎo bǎn yě hěn hǎo měi cì qù chī fàn dōu gěi wǒ men miǎn fèi de xiǎo chī — This restaurant is very small, with only five or six little tables, but every dish has quite a lot. The owner is also good; every time we eat there he gives us free snacks!

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading, Writing and Speaking): write a review
explanations.body: A. Think of a Chinese restaurant you have been to and write a review in Chinese based on seven questions, then share details of your own experience on the review page (the form, with 取消 cancel and 提交 submit, is not included). B. A partner translates your review into English; discuss the translation to ensure accuracy. C. List your reservation preferences and call the restaurant your partner recommended.

examples.text: 你常去这家饭店吗？
examples.translation: nǐ cháng qù zhè jiā fàn diàn ma — Do you often go to this restaurant?

examples.text: 最近一次是什么时候去的？
examples.translation: zuì jìn yí cì shì shén me shí hòu qù de — When did you go most recently?

examples.text: 你自己去的还是和朋友一起去的？
examples.translation: nǐ zì jǐ qù de hái shì hé péng yǒu yì qǐ qù de — Did you go alone or with friends?

examples.text: 这家饭店的服务怎么样？
examples.translation: zhè jiā fàn diàn de fú wù zěn me yàng — How is the service at this restaurant?

examples.text: 你喜欢这家饭店吗？为什么？
examples.translation: nǐ xǐ huān zhè jiā fàn diàn ma wèi shén me — Do you like this restaurant? Why?

examples.text: 你最喜欢/不喜欢的菜是什么？为什么？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì xǐ huān bù xǐ huān de cài shì shén me wèi shén me — What is your favorite or least favorite dish? Why?

examples.text: 你给这家饭店几星？
examples.translation: nǐ gěi zhè jiā fàn diàn jǐ xīng — How many stars do you give this restaurant?

explanations.title: Activities 4 and 5: plan a dinner outing; reply to a friend’s e-mail
explanations.body: Activity 4: in two groups of three, plan a dinner outing in Chinese: compare the three restaurants you reviewed and agree on one; agree on the best time; list your special requests; call the restaurant; one student from the other group plays the host while two write down the details. Activity 5: read this e-mail from a friend and reply with your advice. The e-mail, and one possible reply (the reply is mine):

examples.text: 我住的地方有一家中国饭店。我常常去那儿吃晚饭，每个星期三四次。不过，那里有的菜很贵，有的菜挺咸，味精也很多，常吃对身体不好。可是，我也不想自己做饭，太麻烦，而且，我每天工作都很忙，没有太多时间做饭。你有什么好主意？
examples.translation: wǒ zhù de dì fāng yǒu yì jiā zhōng guó fàn diàn wǒ cháng cháng qù nàr chī wǎn fàn měi gè xīng qī sān sì cì bú guò nà lǐ yǒu de cài hěn guì yǒu de cài tǐng xián wèi jīng yě hěn duō cháng chī duì shēn tǐ bù hǎo kě shì wǒ yě bù xiǎng zì jǐ zuò fàn tài má fán ér qiě wǒ měi tiān gōng zuò dōu hěn máng méi yǒu tài duō shí jiān zuò fàn nǐ yǒu shén me hǎo zhǔ yì — There is a Chinese restaurant where I live. I often go there for dinner, three or four times a week. But some of the dishes there are expensive, some are quite salty, and there is a lot of MSG, so it is bad for your health to eat it often. But I also don’t want to cook for myself; it is too much trouble, and besides I am very busy at work every day and don’t have much time to cook. Do you have any good ideas?

examples.text: 我觉得你最好不要常去那家饭店吃饭。
examples.translation: wǒ jué de nǐ zuì hǎo bú yào cháng qù nà jiā fàn diàn chī fàn — I think you had better not go to that restaurant often.

examples.text: 你可以先查一下附近别的饭店，找一家菜清淡、不放味精的。
examples.translation: nǐ kě yǐ xiān chá yí xià fù jìn bié de fàn diàn zhǎo yì jiā cài qīng dàn bú fàng wèi jīng de — You can first look up other restaurants nearby and find one with mild dishes and no MSG.

examples.text: 周末你也可以做一点儿简单的菜，一次多做一点儿，下个星期再吃。
examples.translation: zhōu mò nǐ yě kě yǐ zuò yì diǎnr jiǎn dān de cài yí cì duō zuò yì diǎnr xià gè xīng qī zài chī — On weekends you can also cook some simple dishes, make a bit more each time, and eat it next week.

units.title: 第八课 中国食品与餐馆 Presentation 3: Cooking Day, 就 and 才, 了, 一边…一边…, 会, and Food in Chinese Culture

lessons.title: 214. Presentation 3: Cooking Day (passage)
lessons.subtitle: 做饭日 · 又香又辣 · 红烧肉 · 一边做饭，一边说中文

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss. A. Do you know your Chinese teachers’ hometowns? B. Do you know what the regional cuisine is like there?

explanations.title: Presentation 3: 做饭日 (Cooking Day)
explanations.body: The book also prints this passage in traditional characters (for example 今天是我們班的做飯日).

examples.text: 今天是我们班的做饭日。一大早，我们就到了学校的厨房。我们先分成了几个小组，每组有一个老师教我们做中国菜。
examples.translation: jīn tiān shì wǒ men bān de zuò fàn rì yí dà zǎo wǒ men jiù dào le xué xiào de chú fáng wǒ men xiān fēn chéng le jǐ gè xiǎo zǔ měi zǔ yǒu yí gè lǎo shī jiāo wǒ men zuò zhōng guó cài — Today is our class’s Cooking Day. Very early in the morning we already arrived at the school kitchen. We first divided into several groups, and in each group a teacher taught us to cook Chinese dishes.

examples.text: 我们的老师来自中国各地，都很会做菜。陈老师是四川人，她教我们做了一个麻婆豆腐，又香又辣。吴老师在北京长大，最会包饺子，他包的饺子又好看，又好吃。
examples.translation: wǒ men de lǎo shī lái zì zhōng guó gè dì dōu hěn huì zuò cài chén lǎo shī shì sì chuān rén tā jiāo wǒ men zuò le yí gè má pó dòu fǔ yòu xiāng yòu là wú lǎo shī zài běi jīng zhǎng dà zuì huì bāo jiǎo zi tā bāo de jiǎo zi yòu hǎo kàn yòu hǎo chī — Our teachers come from all over China and are all good at cooking. Teacher Chen is from Sichuan; she taught us to make a mapo tofu, both fragrant and spicy. Teacher Wu grew up in Beijing and is best at wrapping dumplings; the dumplings he wraps are both good-looking and delicious.

examples.text: 张老师是上海人，他教我们做了一个红烧肉，颜色好，味道甜。因为我和大卫都吃素，陆老师教我们做了一个素菜，又清淡又可口。
examples.translation: zhāng lǎo shī shì shàng hǎi rén tā jiāo wǒ men zuò le yí gè hóng shāo ròu yán sè hǎo wèi dào tián yīn wèi wǒ hé dà wèi dōu chī sù lù lǎo shī jiāo wǒ men zuò le yí gè sù cài yòu qīng dàn yòu kě kǒu — Teacher Zhang is from Shanghai; he taught us to make a soy-braised pork, with nice color and a sweet taste. Because David and I are both vegetarians, Teacher Lu taught us to make a vegetable dish, both mild and tasty.

explanations.body: For each group of words, select the word that does not belong in the same category as the others, and discuss your choices with a partner in Chinese. The five groups, with my answers:

The other three are verbs; 甜 is an adjective.

The others describe how food tastes; 味道 is the noun “taste”.
麻婆豆腐 · 红烧肉 · 饺子 · 厨房
The others are dishes; 厨房 is the kitchen.

lessons.title: 215. Presentation 3 activities: a birthday, and choosing from the menu
lessons.subtitle: 今天是我的生日 · 先…然后 · 我们一边吃饭一边聊天 · 麻婆豆腐

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading and Speaking): a birthday passage
explanations.body: A. Read the passage, highlight the activities and the time phrases associated with them. B. Think about what you did last Saturday and complete a table with the columns Time and Activity. C. Pair up and, referring to the table, tell your partner what you did using time phrases, past tense particles, 先…然后 and 以后.

examples.text: 今天是我的生日，一大早我就起床了。今天天气很好。早饭以后，我和几个同学先去海边玩儿了两个小时，然后，我们一起到城里的一家中国餐馆吃午饭。我们一边吃饭一边聊天。午饭以后，我们还去看了一个新电影。我过了一个很有意思的生日。
examples.translation: jīn tiān shì wǒ de shēng rì yí dà zǎo wǒ jiù qǐ chuáng le jīn tiān tiān qì hěn hǎo zǎo fàn yǐ hòu wǒ hé jǐ gè tóng xué xiān qù hǎi biān wánr le liǎng gè xiǎo shí rán hòu wǒ men yì qǐ dào chéng lǐ de yì jiā zhōng guó cān guǎn chī wǔ fàn wǒ men yì biān chī fàn yì biān liáo tiān wǔ fàn yǐ hòu wǒ men hái qù kàn le yí gè xīn diàn yǐng wǒ guò le yí gè hěn yǒu yì si de shēng rì — Today is my birthday; very early in the morning I got up. The weather is very good today. After breakfast, a few classmates and I first went to the beach and played for two hours, then we went together to a Chinese restaurant in town for lunch. We chatted while we ate. After lunch we also went to see a new movie. I had a very interesting birthday.

lessons.title: 216. Presentation 3 grammar: 就 for “earlier than expected”
lessons.subtitle: 一大早我们就到了 · 早上四点半就起床 · 就 against 才

explanations.title: Adverb 就 (2)
explanations.body: In previous lessons we learned that the adverb 就 is used before a verb to enhance the tone of emphasis. In this lesson 就 indicates that an action happened early: 一大早，我们就到了学校的厨房 (Very early in the morning, we already arrived at the school kitchen). Pattern: 就 + V/VP.

examples.text: 下个星期就是他的生日了。
examples.translation: xià gè xīng qī jiù shì tā de shēng rì le — His birthday is next week.

examples.text: 他的老家就在这儿。
examples.translation: tā de lǎo jiā jiù zài zhèr — His hometown is right here.

examples.text: 一大早，我们就到了学校的厨房。
examples.translation: yí dà zǎo wǒ men jiù dào le xué xiào de chú fáng — Very early in the morning we already arrived at the school kitchen.

examples.text: 他每天早上四点半就起床。
examples.translation: tā měi tiān zǎo shàng sì diǎn bàn jiù qǐ chuáng — He gets up at half past four every morning already.

examples.text: 他每天晚上九点半就睡觉。
examples.translation: tā měi tiān wǎn shàng jiǔ diǎn bàn jiù shuì jiào — He goes to bed at half past nine every night already.

explanations.title: 就 against 才
explanations.body: While the adverb 才 (see Presentation 2) indicates that something happened later than expected, 就 indicates that something happened earlier than expected. Compare the four pairs:

examples.text: 一大早，我们就到了学校的厨房。
examples.translation: yí dà zǎo wǒ men jiù dào le xué xiào de chú fáng — We were already at the school kitchen very early; they didn’t get there until after ten.

examples.text: 他早上四点半就起床。
examples.translation: tā zǎo shàng sì diǎn bàn jiù qǐ chuáng — He gets up at 4:30 already; he doesn’t get up until eight.

examples.text: 十一点我们就吃午饭。
examples.translation: shí yī diǎn wǒ men jiù chī wǔ fàn — We eat lunch as early as eleven; they don’t eat lunch until two in the afternoon.

examples.text: 我老家四月就很热。
examples.translation: wǒ lǎo jiā sì yuè jiù hěn rè — My hometown is already hot in April; his is not hot until August.

examples.text: 十点多，他们才到了学校的厨房。
examples.translation: shí diǎn duō tā men cái dào le xué xiào de chú fáng — We were already at the school kitchen very early; they didn’t get there until after ten.

examples.text: 他早上八点才起床。
examples.translation: tā zǎo shàng bā diǎn cái qǐ chuáng — He gets up at 4:30 already; he doesn’t get up until eight.

examples.text: 下午两点他们才吃午饭。
examples.translation: xià wǔ liǎng diǎn tā men cái chī wǔ fàn — We eat lunch as early as eleven; they don’t eat lunch until two in the afternoon.

examples.text: 他老家八月才热。
examples.translation: tā lǎo jiā bā yuè cái rè — My hometown is already hot in April; his is not hot until August.

explanations.title: Opinion: the same fact with 才 or 就
explanations.body: The use of 才 or 就 contains the speaker’s opinion. Therefore, for the same situation, speaker A may use 才 and speaker B 就:

examples.text: 甲：我一分钟就吃了五个饺子。
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ yì fēn zhōng jiù chī le wǔ gè jiǎo zi — I ate five dumplings in just one minute.

examples.text: 乙：你一分钟才吃了五个饺子？我一分钟就吃了十个！
examples.translation: yǐ nǐ yì fēn zhōng cái chī le wǔ gè jiǎo zi wǒ yì fēn zhōng jiù chī le shí gè — You only ate five dumplings in a minute? I ate ten in a minute!

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Write three things you consider you do earlier than others in daily life (with 就) and three you do later (with 才). Examples: 我每天早上五点半就锻炼。 / 我每天下午四点才锻炼。 B. Pair up and take turns sharing; your partner responds by comparing his or her situation with yours: 我也每天早上五点半就锻炼。 or 你五点半才锻炼？我四点半就锻炼。 or 你早上五点半就锻炼？我下午四点才锻炼。

exercises.prompt: What does 就 show in 一大早，我们就到了学校的厨房?
options: It happened early, earlier than expected

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says he gets up early?
exercises.explanation: 四点半就: as early as 4:30.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says he gets up late?
Which sentence says it is already hot in April?
In 你一分钟才吃了五个饺子？我一分钟就吃了十个！, who thinks five is a small number?
exercises.explanation: 才 expresses “only”; 就 expresses “as many as”.

exercises.prompt: In the same exchange, who thinks ten is a lot, and the speaker’s own pace fast?

options: Before the verb or verb phrase

exercises.prompt: Which means “We eat lunch as early as eleven”?
他每天晚上九点半___睡觉。
十点多，他们___到了学校的厨房。
下个星期___是他的生日了。
exercises.explanation: 就 enhances emphasis: next week IS his birthday.
一大早 (yī dà zǎo) means “early morning; at dawn”.

lessons.title: 217. Presentation 3 grammar: 了 for reporting a new event
lessons.subtitle: 我们做了一个麻婆豆腐 · 没有… · 看没看 · 去年每个月都看一个

explanations.title: 了 for reporting a new event
explanations.body: 了 can be used to report a new event: 我们做了一个麻婆豆腐 (We made a mapo tofu). When 了 is used to report a new event, it occurs between the verb and the object. The negative and interrogative forms use 没(有) without 了. Positive: Subject + Verb + 了 + (Num. + M) + Object. Negative: Subject + 没(有) + Verb + Object. Interrogative: Subject + Verb + 没(有) + Verb + Object?

examples.text: 我们做了一个麻婆豆腐。
examples.translation: wǒ men zuò le yí gè má pó dòu fǔ — We made a mapo tofu.

examples.text: 昨天，我和朋友们看了一个中国电影。
examples.translation: zuó tiān wǒ hé péng yǒu men kàn le yí gè zhōng guó diàn yǐng — Yesterday I and my friends saw a Chinese movie.

examples.text: 今天早上，北京下了一场大雪。
examples.translation: jīn tiān zǎo shàng běi jīng xià le yì cháng dà xuě — This morning it snowed heavily in Beijing.

examples.text: 周末，我买了两本中文书。
examples.translation: zhōu mò wǒ mǎi le liǎng běn zhōng wén shū — On the weekend I bought two Chinese books.

examples.text: 昨天，我值班，没有去上课。
examples.translation: zuó tiān wǒ zhí bān méi yǒu qù shàng kè — Yesterday I was on duty and did not go to class.

examples.text: 你昨天锻炼没锻炼？
examples.translation: nǐ zuó tiān duàn liàn méi duàn liàn — Did you exercise yesterday?

explanations.title: The negative never takes 了
explanations.body: The book marks 昨天，我值班，没有去上课了 as wrong (with 没有 do not add 了); the correct sentence is 昨天，我值班，没有去上课。

explanations.title: Repeated actions do not take 了
explanations.body: This use of 了 can’t refer to repeated actions, even if the actions happened in the past. In Chinese, a simple verb is used to state repeated actions, whether they are in the past, present or future. So 去年，我每个月都看了一个中国电影 is not the way to say it; use:

examples.text: 去年，我每个月都看一个中国电影。
examples.translation: qù nián wǒ měi gè yuè dōu kàn yí gè zhōng guó diàn yǐng — Last year I saw a Chinese movie every month.

examples.text: 明年，我每个月都要看一个中国电影。
examples.translation: míng nián wǒ měi gè yuè dōu yào kàn yí gè zhōng guó diàn yǐng — Next year I will see a Chinese movie every month.

explanations.title: Activities 2 and 3: narrate it
explanations.body: Activity 2: turn the ordering dialog of Presentation 1 into a monolog using as many 了 as possible to report new events; write an outline first, then narrate it to a partner. One possible monolog (mine):

examples.text: 我们去了一家餐馆。
examples.translation: wǒ men qù le yì jiā cān guǎn — We went to a restaurant.

examples.text: 服务员给了我们菜单，问我们想喝点儿什么。
examples.translation: fú wù yuán gěi le wǒ men cài dān wèn wǒ men xiǎng hē diǎnr shén me — The waiter gave us the menu and asked what we wanted to drink.

examples.text: 我要了一瓶啤酒，小文要了一杯橙汁。
examples.translation: wǒ yào le yì píng pí jiǔ xiǎo wén yào le yì bēi chéng zhī — I ordered a bottle of beer and Xiaowen ordered a glass of orange juice.

examples.text: 服务员说北京烤鸭最有特色，我们就点了半只烤鸭、一个糖醋鱼和一个西红柿炒鸡蛋。
examples.translation: fú wù yuán shuō běi jīng kǎo yā zuì yǒu tè sè wǒ men jiù diǎn le bàn zhǐ kǎo yā yí gè táng cù yú hé yí gè xī hóng shì chǎo jī dàn — The waiter said the Beijing roast duck was the most distinctive, so we ordered half a duck, a sweet and sour fish and a tomato and scrambled eggs.

examples.text: 我们还要了两碗米饭和一盘饺子，还请服务员拿了两双筷子。
examples.translation: wǒ men hái yào le liǎng wǎn mǐ fàn hé yì pán jiǎo zi hái qǐng fú wù yuán ná le liǎng shuāng kuài zi — We also ordered two bowls of rice and a plate of dumplings, and asked the waiter to bring two pairs of chopsticks.

examples.text: 五分钟以后，菜来了，我们谢了服务员。
examples.translation: wǔ fēn zhōng yǐ hòu cài lái le wǒ men xiè le fú wù yuán — Five minutes later the dishes came and we thanked the waiter.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: Narrate your last experience at a restaurant. A. List five actions you did, in order, using 了 as many times as possible. B. Arrange the actions into a monolog with necessary time nouns and cohesive devices such as 去年, 上个月, 先…然后 and 还; write an outline in your notebook. C. Pair up and speak your monolog to your partner.

exercises.prompt: Where does 了 go when reporting a new event?
options: At the end of the sentence only
Between the verb and the object

exercises.prompt: What does 周末，我买了两本中文书 mean?
options: I will buy two Chinese books
I buy Chinese books every weekend
On the weekend I bought two Chinese books
exercises.explanation: 买了: a completed new event.

exercises.prompt: How do you say “I did not go to class yesterday”?
How do you ask “Did you exercise yesterday?” in the verb-not-verb form?
Which form is used for repeated actions in the past?
options: Verb + 了: 去年，我每个月都看了一个中国电影
A simple verb: 去年，我每个月都看一个中国电影
exercises.explanation: 了 can’t refer to repeated actions.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence reports a one-time past event?
options: 明年，我每个月都要看一个中国电影。
去年，我每个月都看一个中国电影。
昨天，我和朋友们看了一个中国电影。

exercises.prompt: What does 今天早上，北京下了一场大雪 mean?
options: It snows in Beijing every morning
This morning it snowed heavily in Beijing
exercises.explanation: 下了一场大雪: it snowed a big snow.

options: 昨天，我值班，没有去上课了。
昨天，我值班，没有去上课。
exercises.explanation: 没有 and 了 do not go together.

exercises.prompt: 昨天，我和朋友们看___一个中国电影。
exercises.explanation: Verb + 了 + number + measure word + object.
A 没-verb question reports a past event.
没有 negates a past event.
了 (le) means “(particle reporting a completed new event)”.

lessons.title: 218. Presentation 3 grammar: 一边…一边… for two simultaneous actions
lessons.subtitle: 一边做饭，一边说中文 · 边走边聊

explanations.title: The 一边…一边… construction
explanations.body: The 一边…一边… construction expresses two actions occurring at the same time. Pattern: Subject + 一边 + Verb + (Object), 一边 + Verb + (Object). 一边 can be shortened to 边 for a more colloquial feeling, especially when the verb is monosyllabic.

examples.text: 大家一边做饭，一边说中文。
examples.translation: dà jiā yì biān zuò fàn yì biān shuō zhōng wén — Everyone spoke Chinese while cooking.

examples.text: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视。
examples.translation: tā yì biān chī fàn yì biān kàn diàn shì — He watches TV while eating.

examples.text: 他们一边散步，一边聊天。
examples.translation: tā men yì biān sàn bù yì biān liáo tiān — They chat while taking a walk.

examples.text: 我们边走边聊吧。
examples.translation: wǒ men biān zǒu biān liáo ba — Let’s chat while we walk.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Speaking and Writing)
explanations.body: A. Pair up. Choose three of nine pictures (not included) and describe them to the class using 一边…一边…. B. Use 一边…一边… to complete: 1. 我喜欢… 2. (a classmate) 常常… 3. 请不要… Some of mine (the key is mine):

examples.text: 他们一边喝茶，一边看书。
examples.translation: tā men yì biān hē chá yì biān kàn shū — They read while drinking tea.

examples.text: 她一边走路，一边打电话。
examples.translation: tā yì biān zǒu lù yì biān dǎ diàn huà — She talks on the phone while walking.

examples.text: 孩子们一边包饺子，一边唱歌。
examples.translation: hái zi men yì biān bāo jiǎo zi yì biān chàng gē — The children sing while wrapping dumplings.

examples.text: 我喜欢一边听音乐，一边做作业。
examples.translation: wǒ xǐ huān yì biān tīng yīn yuè yì biān zuò zuò yè — I like to do homework while listening to music.

examples.text: 请不要一边上课，一边玩儿手机。
examples.translation: qǐng bú yào yì biān shàng kè yì biān wánr shǒu jī — Please don’t play with your phone while in class.

exercises.prompt: What does 一边…一边… express?
options: Two actions at the same time
exercises.explanation: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视.

exercises.prompt: What does 他们一边散步，一边聊天 mean?
options: They take a walk, then chat
They chat while taking a walk
exercises.explanation: 一边 + verb, 一边 + verb.

exercises.prompt: What is the colloquial short form of 一边?
When is the short form 边 most natural?
options: When the verb has three syllables
exercises.explanation: 边走边聊: 走 and 聊 are one syllable each.

exercises.prompt: What does 我们边走边聊吧 mean?
Which sentence is right for “He watches TV while eating”?
options: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视。
他一边吃饭，然后看电视。
他一边一边吃饭看电视。
他吃饭一边看电视一边。

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is right for “Everyone spoke Chinese while cooking”?
options: 大家做饭，一边说中文一边。
大家先做饭，然后说中文。
大家一边做饭，一边说中文。

exercises.prompt: 大家一边做饭，一___说中文。

options: at the same time (in 一边…一边…)
exercises.explanation: 一边 (yì biān) means “at the same time (in 一边…一边…)”.

lessons.title: 219. Presentation 3 grammar: the modal verb 会
lessons.subtitle: 我会说中文 · 你会不会写汉字？ · 很会做饭 · 不太会

explanations.title: Modal verb 会
explanations.body: The modal verb 会 indicates an ability that has been learned, that is, one knows how to do something. Pattern: Subject + 会 + Verb + Object.

examples.text: 我会说中文。
examples.translation: wǒ huì shuō zhōng wén — I can speak Chinese.

examples.text: 你会不会写汉字？
examples.translation: nǐ huì bú huì xiě hàn zì — Can you write Chinese characters?

examples.text: 大卫不会游泳。
examples.translation: dà wèi bú huì yóu yǒng — David can’t swim.

examples.text: 你们都会包饺子吗？
examples.translation: nǐ men dū huì bāo jiǎo zi ma — Can you all wrap dumplings?

examples.text: 我妈妈很会做饭，可是她不太会做中国饭。
examples.translation: wǒ mā mā hěn huì zuò fàn kě shì tā bú tài huì zuò zhōng guó fàn — My mother is very good at cooking, but she isn’t very good at cooking Chinese food.

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading and Speaking): can you …?
explanations.body: A. With a partner, take turns asking if he or she knows how to perform the activities below; keep going until you have used up all the items (the last item in the book is a smiley picture). New word: 用 yòng, to use. B. Report your findings to the class using patterns such as 我们都(很/不太/不)会…, 我会, 可是他不会…, 我会，他也会.

tables.title: Can you …?

examples.text: 我们都很会说中文。
examples.translation: wǒ men dōu hěn huì shuō zhōng wén — We can all speak Chinese very well.

examples.text: 我会包饺子，可是他不会包饺子。
examples.translation: wǒ huì bāo jiǎo zi kě shì tā bú huì bāo jiǎo zi — I can wrap dumplings, but he can’t.

examples.text: 我会游泳，他也会游泳。
examples.translation: wǒ huì yóu yǒng tā yě huì yóu yǒng — I can swim and he can swim too.

examples.text: 我们都不太会做红烧肉。
examples.translation: wǒ men dōu bú tài huì zuò hóng shāo ròu — None of us is very good at making soy-braised pork.

options: A learned ability: knowing how to do something

exercises.prompt: What does 大卫不会游泳 mean?
How do you ask “Can you write Chinese characters?” in the verb-not-verb form?
What does 我妈妈很会做饭 mean?
options: My mother is very good at cooking

exercises.prompt: What does 不太会 mean in 她不太会做中国饭?
Which sentence says “I can use chopsticks”?
How do you say “Can you order food in Chinese?”
exercises.explanation: 用中文 comes before 点菜.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence reports that both of you can do it?

options: can; be able to (a learned ability)
exercises.explanation: 会 (huì) means “can; be able to (a learned ability)”.

lessons.title: 220. Presentation 3 grammar: 了 in sequential actions
lessons.subtitle: 吃了饭以后，我们还看了一个中文电影 · 下了课，我们都得去操场跑步

explanations.title: 了 in sequential actions
explanations.body: 了 can be used in sequential actions to indicate that two actions take place one after another: 吃了饭以后，我们还看了一个中文电影 (We saw a Chinese movie after dinner). 了 in a sequence of actions is placed after the first verb. It can refer to a past action, a future action or repeated actions. Past: Subj. + V1 + 了 + Obj., V2 + 了 + (Num. + M) Obj.; or V1 + 了 + Obj., Subj. + V2 + 了 + (Num. + M) Obj. Future or repeated: Subj. + V1 + 了 + Obj., V2 + Obj.; or V1 + 了 + Obj., Subj. + V2 + Obj.

examples.text: 吃了饭以后，我们还看了一个中文电影。
examples.translation: chī le fàn yǐ hòu wǒ men hái kàn le yí gè zhōng wén diàn yǐng — We saw a Chinese movie after dinner.

examples.text: 上周六，买了东西，我和朋友看了一个中国电影。
examples.translation: shàng zhōu liù mǎi le dōng xī wǒ hé péng yǒu kàn le yí gè zhōng guó diàn yǐng — Last Saturday, after buying things, my friend and I saw a Chinese movie. (past action)

examples.text: 吃了午饭以后，我要去图书馆预习功课。
examples.translation: chī le wǔ fàn yǐ hòu wǒ yào qù tú shū guǎn yù xí gōng kè — After eating lunch, I am going to the library to preview the lessons. (future action)

examples.text: 张老师做了麻婆豆腐，还做了一个糖醋鱼。
examples.translation: zhāng lǎo shī zuò le má pó dòu fǔ hái zuò le yí gè táng cù yú — Teacher Zhang made mapo tofu, and also made a sweet and sour fish. (past action)

examples.text: 明天晚上，预习了功课，我要去值班。
examples.translation: míng tiān wǎn shàng yù xí le gōng kè wǒ yào qù zhí bān — Tomorrow evening, after previewing the lessons, I am going on duty. (future action)

examples.text: 每天，下了课，我们都得去操场跑步。
examples.translation: měi tiān xià le kè wǒ men dōu děi qù cāo chǎng pǎo bù — Every day, after class, we have to go run on the drill field. (repeated action)

examples.text: 每个周日，吃了早饭，我都去海边跑步。
examples.translation: měi gè zhōu rì chī le zǎo fàn wǒ dōu qù hǎi biān pǎo bù — Every Sunday, after eating breakfast, I go running at the beach. (repeated action)

explanations.title: Activity 6 (Reading and Speaking): sequences with 了
explanations.body: Pair up. Using the sequential action 了, take turns making sentences with the verbal phrase pairs listed below, and orally translate your partner’s sentences into English. The book’s two examples: 做作业，预习功课 → 做了作业以后，我又预习了明天的功课。 吃早饭，上课 → 等你吃了早饭，我们一起去上课吧。 The eight pairs of the activity, with sentences of my own:

examples.text: 做了作业以后，我又预习了明天的功课。
examples.translation: zuò le zuò yè yǐ hòu wǒ yòu yù xí le míng tiān de gōng kè — After doing my homework, I also previewed tomorrow’s lessons.

examples.text: 等你吃了早饭，我们一起去上课吧。
examples.translation: děng nǐ chī le zǎo fàn wǒ men yì qǐ qù shàng kè ba — When you have eaten breakfast, let’s go to class together.

examples.text: 我做了汤，还做了一个糖醋鱼。
examples.translation: wǒ zuò le tāng hái zuò le yí gè táng cù yú — I made soup, and also made a sweet and sour fish.

examples.text: 锻炼了以后，我们去电影院看电影吧。
examples.translation: duàn liàn le yǐ hòu wǒ men qù diàn yǐng yuàn kàn diàn yǐng ba — After working out, let’s go to the cinema to see a movie.

examples.text: 预习了课文，我们就去饭馆吃饭。
examples.translation: yù xí le kè wén wǒ men jiù qù fàn guǎn chī fàn — Once we have previewed the text, we’ll go to a restaurant to eat.

examples.text: 喝了汤以后，我们再吃饭。
examples.translation: hē le tāng yǐ hòu wǒ men zài chī fàn — After drinking the soup, we’ll eat.

examples.text: 值了班，我就去睡觉了。
examples.translation: zhí le bān wǒ jiù qù shuì jiào le — After going on duty, I went to sleep.

examples.text: 集合了以后，我们去上课。
examples.translation: jí hé le yǐ hòu wǒ men qù shàng kè — After forming up, we go to class.

explanations.title: Activity 7 (Listening and Writing)
explanations.body: Listen to four dialogs and write the activities you hear in sequential order using Chinese characters (audio, not included).

exercises.prompt: Where is 了 placed in a sequence of actions?
options: At the end of the sentence

exercises.prompt: What does the 了 after the first verb show?
options: The first action is completed before the second

exercises.prompt: Can the sequential 了 refer to a future action?
options: Yes: 吃了午饭以后，我要去图书馆预习功课

exercises.prompt: Can the sequential 了 refer to repeated actions?
options: Yes: 每天，下了课，我们都得去操场跑步

exercises.prompt: What does 每个周日，吃了早饭，我都去海边跑步 mean?
options: Every Sunday after breakfast I go running at the beach
I will run next Sunday only

exercises.prompt: What does 明天晚上，预习了功课，我要去值班 mean?
options: Tomorrow evening, after previewing the lessons, I will go on duty

exercises.prompt: What does 张老师做了麻婆豆腐，还做了一个糖醋鱼 mean?
options: Teacher Zhang made mapo tofu and also a sweet and sour fish

exercises.prompt: Which is right for “After class, we have to go to the drill field”?
options: 下了课，我们都得去操场。
我们都得去操场下了课。
下课了，我们都得去操场。
下课，了我们都得去操场。

exercises.prompt: 吃___午饭以后，我要去图书馆。
exercises.explanation: 了 comes after the first verb.

exercises.prompt: 上周六，买___东西，我和朋友看了一个中国电影。
下了课，我们都___去操场跑步。

exercises.explanation: 集合 (jí hé) means “have formation; muster”.

lessons.title: 221. Presentation 3 grammar: the pivotal construction
lessons.subtitle: 林老师教我们包饺子 · 他请我吃饭 · 妈妈叫我回家

explanations.title: The pivotal construction
explanations.body: In a pivotal sentence there are two predicates (verbs). The object of the first verb is also the subject of the second verb. Pattern: Subject + Verb 1 + Subject/Object + Verb 2 + Object 2.

examples.text: 林老师教我们包饺子。
examples.translation: lín lǎo shī jiāo wǒ men bāo jiǎo zi — Teacher Lin teaches us to wrap dumplings.

examples.text: 昨天，老师教我们唱了一个中国歌。
examples.translation: zuó tiān lǎo shī jiāo wǒ men chàng le yí gè zhōng guó gē — Yesterday the teacher taught us to sing a Chinese song.

examples.text: 他请我吃饭。
examples.translation: tā qǐng wǒ chī fàn — He invites me to dinner.

examples.text: 妈妈叫我回家。
examples.translation: mā mā jiào wǒ huí jiā — Mom tells me to come home.

explanations.title: Activity 8 (Reading and Writing): translate
explanations.body: Translate the three sentences into English. The key (mine):

examples.text: 我爸爸教我游泳。
examples.translation: wǒ bà bà jiāo wǒ yóu yǒng — My dad taught me how to swim.

examples.text: 陆老师教我们做了一个素菜。
examples.translation: lù lǎo shī jiāo wǒ men zuò le yí gè sù cài — Teacher Lu taught us to make a vegetable dish.

examples.text: 我的好朋友请我去他家。
examples.translation: wǒ de hǎo péng yǒu qǐng wǒ qù tā jiā — My good friend invited me to his home.

exercises.prompt: How many predicates (verbs) does a pivotal sentence have?
What is special about the object of the first verb?
options: It comes after the second verb
It is also the subject of the second verb

exercises.prompt: In 林老师教我们包饺子, which word is the pivot?
exercises.explanation: 我们 is the object of 教 and the subject of 包.

exercises.prompt: In 他请我吃饭, which word is the pivot?
exercises.explanation: 我 is the object of 请 and the subject of 吃.

exercises.prompt: In 妈妈叫我回家, who comes home?
exercises.explanation: 我 is the subject of 回家.

exercises.prompt: What does 他请我吃饭 mean?
What does 妈妈叫我回家 mean?
options: I tell mom to come home
Mom tells me to come home
exercises.explanation: 叫 here means to tell, to ask.

exercises.prompt: What does 我的好朋友请我去他家 mean?
options: I invited my friend to my home
My good friend invited me to his home

exercises.explanation: 教 + people + verb: teach someone to do.
请我吃饭: invite me to eat.

lessons.title: 222. Presentation 3 skill integration: true or false, dumplings and regional tastes
lessons.subtitle: 我不好意思 · 饺子馅儿 · 一边包一边笑 · 南甜、北咸、东辣、西酸

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Writing and Reading): true or false
explanations.body: A. Listen to the passage once, then write what you remember in pinyin or characters. B. Listen again and refine your notes. C. Decide whether the five statements are true or false based on the passage (the recording is not included, so the key cannot be given here). D. Discuss your answers with the class, then listen again to confirm or correct your understanding. The five statements:

examples.text: 我是韩国人,在中国上学。
examples.translation: wǒ shì hán guó rén zài zhōng guó shàng xué — I am Korean and I go to school in China.

examples.text: 朋友的爸爸妈妈一起做菜。
examples.translation: péng yǒu de bà bà mā mā yì qǐ zuò cài — My friend’s father and mother cook together.

examples.text: 朋友的妈妈也会做菜。
examples.translation: péng yǒu de mā mā yě huì zuò cài — My friend’s mother can cook too.

examples.text: 我不好意思，因为我不会做菜。
examples.translation: wǒ bù hǎo yì sī yīn wèi wǒ bú huì zuò cài — I feel embarrassed because I can’t cook.

examples.text: 今天很有意思，因为我吃了很好吃的中国菜。
examples.translation: jīn tiān hěn yǒu yì si yīn wèi wǒ chī le hěn hǎo chī de zhōng guó cài — Today was interesting because I ate delicious Chinese food.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Listening, Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Listen to a dialog and complete a table: the people mentioned and their relationships, and what you learned about them (audio, not included). B. Pair up and ask each other questions in Chinese about the dialog to verify your notes.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading and Speaking): making dumplings
explanations.body: A. Read the passage and highlight the words you don’t know; try to work out their meaning from context. B. In groups of three, check your understanding of the words you highlighted. C. Identify the pictures (six, not included) that apply to the passage and discuss your choices with the group in Chinese.

examples.text: 我的老家在北京。中国北方人都很喜欢吃饺子。可是来美国以后，我就很少吃饺子了。上个周末，我请了几个同学一起包饺子。我们都不太会做饺子皮，所以饺子皮是买的。我们先做饺子馅儿，有肉馅儿，也有素菜鸡蛋馅儿。做完馅儿我们就开始包饺子。大家一边包一边笑，因为有的饺子真的太难看了！可是，味道还是挺不错的。我们每人吃了二十多个！大家都说，以后还要一起包饺子。不过，下次一定要自己做饺子皮。
examples.translation: wǒ de lǎo jiā zài běi jīng zhōng guó běi fāng rén dōu hěn xǐ huān chī jiǎo zi kě shì lái měi guó yǐ hòu wǒ jiù hěn shǎo chī jiǎo zi le shàng gè zhōu mò wǒ qǐng le jǐ gè tóng xué yì qǐ bāo jiǎo zi wǒ men dōu bú tài huì zuò jiǎo zi pí suǒ yǐ jiǎo zi pí shì mǎi de wǒ men xiān zuò jiǎo zi xiànr yǒu ròu xiànr yě yǒu sù cài jī dàn xiànr zuò wán xiànr wǒ men jiù kāi shǐ bāo jiǎo zi dà jiā yì biān bāo yì biān xiào yīn wèi yǒu de jiǎo zi zhēn de tài nán kàn le kě shì wèi dào hái shì tǐng bú cuò de wǒ men měi rén chī le èr shí duō gè dà jiā dōu shuō yǐ hòu hái yào yì qǐ bāo jiǎo zi bú guò xià cì yí dìng yào zì jǐ zuò jiǎo zi pí — My hometown is in Beijing. Northern Chinese all like to eat dumplings very much. But since coming to America I rarely eat dumplings. Last weekend I invited a few classmates to wrap dumplings together. None of us is very good at making dumpling wrappers, so the wrappers were bought. We first made the filling, with meat filling and also vegetable and egg filling. After making the filling we began to wrap the dumplings. Everyone laughed while wrapping, because some of the dumplings really looked too ugly! But the taste was still quite good. We each ate more than twenty! Everyone said that in the future we will wrap dumplings together again. But next time we must make the wrappers ourselves.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Writing and Speaking): regional tastes
explanations.body: A. Read the passage and highlight the words you don’t know. B. In groups of three, check the terms you highlighted. C. Copy the keywords from the passage in the space provided and discuss your choice of key words with the group in Chinese. My choice of keywords:

examples.text: 每个地方的饭菜都有自己的特色。有人说，中国菜是南甜、北咸、东辣、西酸。意思是说南方人喜欢吃甜的，北方人喜欢吃咸的，东部的人爱吃辣的，西部的人爱吃酸的。不过，真正喜欢吃辣的人是在湖南、湖北、四川这些地方。喜欢吃辣和气候有关。这些地方一年四季很少有太阳，阴天多，雾也多。吃辣椒出汗，对身体很有好处。东北一些地区的人也喜欢吃辣，这是因为那里气候寒冷，吃完辣椒就暖和了。
examples.translation: měi gè dì fāng de fàn cài dōu yǒu zì jǐ de tè sè yǒu rén shuō zhōng guó cài shì nán tián běi xián dōng là xī suān yì si shì shuō nán fāng rén xǐ huān chī tián de běi fāng rén xǐ huān chī xián de dōng bù de rén ài chī là de xī bù de rén ài chī suān de bú guò zhēn zhèng xǐ huān chī là de rén shì zài hú nán hú běi sì chuān zhè xiē dì fāng xǐ huān chī là hé qì hòu yǒu guān zhè xiē dì fāng yì nián sì jì hěn shǎo yǒu tài yáng yīn tiān duō wù yě duō chī là jiāo chū hàn duì shēn tǐ hěn yǒu hǎo chù dōng běi yì xiē dì qū de rén yě xǐ huān chī là zhè shì yīn wèi nà lǐ qì hòu hán lěng chī wán là jiāo jiù nuǎn huo le — The food of every place has its own character. Some say that Chinese food is “south sweet, north salty, east spicy, west sour”. This means that southerners like sweet food, northerners like salty food, people in the east love spicy food, and people in the west love sour food. But the people who truly like spicy food are in places like Hunan, Hubei and Sichuan. Liking spicy food is related to the climate. In these places there is little sun all year round, with many overcast days and a lot of fog. Eating chili peppers makes you sweat, which is very good for the body. People in some parts of the northeast also like spicy food, because the climate there is cold, and after eating chili peppers you feel warm.

examples.text: 南甜、北咸、东辣、西酸
examples.translation: nán tián běi xián dōng là xī suān — south sweet, north salty, east spicy, west sour

examples.text: 湖南、湖北、四川
examples.translation: hú nán hú běi sì chuān — Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan

examples.text: 气候
examples.translation: qì hòu — climate

examples.text: 吃辣椒出汗
examples.translation: chī là jiāo chū hàn — eating chili peppers makes you sweat

examples.text: 东北，气候寒冷，暖和
examples.translation: dōng běi qì hòu hán lěng nuǎn huo — the northeast: cold climate, warm up

lessons.title: 223. Presentation 3: using Chinese in context (a dish, interviews, a Saturday)

explanations.title: Activities 2 and 3: interview the instructors; plan a potluck
explanations.body: Activity 2: interview some Chinese instructors about their hometown cuisine, the types of dishes they like to cook, and the dishes they would recommend from their favorite restaurant. A. As a class, generate six interview questions and write them in Chinese. B. Interview the instructors and take notes. C. Report your results to the class while the others take notes; your teacher will then ask the class questions about the interview. Activity 3: plan a Chinese potluck for the class from the interview results. A. Divide into two groups: Plan A, based on the dishes the instructors like to cook; Plan B, based on the dishes they recommended from their favorite restaurants. Each group presents its plan. B. Vote for the best plan.

lessons.title: 224. Area Studies: Food in Chinese Culture
lessons.subtitle: 饭 and 菜 · eight cuisines · stir-frying · alcohol · tea

explanations.title: Food in Chinese Culture (1): fan and cai, and the regional styles
explanations.body:
Although written records only date back to 1250 BCE, China is popularly said to have “5,000 years of civilization.” Regardless, its venerable culinary tradition has always been an integral part of Chinese culture.

In Chinese cuisine, food preparation is complex. Food is divided into fan (饭 fàn) and cai (菜 cài), fan being grains such as rice, and cai being vegetables and meat. Both ingredients are necessary for a balanced meal. To prepare cai, a cook must cut up and mix different ingredients to enhance their flavors and increase variety. Pork, for example, can be diced, shredded, or ground and combined with various other meats.

Chinese cuisine can be basically divided into Southern and Northern styles. Southern cuisine emphasizes freshness and tenderness, while Northern dishes tend to be richer in oil and reliant on vinegar and garlic. The four oldest types of Chinese food are Sichuanese, Cantonese, Northern, and Huaiyang. Eventually, eight types of Chinese cuisine evolved, each of which has its own distinct history and characteristics. Many Chinese dishes are named after historical figures, such as 东坡肉 (dōngpōròu, steamed pork shoulder), the favorite dish of Song dynasty poet 苏东坡; 贵妃鸡 (guìfēijī, Imperial Concubine Chicken), named after the Tang dynasty courtesan, 杨贵妃; and the spicy 左宗棠鸡 (zuǒzōngtángjī, General Zuo’s Chicken), named for the Qing dynasty Hunanese general, 左宗棠.

explanations.title: Food in Chinese Culture (2): cooking methods
explanations.body: Chinese food involves stir-frying, deep-frying, steaming, stewing or roasting. Stir-frying is the most common and entails quick cooking over high heat with a small amount of oil. With this method, meat stays juicy and vegetables remain crisp. Chinese people are very conscious of what they eat and enjoy nutritious food from the vegetable, herb and fungi kingdoms; in fact, many foods are specifically prepared for disease prevention and cure. As both science and art, Chinese cuisine also prescribes how different foods should be cooked and prepared for optimal health.

explanations.title: Alcohol
explanations.body:
Alcohol, of course, is also a part of traditional Chinese culture. It plays an important role in birthday parties for adults, wedding feasts, business banquets, and even ceremonial offerings at ancestral gravesites. Naturally, it is also part of daily life. In restaurants or bars, for example, people play drinking games, like the “finger guessing game” (划拳 or 猜拳). A little like “paper, scissors, rock,” two players each throw out a Chinese hand sign for a number from zero to ten while one of them calls a number out loud. If the combined sign numbers add up to the “caller’s” number, he wins and the loser has to drink. There are many other drinking games that involve telling jokes, riddles, or playing on Chinese customs or poetry.

Alcohol also features prominently in Chinese art and literature. In general, Chinese people consider moderate drinking healthy and now imbibe a wide variety of liquor, wine and beer. The most famous Chinese liquors are Maotai, Fenjiu, and Wuliangye. The foremost three wines are Great Wall Wine, Dynasty Wine and Changyu Wine. The top three beers are China Resources Beer, Tsingtao and AB InBev.

tables.title: Names in the reading (1)

explanations.title: Tea
explanations.body:
China has cultivated tea for over three thousand years. It is an integral part of Chinese culture and cuisine. Legend has it that tea was introduced to China by the mythical emperor and herbalist Shénnóng 神农 in 2737 BC. There are five major types: green tea, Oolong tea, jasmine tea, black tea and compressed tea. These teas are classified according to the different ways they are processed. For example, green tea is not fermented to preserve the original color, fragrance and flavor of the leaves. The three finest teas in China are considered to be West Lake Longjing, Dahongpao and Tieguanyin.

Tea is the most important daily beverage in China, valued for both its health properties and its salient role in social customs and ceremony. Chinese people believe that tea cools and relaxes by dispelling heat from the body, so teahouses abound in cities, towns and villages, where locals often meet to chat over a cup of tea. An ancient Chinese proverb says, “Better to go without salt for three days than without tea for a single day.”

Chinese tea has been internationally renowned for centuries. The world’s largest tea producer, China exported $2 billion worth of tea in 2019, 31.8% of the global market share.

explanations.title: Lesson 9 Shopping: objectives
explanations.body: 第九课 买东西. Upon completion of this lesson you will be able to obtain and provide information about shopping: asking and giving opinions, asking to exchange one item for another, asking for the unit and total price, negotiating a price and asking for the payment method; and narrate a past shopping experience. To do this you must master: the new words and phrases of the Core Vocabulary; the basic monetary units; the basic units of weight; 有一点儿 + adjective; adjective + 一点儿; adjective 了 + 一点儿; measure words for clothing, daily necessities and produce; basic color names; 快 + verb + 了; 就 (just, only); the 连…也/都… pattern; and the pivotal construction 请. Area Studies: Shopping in China.

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss. A. When was the last time you shopped for clothes? Where did you go? What did you buy? B. What are some questions you might ask the store clerk? Can you ask them in Chinese?

lessons.title: 228. Lesson 9 Presentation 1 grammar: the basic Chinese money units
lessons.subtitle: 块（元）· 毛（角）· 分 · 九百零五 · 十九块零八

explanations.title: Basic Chinese monetary units
explanations.body: The basic units are 块/元, 毛/角 and 分. Grammatically, 块/元, 毛/角 and 分 are measure words as well as nouns. 元 and 角 are formal versions usually found only in written Chinese. When one or more units or digits are skipped, 零 must be inserted to fill the gap, as in the last three examples. 钱 (money) may be added at the end: 两块钱. In spoken Chinese the last unit is often dropped (九块二 for 9.20; 七十九块四毛二).

lessons.title: 229. Lesson 9 Presentation 1 grammar: 有(一)点儿 + adjective
lessons.subtitle: 有一点儿贵 · 有点儿热 · 今天我有一点儿不高兴

explanations.title: The 有(一)点儿 + Adjective pattern
explanations.body: The pattern “有一点儿 + adjective” describes something dissatisfying, uncomfortable or contrary to one’s wishes. In essence it means “a bit too much” of a certain quality. Hence you will not hear *有点高兴, *有点舒服 or *有点好玩儿, because “happy”, “comfortable” and “fun” are adjectives with positive connotations. It is correct, however, to say 今天我有一点儿不高兴/不舒服. Patterns: Subject + 有一点(儿) + Adjective; Subject + 有点(儿) + Adjective (spoken Chinese). Also: the shortened answer must keep 有 (*一点忙，一点快 is wrong).

examples.text: 上个周末有一点儿忙。
examples.translation: shàng gè zhōu mò yǒu yì diǎnr máng — Last weekend was a bit busy.

examples.text: 这件衣服有一点儿贵。
examples.translation: zhè jiàn yī fú yǒu yì diǎnr guì — This piece of clothing is a bit expensive.

examples.text: 今天有一点儿热。
examples.translation: jīn tiān yǒu yì diǎnr rè — Today is a bit hot.

examples.text: 纽约的冬天有一点儿冷。
examples.translation: niǔ yuē de dōng tiān yǒu yì diǎnr lěng — Winter in New York is a bit cold.

examples.text: 这道菜有一点儿辣。
examples.translation: zhè dào cài yǒu yì diǎnr là — This dish is a bit spicy.

examples.text: 今天我有一点儿不高兴。
examples.translation: jīn tiān wǒ yǒu yì diǎnr bù gāo xìng — Today I am a bit unhappy.

examples.text: 甲：国防语言学院的学习怎么样？

examples.text: 乙：有一点忙，有一点快。
examples.translation: yǐ yǒu yì diǎn máng yǒu yì diǎn kuài — A bit busy, a bit fast.

lessons.title: 230. Lesson 9 Presentation 1 grammar: adjective + 了 + (一)点儿
lessons.subtitle: 小了一点儿 · 咸了点 · 贵了一点 · 不能说“紧张了一点”

explanations.title: The Adjective + 了 + (一)点儿 pattern
explanations.body: “Adjective 了 + 一点儿” is similar to “有一点(儿) + adjective” in expressing “a little bit too much”. However, only “有一点(儿) + adjective” can take adjectives or emotive verbs such as 紧张, 不高兴 and 难过 (nánguò, sad). You can say 有一点紧张, 有点不高兴 or 有一点难过, but it is incorrect to say *紧张了一点, *不高兴了一点 or *难过了一点. Pattern: Adjective + 了(一)点儿.

examples.text: 这条裤子小了一点儿，有大一号的吗？
examples.translation: zhè tiáo kù zi xiǎo le yì diǎnr yǒu dà yī hào de ma — These trousers are a little too small; do you have a size bigger?

examples.text: 这道菜咸了点，能换一盘清淡一点的吗？
examples.translation: zhè dào cài xián le diǎn néng huàn yì pán qīng dàn yì diǎn de ma — This dish is a little too salty; can I change it for a milder one?

examples.text: 现在做作业晚了一点吧？五分钟后你就得交了。
examples.translation: xiàn zài zuò zuò yè wǎn le yì diǎn ba wǔ fēn zhōng hòu nǐ jiù děi jiāo le — Isn’t it a bit late to do homework now? In five minutes you have to hand it in.

examples.text: 蒙特雷的夏天冷了一点，所以不能去游泳。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de xià tiān lěng le yì diǎn suǒ yǐ bù néng qù yóu yǒng — Summer in Monterey is a bit too cold, so you can’t go swimming.

examples.text: 这个学校贵了一点，但是老师都很不错。
examples.translation: zhè ge xué xiào guì le yì diǎn dàn shì lǎo shī dōu hěn bú cuò — This school is a little expensive, but the teachers are all very good.

咸了点: a little too salty.
Only 有一点 can take emotive adjectives like 紧张.

options: Summer in Monterey is very hot

exercises.explanation: 冷了一点: a bit too cold.

The school is cheap and the teachers are bad

options: It may be a bit late to do homework now
exercises.explanation: 晚了一点: a bit too late.

options: At the end of the sentence

exercises.explanation: 咸了点: a little too salty.

lessons.title: 231. Lesson 9 Presentation 1 grammar: adjective + (一)点儿 for requests
lessons.subtitle: 便宜一点儿 · 快一点儿 · 小一号 · 有点儿贵 / 贵了点儿 / 便宜点

explanations.title: The Adjective + (一)点儿 pattern
explanations.body: “Adjective + (一)点儿” is very different from “有(一)点儿 + adjective” in both form and meaning. In form, 有一点儿 precedes the adjective, while (一)点儿 follows it. In meaning, “有一点 + adjective” has an undesirable or negative connotation, while “adjective + 一点” connotes desirability. The latter is most often used in making requests. Pattern: Adjective + 一点(儿).

examples.text: 请你快一点儿！
examples.translation: qǐng nǐ kuài yì diǎnr — Please hurry up a little!

examples.text: 老板，能不能便宜一点儿？
examples.translation: lǎo bǎn néng bù néng pián yi yì diǎnr — Boss, can you make it a little cheaper?

examples.text: 这件黑皮鞋比那双白皮鞋质量好一点。
examples.translation: zhè jiàn hēi pí xié bǐ nà shuāng bái pí xié zhì liàng hǎo yì diǎn — These black leather shoes are a little better in quality than those white ones.

examples.text: 蒙特雷的冬天比纽约暖和一点儿。
examples.translation: méng tè léi de dōng tiān bǐ niǔ yuē nuǎn huo yì diǎnr — Winter in Monterey is a little warmer than in New York.

examples.text: 明天人一定很多，请你早一点来。
examples.translation: míng tiān rén yí dìng hěn duō qǐng nǐ zǎo yì diǎn lái — There will be a lot of people tomorrow; please come a little earlier.

explanations.title: When you know the exact size: 一号
explanations.body: When you know the exact size or amount you need, instead of 一点儿 use “Adjective + 了 + exact amount” to express dissatisfaction and “Adjective + exact amount” to express your preference.

examples.text: 这件衣服有大一点吗？
examples.translation: zhè jiàn yī fú yǒu dà yì diǎn ma — Do you have this piece in a slightly bigger size?

examples.text: 这件衣服大了一号，有没有小一号的？
examples.translation: zhè jiàn yī fú dà le yī hào yǒu méi yǒu xiǎo yī hào de — This piece is one size too big; do you have one size smaller?

explanations.title: Three patterns compared
explanations.body: To describe something undesirable use 有(一)点(儿) + adjective or adjective + 了(一)点(儿); to make a request use adjective + (一)点(儿). The adjective 贵 (expensive) goes with all three; an emotive word like 不高兴 cannot take 了点, so it has an X in the middle:

tables.title: Describing and requesting

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading and Speaking): dissatisfaction, then a request
explanations.body: A. Student A uses “有一点儿 + adjective” to express dissatisfaction with each item below (the book has 这条衬衫; 这件衬衫 is the usual measure word); Student B repeats it and uses “adjective + 一点儿” to request their preference. Example: 这件衣服有一点儿贵。 → 这件衣服有一点贵，有没有便宜一点儿的？ B. Student B uses “adjective 了 + 一点儿”, e.g. 这件衣服贵了一点儿。 → 这件衣服贵了一点儿，有没有便宜一点儿的？ Sentences made from the two lists (mine):

examples.text: 这件衬衫有一点儿贵，有没有便宜一点儿的？

examples.text: 这套西装有一点儿大，有没有小一点儿的？
examples.translation: zhè tào xī zhuāng yǒu yì diǎnr dà yǒu méi yǒu xiǎo yì diǎnr de — 这套西装 is a bit too 大; do you have one that is a little 小?

examples.text: 这个教室有一点儿小，有没有大一点儿的？
examples.translation: zhè ge jiào shì yǒu yì diǎnr xiǎo yǒu méi yǒu dà yì diǎnr de — 这个教室 is a bit too 小; do you have one that is a little 大?

examples.text: 这道麻婆豆腐贵了一点儿，有没有便宜一点儿的？
examples.translation: zhè dào má pó dòu fǔ guì le yì diǎnr yǒu méi yǒu pián yi yì diǎnr de — 这道麻婆豆腐 is a little too 贵; do you have one that is a little 便宜?

examples.text: 今晚的作业多了一点儿，有没有少一点儿的？
examples.translation: jīn wǎn de zuò yè duō le yì diǎnr yǒu méi yǒu shǎo yì diǎnr de — 今晚的作业 is a little too 多; do you have one that is a little 少?

examples.text: 这家饭店淡了一点儿，有没有辣一点儿的？
examples.translation: zhè jiā fàn diàn dàn le yì diǎnr yǒu méi yǒu là yì diǎnr de — 这家饭店 is a little too 淡; do you have one that is a little 辣?

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Listening and Speaking): a customer and a clerk
explanations.body: A. Listen to a dialog between a customer and a clerk, take notes and summarize (audio, not included). B. Listen again and decide whether each statement is true or false; say the correct answers for the false statements aloud. (The key needs the recording.) The four statements:

examples.text: 客人买了黑西装，因为比蓝的便宜。

Example: 我觉得每天晚上的作业有点儿多，作业可以少一点吗？ B. Share your list with the class in Chinese. C. As a class, select the top three suggestions for the team leader.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading, Writing and Speaking): the passage
explanations.body: A. Read the passage and answer in Chinese: 1. What did the customer want to buy? 2. What did he end up buying, and why? 3. What is his method of payment and how much does he pay? B. Check your answers with a partner in Chinese. C. In pairs, write your own clerk and customer dialog based on the passage and act it out; switch roles and repeat.

examples.text: 这位客人想买一件红颜色的衬衫。服务员给他中号的，可是那件衬衫有点大，他请服务员给他小一号的。不过那件衬衫没有他要的颜色，只有蓝色的。他还是试了一下。他觉得挺合适的就买了那件。因为他没有这么多现金，最后他用手机扫码付费，一共付了七十六块五。
examples.translation: zhè wèi kè rén xiǎng mǎi yí jiàn hóng yán sè de chèn shān fú wù yuán gěi tā zhōng hào de kě shì nà jiàn chèn shān yǒu diǎn dà tā qǐng fú wù yuán gěi tā xiǎo yī hào de bú guò nà jiàn chèn shān méi yǒu tā yào de yán sè zhǐ yǒu lán sè de tā hái shì shì le yí xià tā jué de tǐng hé shì de jiù mǎi le nà jiàn yīn wèi tā méi yǒu zhè me duō xiàn jīn zuì hòu tā yòng shǒu jī sǎo mǎ fù fèi yí gòng fù le qī shí liù kuài wǔ — This customer wanted to buy a red shirt. The clerk gave him a medium, but that shirt was a little big, so he asked the clerk for one a size smaller. But that shirt did not come in the color he wanted, only in blue. He tried it on anyway. He felt it fit very well, so he bought it. Because he did not have that much cash, in the end he paid by scanning a code with his cell phone, 76.5 yuan in all.
