lessons.title: 526. Lesson 21 Presentation 1 skill integration: registration chart and two hospital notices
lessons.subtitle: 挂号流程 · 预约方式 · 人工窗口挂号 · 自助机挂号 · 初诊 复诊

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Speaking and Reading)
explanations.body: A. Pair up; each student listens to one segment of a conversation and answers questions. Segment 1: 1. What happened to the woman’s son? 2. Is the mother familiar with the place? How do you know? 3. What suggestion does the second speaker give? 4. Which department should the mother register for? 5. What does the mother ask the second speaker to do for her? 6. What does the mother need to show the second speaker, and why? Segment 2: 1. How long does the mother have to wait? 2. What should the mother pay attention to? 3. What should the mother fill out? 4. What should she do on future visits? 5. What is her registration number? 6. What reminder is the mother given at the end? B. Exchange information with your partner in Chinese. C. Listen to the entire conversation and reorder the activities 1. 准备医保卡, 2. 买病历本, 3. 填病历本, 4. 挂号, 5. 预约 in the sequence you hear. D. Share your answers and read the script. (Audio, not included; my sequence from the flow chart: 预约 → 准备医保卡 → 挂号 → 买病历本 → 填病历本.)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Listening, Speaking and Reading)
explanations.body: A. Listen to a dialog and mark each statement True or False: 1. 病人不知道在哪儿挂号。 2. 病人第一次来看病。 3. 病人已经打电话预约了。 4. 病人挂的是普通门诊内科。 5. 王大夫是医院最有名的专家。 6. 病人最近开始头疼。 7. 病人只有医保卡，没有病历卡。 8. 病人不需要在挂号窗口排队挂号。 B. Listen again and answer in detail: 1. How could the patient get his registration number from the self-service registration machine? List at least three details. 2. What payment methods does the self-service machine accept? C. Pair up and share. D. Read the script. (Audio, not included; the book prints no key.)

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: Answer the following questions based on the information in the chart: 1. What is the information about? 2. How many ways are patients permitted to register and what are they? 3. When should patients make their appointment? 4. What registration methods were used when you visited the doctor?

rows: 支付宝生活号；微信公众号
平安医疗导航平台；平安互联医疗平台支付宝生活号；平安预约医疗服务平台；平安联挂号服务

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Writing, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. Pair up and read the patient guide for a hospital in Taiwan at the link given (wd.vghtpe.gov.tw). You read Part 1 and your partner reads Part 2; write a summary of the part you read, including what the guide is about and what patients should and should not do (under the headings 初诊/初診 and 复诊/複診). B. In Chinese, exchange your information. C. What are the differences between the registration process in hospitals in Taiwan and in the U.S.? Share your thoughts with the class. (The linked guide is not included.)

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading, Writing, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: You want to understand the best way to register at a hospital in China, so you find the information below on a hospital’s website. A. Pair up; each student reads their own part, then notes the advantages in their partner’s part. B. Share your information and complete the table with your partner’s. C. Compare the information and decide which way you prefer; share your choice with the class. D. Learn three new Chinese words from the passages (my three: 自助, 缴费, 人工). Student 1 and Student 2:

rows: 可以买病历本或办病历卡，有问题可以问工作人员
功能多，可以用现金、支付宝、银行卡付钱，也可以自己办卡
提前预约好，到医院用手机或自助机取号就行了
tables.title: Activity 5: the advantages of the three ways (the book leaves the table blank; this is my filling)

examples.text: 人工窗口挂号。挂号交费人工窗口位于门诊六到八楼。带身份证的病人，可到人工窗口填写病历信息登记表，购买病历本或办理病历卡，挂普通门诊看病。网上提前预约好了，如何挂号？一、可用支付宝或微信“预约取号”功能，完成手机取号。二、也可以在门诊大厅自助机上使用“预约取号”功能，自助取号。三、或是到门诊六到八楼人工窗口取号。
examples.translation: rén gōng chuāng kǒu guà hào guà hào jiāo fèi rén gōng chuāng kǒu wèi yú mén zhěn liù dào bā lóu dài shēn fèn zhèng de bìng rén kě dào rén gōng chuāng kǒu tián xiě bìng lì xìn xī dēng jì biǎo gòu mǎi bìng lì běn huò bàn lǐ bìng lì kǎ guà pǔ tōng mén zhěn kàn bìng wǎng shàng tí qián yù yuē hǎo le rú hé guà hào yì kě yòng zhī fù bǎo huò wēi xìn yù yuē qǔ hào gōng néng wán chéng shǒu jī qǔ hào èr yě kě yǐ zài mén zhěn dà tīng zì zhù jī shàng shǐ yòng yù yuē qǔ hào gōng néng zì zhù qǔ hào sān huò shì dào mén zhěn liù dào bā lóu rén gōng chuāng kǒu qǔ hào — Registering at the manual window. The manual registration and payment windows are on floors 6 to 8 of the outpatient building. Patients with an ID card can go to a manual window, fill in the medical-record information form, buy a record book or get a record card, and register for a regular outpatient visit. If you have booked online in advance, how do you register? 1. You can use the “collect number for appointment” function of Alipay or WeChat to collect a number on your phone. 2. You can also use the “collect number for appointment” function on the self-service machine in the outpatient hall. 3. Or go to the manual windows on floors 6 to 8 to collect a number. (Student 1’s part; the book writes 6-8 and 1、2、3; translation mine)

examples.text: 自助机挂号。一、门诊各楼层的自助机有自助挂号、缴费、预约挂号、预约取号和自助办卡、账户管理等功能。二、自助机可以用现金、支付宝、银行卡等方式支付。三、第一次看病的病人，可以使用自助机办理病历卡：（一）用二代身份证通过自助机自助办理；（二）有支付宝的病人，可以使用自助机的“支付宝刷脸”功能自助办理；（三）也可以使用手机应用或支付宝申请电子病历卡或医保卡。
examples.translation: zì zhù jī guà hào yì mén zhěn gè lóu céng de zì zhù jī yǒu zì zhù guà hào jiǎo fèi yù yuē guà hào yù yuē qǔ hào hé zì zhù bàn kǎ zhàng hù guǎn lǐ děng gōng néng èr zì zhù jī kě yǐ yòng xiàn jīn zhī fù bǎo yín háng kǎ děng fāng shì zhī fù sān dì yī cì kàn bìng de bìng rén kě yǐ shǐ yòng zì zhù jī bàn lǐ bìng lì kǎ yí yòng èr dài shēn fèn zhèng tōng guò zì zhù jī zì zhù bàn lǐ èr yǒu zhī fù bǎo de bìng rén kě yǐ shǐ yòng zì zhù jī de zhī fù bǎo shuā liǎn gōng néng zì zhù bàn lǐ sān yě kě yǐ shǐ yòng shǒu jī yìng yòng huò zhī fù bǎo shēn qǐng diàn zi bìng lì kǎ huò yī bǎo kǎ — Registering at the self-service machine. 1. The self-service machines on each floor of the outpatient building have the functions of self-service registration, payment, appointment registration, collecting a number for an appointment, getting a card and account management. 2. The machines accept cash, Alipay, bank cards and other ways of payment. 3. Patients on a first visit can use the machine to get a record card: (1) with the second-generation ID card through the machine; (2) patients with Alipay can use the machine’s “Alipay face scan” function; (3) or apply for an electronic record card or insurance card with a phone app or Alipay. (Student 2’s part; translation mine)

lessons.title: 527. Lesson 21 Presentation 1 using Chinese in context: helping a friend see a doctor in Beijing
lessons.subtitle: 北京大学的朋友生病了 · 中国和美国看病的流程 · 打电话问医院

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading, Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: Scenario: while studying at Beijing University, one of your American friends became ill and had to go to a hospital in Beijing. You and your classmates need to research to help your friend make an appointment and register, and explain the similarities and differences between Chinese and U.S. procedures. A. During your research online you find a chart (a picture, not included). Work in pairs; one of you reads the part about China and the other the part about the U.S. B. Exchange information and, in Chinese characters or pinyin, take notes in the table (流程: 预约, 挂号, 看病, 取药). C. Based on your notes, write the similarities and differences (相同点 / 不同点). D. Share your result in the class. My table:

rows: 打电话、用手机或网上预约，也可以到医院的自助机预约
带身份证、医保卡到挂号窗口或自助机挂号，买病历本
到诊所前台登记，出示保险卡
在候诊室等护士叫号，叫到号就进去看病
在候诊室等护士叫名字，然后看医生
先划价、交费，然后去药房取药
医生开药方，到药店取药
tables.title: Activity 1B: the process in China and in the U.S. (the chart in the book is a picture, not included; the China column is from this lesson and the U.S. column is my general description)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Writing, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: Scenario: after learning the procedures of making an appointment and registering in a Chinese hospital, you and your classmates call the hospital where you will take your friend and want more information. A. Work in pairs and make a list of questions to ask, covering: 1. the most convenient way to book an appointment, 2. what to bring, 3. which department to register for, 4. paperwork, 5. insurance, 6. payment. B. Each pair calls the hospital (the teacher and two students play the patient-assistance worker) and writes down the answers. C. In a group of three share the information and decide how to handle the appointment and registration. D. After the discussion call the hospital again, make an appointment and register your friend. My six questions:

examples.text: 请问，挂号和预约最方便的办法是什么？
examples.translation: qǐng wèn guà hào hé yù yuē zuì fāng biàn de bàn fǎ shì shén me — 1. Excuse me, what is the most convenient way to register and make an appointment? (mine)

examples.text: 去医院的时候，我要带什么？
examples.translation: qù yī yuàn de shí hòu wǒ yào dài shén me — 2. What do I need to bring when I go to the hospital? (mine)

examples.text: 我头疼，还有点发烧，应该挂哪一科？
examples.translation: wǒ tóu téng hái yǒu diǎn fā shāo yīng gāi guà nǎ yì kē — 3. I have a headache and a bit of fever; which department should I register for? (mine)

examples.text: 挂号需要填什么表？要不要买病历本？
examples.translation: guà hào xū yào tián shén me biǎo yào bú yào mǎi bìng lì běn — 4. What forms do I need to fill in to register? Do I need to buy a record book? (mine)

examples.text: 你们收不收外国人的医保卡？
examples.translation: nǐ men shōu bù shōu wài guó rén de yī bǎo kǎ — 5. Do you accept foreigners’ medical insurance cards? (mine)

examples.text: 可以用现金付钱，还是只能用手机付钱？
examples.translation: kě yǐ yòng xiàn jīn fù qián hái shì zhǐ néng yòng shǒu jī fù qián — 6. Can I pay with cash, or only by phone? (mine)

exercises.prompt: Who needs help in the scenario?
options: An American friend studying in Beijing

exercises.prompt: What do you need to explain to your friend?
options: The similarities and differences between Chinese and U.S. procedures

explanations.title: Degree Complements with 得 (Verb + 得 vs Adjective + 得)
explanations.body: In Chinese there are two main reasons for using degree complements: to express how a verb happened or assess its quality, and to express to what extent (or degree) an adjective is true. Degree complements are usually composed of an adverb (sometimes omitted) and an adjective together. They appear after the main verb or adjective in a sentence with a 得 marker between them.

rows: V + 得 + degree complement (degree adverb + adjective)
V + O + V + 得 + degree complement
V + 得 + 不 + degree complement (adjective)
V + 得 + complement (adjective) + 不 + complement (adjective)
tables.title: Verbs with degree complements (Verb + 得 + degree complement)

examples.text: 前两天流得厉害，今天不流了，但是有点堵。
examples.translation: qián liǎng tiān liú de lì hài jīn tiān bù liú le dàn shì yǒu diǎn dǔ — 1. I had a very bad runny nose over the past couple of days. Today it stopped, but my nose is a bit stuffy.

examples.text: 我发烧、咳嗽，头也疼得厉害。
examples.translation: wǒ fā shāo ké sòu tóu yě téng de lì hài — 2. I had a fever and a cough. My headache was really bad, too.

examples.text: 他每天起得很早。
examples.translation: tā měi tiān qǐ de hěn zǎo — 1. He gets up very early every day.

examples.text: 王老师讲得真好。
examples.translation: wáng lǎo shī jiǎng de zhēn hǎo — 2. Teacher Wang explains really well.

examples.text: 李平学得快，我学得慢。

examples.text: 她回答问题回答得很好。

examples.text: 他说中文说得非常好。

explanations.title: Adjectives with Degree Complements
explanations.body: Degree complements with adjectives follow the basic patterns of degree complements with verbs (Adjective + 得 + degree complement). However, the complements can be adjectives, adverbs or other extents. They are often translated with the pattern “so … that” in English.

examples.text: 他身体好得很。
examples.translation: tā shēn tǐ hǎo de hěn — 1. His health is very good.

examples.text: 我肚子疼得厉害。
examples.translation: wǒ dǔ zi téng de lì hài — 2. My stomach hurts badly.

examples.text: 张华最近忙得要命。
examples.translation: zhāng huá zuì jìn máng de yào mìng — 3. Zhang Hua has been extremely busy lately.

examples.text: 她高兴得跳了起来。
examples.translation: tā gāo xìng de tiào le qǐ lái — 4. She was so happy that she jumped up.

examples.text: 她累得说不出话。
examples.translation: tā lèi de shuō bù chū huà — 5. She was so tired she couldn’t speak.

examples.text: 周末的时候，马克累得不想起床。
examples.translation: zhōu mò de shí hòu mǎ kè lèi de bù xiǎng qǐ chuáng — 6. At the weekend Mark was so tired he didn’t want to get up.

examples.text: 他今天开心得很。
examples.translation: tā jīn tiān kāi xīn de hěn — 7. He is very happy today.

examples.text: 他今天开心得唱起歌来。
examples.translation: tā jīn tiān kāi xīn de chàng qǐ gē lái — 7. He was so happy today that he started singing.

lessons.title: 532. Lesson 21 Presentation 2 grammar: adjectives as predicates (2)
lessons.subtitle: 嗓子疼，口也干 · 很 真 非常 更 有点儿 · 不很 很不 · 学习中文

explanations.title: Adjectives as Predicate (2)
explanations.body: As you learned in a previous lesson, when an adjective is used predicatively in Chinese it does not need a verb-to-be (是) to help it constitute a predicate, as in 今天天气很好. A predicate-adjective sentence describes or evaluates a person or thing. Structurally, a predicate adjective generally appears with some kind of degree adverb. The degree adverbs include 很, 太, 真, 更, 非常, etc.; among them 很 is the most common. Without an adverb, the sentence usually appears in a comparative situation.

rows: 这个房间大，那个房间小
tables.title: Adjectives as predicate (the book’s patterns)

examples.text: 嗓子疼，口也干，头也有点儿晕。
examples.translation: sǎng zi téng kǒu yě gān tóu yě yǒu diǎnr yūn — The book’s first example: I have a sore throat. My mouth is dry too. And I’m a bit dizzy too.

examples.text: 这个房间很大。
examples.translation: zhè ge fáng jiān hěn dà — 1. This room is very big. (很 + adj. = very)

examples.translation: tā sòng wǒ men de huār zhēn hǎo kàn — 2. The flowers he gave us are really pretty. (真 + adj. = really)

examples.text: 你们来看我，我非常高兴。

lessons.title: 533. Lesson 21 Presentation 2 grammar: 多/少, 快/慢, 早/晚 before a verb
lessons.subtitle: 多喝水 · 早来晚走 · 快跑 · 快跑 和 跑得快 的不同

explanations.title: 多/少、快/慢、早/晚 + Verb
explanations.body: In Chinese, the monosyllabic adjectives 多, 少, 快, 慢, 早, 晚 can be placed before a verb to tell how an action should be performed. In such usage the adjectives are called “adverbial adjuncts.” Adverbial adjuncts are usually placed immediately before a verb.

tables.title: Adjectives used as adverbial adjuncts

examples.text: 多喝水。
examples.translation: duō hē shuǐ — Drink more water. (the book’s first example)

examples.text: 明天早上你能早来半个小时吗？
examples.translation: míng tiān zǎo shàng nǐ néng zǎo lái bàn gè xiǎo shí ma — 1. Tomorrow morning, can you come half an hour early?

examples.text: 学习中文，一定要多听、多说、多看、多写。
examples.translation: xué xí zhōng wén yí dìng yào duō tīng duō shuō duō kàn duō xiě — 2. To learn Chinese you must listen more, speak more, read more and write more.

examples.text: 老王工作非常努力，他每天上班，总是早来晚走。
examples.translation: lǎo wáng gōng zuò fēi cháng nǔ lì tā měi tiān shàng bān zǒng shì zǎo lái wǎn zǒu — 3. Lao Wang works very hard; every day he always comes early and leaves late.

examples.text: 还有十分钟就要上课了，我们快跑吧！
examples.translation: hái yǒu shí fēn zhōng jiù yào shàng kè le wǒ men kuài pǎo ba — 4. There are ten minutes until class; let’s run fast!

examples.text: 你血压高，应该少喝酒。
examples.translation: nǐ xuè yā gāo yīng gāi shǎo hē jiǔ — 5. Your blood pressure is high; you should drink less alcohol.

explanations.title: Notes: (ADJ + Verb) vs (Verb 得 + ADJ)
explanations.body: An adjunct adjective tells the desired or factual manner of an action. The function of the adjectival degree complement is to describe the degree of the manner carried out by a completed action or a habitual action. 快 in 快跑 is an adjunct adjective that tells how you are expected to run, and no adverb can be placed before it. 很快 in 跑得很快 forms a degree complement and describes how you run habitually; an adverb is required before the adjective.

examples.text: 你快跑！
examples.translation: nǐ kuài pǎo — 1. (You) run quickly! (快 is an adjunct adjective; no adverb can be placed before it)

examples.text: 你跑得很快。
examples.translation: nǐ pǎo de hěn kuài — 2. You run very fast. (很快 forms a degree complement and needs an adverb)

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Writing, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: The following information is from a medical magazine. A. Pre-reading: guess the meaning of the words 症状, 明显, 发热, 呼吸, 治疗 (supplementary vocabulary). B. Work in groups of three; each student reads one short passage, summarizes it in one sentence and fills in the table. C. Exchange information with your partners. D. Compare the similarities and differences among the three. E. Share your comparison with the class. The three passages:

tables.title: Activity 4A: the supplementary words (the book leaves them blank)

rows: 鼻子堵、流鼻涕、发热、咳嗽、头疼
很少身体酸疼，没有明显发热
轻，多数人不需要看医生
发热、嗓子疼、流鼻涕、全身疼痛、没有力气
咳嗽、高烧，甚至肺炎的症状
比较重，需要服药、休息或看医生
发热，突然发冷，然后高烧
咳嗽越来越厉害、胸痛、呼吸困难、头疼、全身酸疼、食量减少
tables.title: Activity 4B: the three illnesses (the book leaves the table blank; this is my filling)

examples.text: 感冒。症状有鼻子堵、流鼻涕、发热、咳嗽、头疼等。很少出现身体酸疼等全身不舒服的症状，病情比较轻。多数人不需要看医生就可以好。普通感冒通常没有明显发热，如果发热，一般也是中低烧，通常一到三天能正常，服用退烧药就可以。
examples.translation: gǎn mào zhèng zhuàng yǒu bí zi dǔ liú bí tì fā rè ké sòu tóu téng děng hěn shǎo chū xiàn shēn tǐ suān téng děng quán shēn bù shū fú de zhèng zhuàng bìng qíng bǐ jiào qīng duō shù rén bù xū yào kàn yī shēng jiù kě yǐ hǎo pǔ tōng gǎn mào tōng cháng méi yǒu míng xiǎn fā rè rú guǒ fā rè yì bān yě shì zhōng dī shāo tōng cháng yí dào sān tiān néng zhèng cháng fú yòng tuì shāo yào jiù kě yǐ — The common cold. Symptoms are a blocked nose, a runny nose, fever, cough, headache and so on. Aches and pains all over the body are seldom present and the condition is fairly light. Most people recover without seeing a doctor. An ordinary cold usually has no obvious fever; if there is a fever it is generally a medium-low one, usually back to normal in one to three days, and taking fever-reducing medicine is enough. (the book writes 1-3 天; translation mine)

examples.text: 流行性感冒（流感）。症状有发热、嗓子疼、流鼻涕、全身疼痛、没有力气等。部分的病人还会出现咳嗽、高烧，甚至有肺炎的症状。流感的发病特点是起病急、进展快，病人多有明显发热，而且常常是高烧。病人需要服药、在家休息或去看医生。
examples.translation: liú xíng xìng gǎn mào liú gǎn zhèng zhuàng yǒu fā rè sǎng zi téng liú bí tì quán shēn téng tòng méi yǒu lì qì děng bù fèn de bìng rén hái huì chū xiàn ké sòu gāo shāo shèn zhì yǒu fèi yán de zhèng zhuàng liú gǎn de fā bìng tè diǎn shì qǐ bìng jí jìn zhǎn kuài bìng rén duō yǒu míng xiǎn fā rè ér qiě cháng cháng shì gāo shāo bìng rén xū yào fú yào zài jiā xiū xī huò qù kàn yī shēng — Influenza (the flu). Symptoms are fever, sore throat, runny nose, aches all over, lack of strength and so on. Some patients also have a cough, high fever, and even the symptoms of pneumonia. The flu is characterized by a sudden onset and quick progress; patients mostly have an obvious fever, often a high one. Patients need to take medicine, rest at home or see a doctor. (translation mine)

examples.text: 肺炎。主要症状是发热，病人常常突然发冷，然后就是高烧。老年人可以是低烧或者不发热，咳嗽、胸痛。咳嗽会越来越厉害，有时呼吸困难。病人还会出现头疼、全身酸疼，食量减少的症状。得了肺炎的人需要马上去医院检查治疗。
examples.translation: fèi yán zhǔ yào zhèng zhuàng shì fā rè bìng rén cháng cháng tū rán fā lěng rán hòu jiù shì gāo shāo lǎo nián rén kě yǐ shì dī shāo huò zhě bù fā rè ké sòu xiōng tòng ké sòu huì yuè lái yuè lì hài yǒu shí hū xī kùn nán bìng rén hái huì chū xiàn tóu téng quán shēn suān téng shí liàng jiǎn shǎo de zhèng zhuàng dé le fèi yán de rén xū yào mǎ shàng qù yī yuàn jiǎn chá zhì liáo — Pneumonia. The main symptom is fever; patients often suddenly feel cold and then have a high fever. Elderly people may have a low fever or none, with cough and chest pain. The cough gets worse and worse and sometimes breathing is difficult. Patients also have headache, aches all over and reduced appetite. A person with pneumonia needs to go to the hospital at once for examination and treatment. (translation mine)

examples.text: 今天早上起床以后，林强觉得有点儿不舒服。下了课就到校医院去看病。他先挂了一个内科的号，然后就坐在内科门诊室的外面等着。过了一会儿，一个护士出来叫他进去。医生问他哪儿不舒服。林强告诉医生，他嗓子疼得厉害，不但咳嗽，而且口干，鼻子也堵得厉害。医生给他量了体温和血压，还听了听他的心脏。医生说他发高烧，三十九度，所以林强才觉得没有力气，全身都疼。不过，因为他的血压和心跳都还正常，所以医生认为他得的是流感。后来，医生给他开了一些感冒药，还让护士给他打了退烧针。医生告诉他那些感冒药他得吃一个星期，每天三次，一次两片，最好是早中晚各吃一次。另外，医生也让他不要去上课，在家休息，多喝热水。要是嗓子还疼，可以多吃梨。
examples.translation: jīn tiān zǎo shàng qǐ chuáng yǐ hòu lín qiáng jué de yǒu diǎnr bù shū fú xià le kè jiù dào xiào yī yuàn qù kàn bìng tā xiān guà le yí gè nèi kē de hào rán hòu jiù zuò zài nèi kē mén zhěn shì de wài miàn děng zhe guò le yí huìr yí gè hù shì chū lái jiào tā jìn qù yī shēng wèn tā nǎr bù shū fú lín qiáng gào sù yī shēng tā sǎng zi téng de lì hài bú dàn ké sòu ér qiě kǒu gān bí zi yě dǔ de lì hài yī shēng gěi tā liáng le tǐ wēn hé xuè yā hái tīng le tīng tā de xīn zàng yī shēng shuō tā fā gāo shāo sān shí jiǔ dù suǒ yǐ lín qiáng cái jué de méi yǒu lì qì quán shēn dōu téng bú guò yīn wèi tā de xuè yā hé xīn tiào dōu hái zhèng cháng suǒ yǐ yī shēng rèn wéi tā dé de shì liú gǎn hòu lái yī shēng gěi tā kāi le yì xiē gǎn mào yào hái ràng hù shì gěi tā dǎ le tuì shāo zhēn yī shēng gào sù tā nà xiē gǎn mào yào tā děi chī yí gè xīng qī měi tiān sān cì yí cì liǎng piàn zuì hǎo shì zǎo zhōng wǎn gè chī yí cì lìng wài yī shēng yě ràng tā bú yào qù shàng kè zài jiā xiū xī duō hē rè shuǐ yào shì sǎng zi hái téng kě yǐ duō chī lí — This morning after getting up Lin Qiang felt a bit unwell. After class he went to the school hospital to see a doctor. He first registered for internal medicine and then sat outside the internal-medicine consulting room waiting. After a while a nurse came out and called him in. The doctor asked where he felt unwell. Lin Qiang told the doctor that his throat hurt badly, that he not only coughed but his mouth was dry and his nose was badly blocked. The doctor took his temperature and blood pressure and also listened to his heart. The doctor said he had a high fever, 39 degrees, which is why Lin Qiang had no strength and ached all over. However, because his blood pressure and heartbeat were still normal, the doctor thought he had the flu. Then the doctor prescribed some cold medicine and had the nurse give him a fever-reducing injection. The doctor told him he had to take the cold medicine for a week, three times a day, two tablets each time, best once each morning, noon and evening. In addition, the doctor also told him not to go to class, to rest at home and drink plenty of hot water. If his throat still hurt he could eat more pears. (the book writes 三十九度 in characters; translation mine)

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Speaking and Writing)
explanations.body: Scenario: Doctor’s Visit in China. While you are studying at Sichuan University in Chengdu, China, you don’t feel well one day and need to see a doctor at a local hospital. Since it is your first visit and your Chinese is limited, you ask a classmate to help you find information about seeing the doctor, and you prepare a list of questions and other information you will need. A. Pair up; one partner plays the sick friend and the other the helper. Using the link given, both watch a YouTube video posted by an American student who just went to see a doctor in Chengdu and take notes in the table. B. Exchange your information. C. Discuss the differences between seeing a doctor in the U.S. and in China, as noted by the student in the video (中国 | 美国). D. Together create a list of questions and important information in Chinese that you think you will need (要告诉医生的信息 | 要问医生的问题). E. Share your information with the class. (The video is not included.)

headers: 在中国看病 (mine: what to note while watching)
rows: Doctor’s advice, treatment, getting the medicine
tables.title: Activity 1A: the note-taking table (the video is not included; only the scenario facts are filled)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Speaking, Writing and Listening): role-play cards
explanations.body: In this activity you create a role-play scenario between a patient and a doctor during a doctor’s visit. A. Each pair receives a set of role-play cards: Student 1 plays the patient and Student 2 the doctor. B. Study your card and decide what you need to say; you may jot down information or questions in Chinese pinyin or characters on your card. C. When you are ready, begin the role play. Patient card: you are sick and are seeing a doctor in a Chinese hospital; convey the following information appropriately: explain your symptoms; tell the time that you first got sick; explain your medical history; ask questions about checkups; ask about the doctor’s diagnosis; ask questions about treatments; ask about how to take medication(s); ask about anything else you need to pay attention to; ask where to get your medication or treatments; additional questions you may have. Doctor card: you are talking to your new patient and trying to figure out what their illness is; convey the following information, providing treatment and advice: ask about the patient’s conditions and symptoms; ask when the patient got sick; ask for the patient’s medical history; explain what checkups you will conduct; explain your diagnosis; explain treatment plans; tell the patient how to take his or her medicine(s); offer other advice for recovery; answer any additional questions the patient may ask.

lessons.title: 538. Lesson 21 Presentation 3: a night in the emergency room
lessons.subtitle: 肚子疼 恶心 呕吐 · 叫出租车 · 急诊室 · 验血 验尿 透视 · 急性肠胃炎 · 住院 输液

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss: A. Have you ever been to an emergency room (ER)? Why did you need to go? B. Do you have any friends or relatives who have been to the ER? What happened to them? C. What treatment or examinations did you receive on your last doctor’s visit? (Four small pictures, not included.)

explanations.title: Presentation 3: 急诊室
explanations.body: The passage is in four paragraphs; the book also prints it in traditional characters. The translations are mine.

examples.text: 星期二晚上大约九点左右，我觉得肚子疼，还有点恶心。过了半个小时以后，又开始呕吐，拉肚子。差不多半夜十二点我又发起烧来，而且腹痛、腹泻也越来越厉害。我的室友张林和王明赶紧叫了一辆出租车，把我送到了医院的急诊室。
examples.translation: xīng qī èr wǎn shàng dà yuē jiǔ diǎn zuǒ yòu wǒ jué de dǔ zi téng hái yǒu diǎn ě xīn guò le bàn gè xiǎo shí yǐ hòu yòu kāi shǐ ǒu tù lā dù zi chà bu duō bàn yè shí èr diǎn wǒ yòu fā qǐ shāo lái ér qiě fù tòng fù xiè yě yuè lái yuè lì hài wǒ de shì yǒu zhāng lín hé wáng míng gǎn jǐn jiào le yí liàng chū zū chē bǎ wǒ sòng dào le yī yuàn de jí zhěn shì — On Tuesday evening at about nine o’clock I felt a pain in my stomach and a bit of nausea. Half an hour later I began vomiting and had diarrhea. At about midnight I started running a fever again, and the stomach pain and diarrhea grew worse and worse. My roommates Zhang Lin and Wang Ming hurriedly called a taxi and took me to the hospital emergency room. (translation mine)

examples.text: 那天晚上看急诊的病人还真不少，我们等了半个小时，医生才给我检查。他先让我验血、验尿，还给我做了一个透视，最后确诊为急性肠胃炎。医生说我的病情很严重，得住院治疗。当天夜里我就在病房里接受治疗，护士给我输了液，还给我吃了药。
examples.translation: nà tiān wǎn shàng kàn jí zhěn de bìng rén hái zhēn bù shǎo wǒ men děng le bàn gè xiǎo shí yī shēng cái gěi wǒ jiǎn chá tā xiān ràng wǒ yàn xiě yàn niào hái gěi wǒ zuò le yí gè tòu shì zuì hòu què zhěn wèi jí xìng cháng wèi yán yī shēng shuō wǒ de bìng qíng hěn yán zhòng děi zhù yuàn zhì liáo dàng tiān yè lǐ wǒ jiù zài bìng fáng lǐ jiē shòu zhì liáo hù shì gěi wǒ shū le yè hái gěi wǒ chī le yào — There really were quite a few patients in the emergency room that night; we waited half an hour before the doctor examined me. He first had me do a blood test and a urine test and also gave me an X-ray, and finally confirmed acute gastroenteritis. The doctor said my condition was serious and I had to be hospitalized for treatment. That very night I received treatment in the ward; the nurse gave me an infusion and also gave me medicine. (translation mine)

examples.text: 医生让我住三天院，所以星期三早上张林帮我跟老师请了病假。老师让我不要着急，安心地在医院治疗。
examples.translation: yī shēng ràng wǒ zhù sān tiān yuàn suǒ yǐ xīng qī sān zǎo shàng zhāng lín bāng wǒ gēn lǎo shī qǐng le bìng jià lǎo shī ràng wǒ bú yào zháo jí ān xīn de zài yī yuàn zhì liáo — The doctor had me stay in hospital for three days, so on Wednesday morning Zhang Lin asked the teacher for sick leave for me. The teacher told me not to worry and to keep my mind at ease while being treated in the hospital. (translation mine)

examples.text: 三天后，我出了院，又在宿舍休息了两天，现在感觉好多了。医生说这次我生病是因为吃了不干净的东西，让我以后一定多加小心。这次多亏了室友们及时地把我送到了医院，我从心里感谢他们。下个星期我就可以回去上课了。
examples.translation: sān tiān hòu wǒ chū le yuàn yòu zài sù shè xiū xī le liǎng tiān xiàn zài gǎn jué hǎo duō le yī shēng shuō zhè cì wǒ shēng bìng shì yīn wèi chī le bù gān jìng de dōng xī ràng wǒ yǐ hòu yí dìng duō jiā xiǎo xīn zhè cì duō kuī le shì yǒu men jí shí de bǎ wǒ sòng dào le yī yuàn wǒ cóng xīn lǐ gǎn xiè tā men xià gè xīng qī wǒ jiù kě yǐ huí qù shàng kè le — Three days later I left the hospital and rested another two days in the dorm, and now I feel much better. The doctor said I fell ill this time because I ate something unclean, and told me to be especially careful from now on. This time, thanks to my roommates’ timely taking me to the hospital, I thank them from my heart. Next week I can go back to class. (translation mine)

lessons.title: 540. Lesson 21 Presentation 3 grammar: the compound directional complement 起来
lessons.subtitle: 发起烧来 · 热起来了 · 唱起歌来 · 开始 和 继续

explanations.title: Compound Directional Complement 起来
explanations.body: In Chinese, 起来 can be used both as a directional complement and as a resultative complement. As a directional complement it is similar to “up” in English, used literally as in “stand up”; as a resultative complement it often means “to start doing something” (traceable back to its directional meaning, “an upward action”). When 起来 shows that an action or state has begun and is ongoing, it is often used after a verb or an adjective, with 了 at the end of the sentence. The verbs are usually spontaneous actions like 唱, 跳, 聊, or states like 热, 冷, 好; 起来 cannot be used with planned actions. When 起来 is used with a verb that has an object, the V + 起 + O + 来 structure is often used, meaning “to start doing something”; such verb-object phrases include 唱歌, 跳舞, 吃饭, 发烧, 看书 etc.

headers: Action/state has begun and is ongoing
rows: V + 起 + O + 来 + 了
tables.title: The compound directional complement 起来

examples.text: 差不多半夜十二点我又发起烧来。
examples.translation: chà bu duō bàn yè shí èr diǎn wǒ yòu fā qǐ shāo lái — The book’s first example: Then I started having a fever around midnight.

examples.text: 小鸟飞起来了。
examples.translation: xiǎo niǎo fēi qǐ lái le — 1. The bird flew up.

examples.text: 大家都笑起来了。
examples.translation: dà jiā dōu xiào qǐ lái le — 2. Everyone started laughing.

examples.text: 天气热起来了。
examples.translation: tiān qì rè qǐ lái le — 3. The weather is getting hot.

examples.text: 因为很长时间没锻炼，他胖起来了。
examples.translation: yīn wèi hěn cháng shí jiān méi duàn liàn tā pàng qǐ lái le — 4. Because he hasn’t exercised for a long time, he is getting fat.

examples.text: 刚才还好好的，怎么现在下起雨来了？
examples.translation: gāng cái hái hǎo hǎo de zěn me xiàn zài xià qǐ yǔ lái le — 5. It was fine just now; how come it has started to rain?

examples.text: 烧烤以后，同学们在草地上跳起舞来。
examples.translation: shāo kǎo yǐ hòu tóng xué men zài cǎo dì shàng tiào qǐ wǔ lái — 6. After the barbecue the students started dancing on the grass.

examples.text: 半个小时以前，我拉起肚子来。
examples.translation: bàn gè xiǎo shí yǐ qián wǒ lā qǐ dǔ zi lái — 7. Half an hour ago I started having diarrhea.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. Pair up. Study the two word lists and take turns selecting one word from each list to create sentences with “Verb/Adjective + 起来 + 了” or “Verb + 起 + Object + 来”. List 1: 流鼻涕, 量血压, 发烧, 嗓子疼, 鼻子堵, 头晕, 量体温, 喝水, 吃药, 高兴, 兴奋, 紧张. List 2: 输液, 刮风, 下雪, 打, 跳, 站, 唱歌, 工作, 聊天, 哭, 热, 冷. B. Share your sentences with the class. My sentences:

examples.text: 我的鼻子堵起来了。
examples.translation: wǒ de bí zi dǔ qǐ lái le — My nose has started to get blocked. (Activity 1A, mine: 鼻子堵)

examples.text: 听到这个消息，大家都兴奋起来了。
examples.translation: tīng dào zhè ge xiāo xī dà jiā dōu xīng fèn qǐ lái le — Hearing this news everybody got excited. (兴奋, mine)

examples.text: 看到老师，他有点紧张起来了。
examples.translation: kàn dào lǎo shī tā yǒu diǎn jǐn zhāng qǐ lái le — Seeing the teacher, he began to get a bit nervous. (紧张, mine)

examples.text: 刚说了几句，他们就聊起天来了。
examples.translation: gāng shuō le jǐ jù tā men jiù liáo qǐ tiān lái le — After just a few sentences they started chatting. (聊天, mine)

examples.text: 天气冷起来了，快下雪了。
examples.translation: tiān qì lěng qǐ lái le kuài xià xuě le — It’s getting cold and it’s about to snow. (冷, mine)

examples.text: 一到周末，他就唱起歌来。
examples.translation: yí dào zhōu mò tā jiù chàng qǐ gē lái — As soon as the weekend comes he starts singing. (唱歌, mine)

explanations.title: Activity 2 and Activity 3
explanations.body: Activity 2 (Listening and Speaking): A. Listen to six sentences and translate what you hear. B. Share your answers and read the scripts. (Audio, not included.) Activity 3 (Writing, Speaking and Listening): in this activity you describe your activities at an event you attended recently, using “起来 + 了” or “V + 起 + O + 来”. A. Write your story with at least four to six sentences. B. Pair up and exchange. C. Retell your partner’s story to the class. My sample:

examples.text: 上个星期六我们去参加了一个烧烤晚会。一到公园，大家就聊起天来了。过了一会儿，天气热起来了，我们都喝起水来。晚饭以后，有人唱起歌来，有人跳起舞来，大家都高兴起来了。
examples.translation: shàng gè xīng qī liù wǒ men qù cān jiā le yí gè shāo kǎo wǎn huì yí dào gōng yuán dà jiā jiù liáo qǐ tiān lái le guò le yí huìr tiān qì rè qǐ lái le wǒ men dōu hē qǐ shuǐ lái wǎn fàn yǐ hòu yǒu rén chàng qǐ gē lái yǒu rén tiào qǐ wǔ lái dà jiā dōu gāo xìng qǐ lái le — Last Saturday we went to a barbecue party. As soon as we reached the park everybody started chatting. After a while the weather got hot and we all started drinking water. After dinner some people started singing and some started dancing, and everyone cheered up. (Activity 3, my sample story)

lessons.title: 541. Lesson 21 Presentation 3 grammar: the 把 construction with a locative complement
lessons.subtitle: 把我送到了急诊室 · 把…放在 · 把…搬到 · 把和没有把

explanations.title: 把-Construction with Locative Complement
explanations.body: In a previous lesson you learned the Chinese 把 construction. The two major conditions for using it are (1) the definiteness of the object noun phrase and (2) the complexity of the verb phrase. The 把 construction is compulsory when the verb is followed by a locative complement, indicating placement or relocation of a thing or a person as a result of the action. A locative complement is made up of 在 or 到, followed by a place word. When a disposal verb takes both an object and a locative complement, the object must be placed after 把 and before the verb, leaving the verb and the complement to form one closed verbal unit. The locative complement tells where the object is moved via the disposal verb.

rows: 把 + Object + Verb + 在 or 到 + Place
tables.title: The 把 construction with a locative complement

examples.text: 我的室友张林和王明赶紧叫了一辆出租车，把我送到了医院的急诊室。
examples.translation: wǒ de shì yǒu zhāng lín hé wáng míng gǎn jǐn jiào le yí liàng chū zū chē bǎ wǒ sòng dào le yī yuàn de jí zhěn shì — The book’s first example: My roommates Zhang Lin and Wang Ming called a cab in a hurry and sent me to the hospital emergency room.

examples.text: 我把那些树种在院子里了。
examples.translation: wǒ bǎ nà xiē shù zhòng zài yuàn zi lǐ le — 1. I planted those trees in the yard.

examples.text: 你把自行车放在哪儿了？
examples.translation: nǐ bǎ zì xíng chē fàng zài nǎr le — 2. Where did you put the bicycle?

examples.text: 她把老师说的话都写在笔记本上了。
examples.translation: tā bǎ lǎo shī shuō de huà dōu xiě zài bǐ jì běn shàng le — 3. She wrote down everything the teacher said in her notebook.

examples.text: 我们快把这个病人送到医院去吧。
examples.translation: wǒ men kuài bǎ zhè ge bìng rén sòng dào yī yuàn qù ba — 4. Let’s quickly take this patient to the hospital.

examples.text: 我已经把椅子搬到楼上去了。
examples.translation: wǒ yǐ jīng bǎ yǐ zi bān dào lóu shàng qù le — 5. I have already moved the chair upstairs.

examples.text: 飞机是八点半起飞的。我七点十分开车把他们送到了机场。
examples.translation: fēi jī shì bā diǎn bàn qǐ fēi de wǒ qī diǎn shí fēn kāi chē bǎ tā men sòng dào le jī chǎng — 6. The plane took off at half past eight. At ten past seven I drove them to the airport.

explanations.title: 把-Construction with a Locative Complement vs. a Sentence Without the 把 Construction
explanations.body: The first sentence below tells what the speaker did with the trees; the second describes what the speaker did in the yard.

examples.text: 我把那些树种在院子里了。
examples.translation: wǒ bǎ nà xiē shù zhòng zài yuàn zi lǐ le — This tells what the speaker did with the trees, namely planting them in the backyard: I have planted those trees in the yard.

examples.text: 我在院子里种了一些树。
examples.translation: wǒ zài yuàn zi lǐ zhòng le yì xiē shù — This describes what the speaker did in the yard: I have planted some trees in the yard.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. Pair up and complete the following sentences using the 把 construction with a locative complement. B. Share your answers. The book prints the five questions (A) and leaves B blank; my answers:

examples.text: 甲：老师把我的作业放到哪儿了？
examples.translation: jiǎ lǎo shī bǎ wǒ de zuò yè fàng dào nǎr le — 2. Where did the teacher put my homework?

examples.text: 乙：老师把你的作业放到桌子上了。
examples.translation: yǐ lǎo shī bǎ nǐ de zuò yè fàng dào zhuō zi shàng le — The teacher put your homework on the desk. (mine)

examples.text: 甲：你把你的军服送到哪儿去洗了？
examples.translation: jiǎ nǐ bǎ nǐ de jūn fú sòng dào nǎr qù xǐ le — 3. Where did you send your uniform to be washed?

examples.text: 甲：今年你家人朋友给你生日礼物了吗？他们要把礼物寄到这里了吗？

examples.text: 乙：给了，他们把礼物寄到学校来了。
examples.translation: yǐ gěi le tā men bǎ lǐ wù jì dào xué xiào lái le — Yes, they sent the gifts to the school. (mine)

explanations.title: Activity 5 and Activity 6
explanations.body: Activity 5 (Listening and Speaking): A. Listen to the dialog and answer: 1. What is the relationship between the two speakers? 2. What happened to the male speaker’s wallet? 3. What did he learn about his wallet? 4. What is the female speaker’s plan for tomorrow? 5. What kind of person do you think the male speaker is? 6. What kind of person is the female speaker? 7. What did the male speaker promise the female speaker? B. Share your answers and read the script with the class. (Audio, not included.) Activity 6 (Speaking, Listening and Writing): A. Pair up and take turns asking your partner to move an object in the classroom for you, using the 把 construction with a locative complement; your partner completes the action. B. lessons.title: 542. Lesson 21 Presentation 3 grammar: the negative imperative 不要, and negative modals
lessons.subtitle: 不要着急 · 不要说话了 · 不想 不能 不会 不用 不可以 不应该 不要 · 老外在中国不要做的九件事

explanations.title: Negative Imperative 不要
explanations.body: In Chinese, 不要 is a variant form of 别. It is used as a negative imperative to express a demand or command to refrain from doing something, like the English “Don’t do something.” 不要 and 别 may be used interchangeably; 别 can be seen as the short, informal form of 不要. Just like 别, 不要 appears before a verb, and the subject is usually omitted, as in English. You can also use 了 at the end of a sentence with 不要, which means to stop doing something.

tables.title: Negative imperative 不要

examples.text: 老师让我不要着急，安心地在医院治疗。
examples.translation: lǎo shī ràng wǒ bú yào zháo jí ān xīn de zài yī yuàn zhì liáo — The book’s first example: My teacher told me not to worry and keep my mind on the treatment in the hospital.

examples.text: 不要走。
examples.translation: bú yào zǒu — 1. Don’t go.

examples.text: 不要打我。
examples.translation: bú yào dǎ wǒ — 2. Don’t hit me.

examples.text: 你晚上不要开车。
examples.translation: nǐ wǎn shàng bú yào kāi chē — 3. Don’t drive at night.

examples.text: 请不要离开我。
examples.translation: qǐng bú yào lí kāi wǒ — 4. Please don’t leave me.

examples.text: 请不要忘了关门。
examples.translation: qǐng bú yào wàng le guān mén — 5. Please don’t forget to close the door.

examples.text: 上课的时候，不要玩手机。
examples.translation: shàng kè de shí hòu bú yào wán shǒu jī — 6. Don’t play with your phone during class.

examples.text: 不要说话了，现在开始上课。
examples.translation: bú yào shuō huà le xiàn zài kāi shǐ shàng kè — 7. Stop talking; class is starting now.

examples.text: 不要再吃了，你都吃了三碗米饭了。
examples.translation: bú yào zài chī le nǐ dōu chī le sān wǎn mǐ fàn le — 8. Stop eating; you have already had three bowls of rice.

Don’t move. 4. Stop talking. 5. Stop sleeping. 6. Stop laughing. 7. Stop horsing around. Write your answers and share your work with the class. Mine:

explanations.title: Activity 8 (Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. Complete the sentences with the correct word from the list 不想 | 不能 | 不会 | 不用 | 不可以 | 不应该 | 不要. B. Pair up; share your answers and explain your choices. C. Study and compare the words and their meanings in the table. The book prints the seven sentences with blanks and no key; each word fits once, and my key:

tables.title: Activity 8C: the table of modals and their negatives (the book’s table)

examples.text: 我不会游泳，你能教我吗？
examples.translation: wǒ bú huì yóu yǒng nǐ néng jiāo wǒ ma — 1. 不会. I can’t swim; can you teach me? (key mine)

examples.text: 我明天要上班，不能跟你们一起去旧金山。
examples.translation: wǒ míng tiān yào shàng bān bù néng gēn nǐ men yì qǐ qù jiù jīn shān — 2. 不能. I have to work tomorrow, so I can’t go to San Francisco with you.

examples.text: 老师说，明天不用上课，因为是军事训练日。
examples.translation: lǎo shī shuō míng tiān bú yòng shàng kè yīn wèi shì jūn shì xùn liàn rì — 4. 不用. The teacher said there’s no need to go to class tomorrow because it’s a military training day.

examples.text: 我不想去看电影，我想在家休息。
examples.translation: wǒ bù xiǎng qù kàn diàn yǐng wǒ xiǎng zài jiā xiū xī — 5. 不想. I don’t want to go to a movie; I want to rest at home.

examples.text: 你身体不好，真不应该喝那么多酒。

explanations.title: Activity 9 (Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: The following article is from Chinadaily.com (adapted from world.chinadaily.com.cn): 老外在中国不要做的9件事 (nine things foreigners shouldn’t do in China). A. Scan the title and guess who should pay attention to it and what you expect to read about (看题目，猜大意). B. Work in groups of three; each student reads three items and shares the information with the group. C. Why do you think each tip is given? The nine items:

examples.text: 不要在公共场合发脾气。
examples.translation: bú yào zài gōng gòng chǎng hé fā pí qì — 1. Don’t lose your temper in public.

examples.text: 不要随便接受表扬。
examples.translation: bú yào suí biàn jiē shòu biǎo yáng — 2. Don’t accept praise casually. (the book glosses 表扬 as praise)

examples.text: 不要一开始就用中国人的名字叫他们。
examples.translation: bú yào yì kāi shǐ jiù yòng zhōng guó rén de míng zì jiào tā men — 3. Don’t call Chinese people by their first names right from the start. (the book prints 名叫, which I read as 名字叫)

examples.text: 不要让中国人丢脸。
examples.translation: bú yào ràng zhōng guó rén diū liǎn — 4. Don’t make Chinese people lose face.

examples.text: 不要等着别人买单。
examples.translation: bú yào děng zhe bié rén mǎi dān — 5. Don’t wait for others to pay the bill.

examples.text: 不要空手去朋友家。
examples.translation: bú yào kōng shǒu qù péng yǒu jiā — 6. Don’t go to a friend’s home empty-handed.

examples.text: 不要把中国人客气的时候说的“不，谢谢”当真。
examples.translation: bú yào bǎ zhōng guó rén kè qì de shí hòu shuō de bú xiè xiè dàng zhēn — 7. Don’t take the “No, thank you” that Chinese people say out of politeness seriously.

examples.text: 不要马上接受别人给的食物、饮料或礼物。
examples.translation: bú yào mǎ shàng jiē shòu bié rén gěi de shí wù yǐn liào huò lǐ wù — 8. Don’t accept food, drinks or gifts that others offer immediately.

examples.text: 不要在祝酒前喝酒。
examples.translation: bú yào zài zhù jiǔ qián hē jiǔ — 9. Don’t drink before the toast.

exercises.prompt: What is 不要 compared with 别?
exercises.explanation: 别 is the short, informal form.

exercises.prompt: What does 不要 + verb + 了 mean?
Which blank takes 不会: “我___游泳，你能教我吗？”
Which blank takes 不能: “我明天要上班，___跟你们一起去旧金山”?
Which blank takes 不用: “老师说，明天___上课，因为是军事训练日”?
Which blank takes 不应该: “你身体不好，真___喝那么多酒”?
Which blank takes 不想: “我___去看电影，我想在家休息”?
What does 不要空手去朋友家 advise?

不要再吃了，你都吃了三碗___饭了。

lessons.title: 543. Lesson 21 Presentation 3 skill integration: 120, sick-leave notes and a back injury
lessons.subtitle: 120 · 病假条 · 请假 批准 · 伤到后背 · 幸亏你来得早

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Writing, Speaking and Reading)
explanations.body: A. Listen to three dialogs once and answer: 1. What is 120? 2. When should people call this number? B. Listen again and complete the table (Dialog 1–3: who called 120 and the patient’s relation; the patient’s symptoms). C. Work in groups of three and share. D. Discuss: 1. What number should people call in the U.S. when they have an emergency? 2. Who is part of an emergency team in the U.S.? E. Share your answers and read the scripts. (Audio, not included; 120 is the emergency number for ambulances in China, as the scenario later in the lesson shows.)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Listening, Writing, Speaking and Reading)
explanations.body: A. Listen to a voicemail and mark the statements True or False; pair up, share and explain your reasoning: 1. 小雨给妈妈打电话留言。 2. 小雨今天不能回家因为她病了。 3. 小雨和室友叫了一辆出租车去医院急诊室。 4. 小雨在医院呆了一个晚上，她的室友文文回宿舍了。 5. 老师下午会到医院看小雨和王玲。 6. 小雨这个周末不能回家，她得等出院以后才能回家。 B. Listen again and complete the table (who was sent to the emergency room; when; how; symptoms; details about the emergency room; examinations; diagnosis; treatment; what the speaker and her roommate did for the patient; other details). C. Form a group of three and exchange. D. Read the script and compare. (Audio, not included; the book prints no key.)

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading, Speaking, Listening and Writing)
explanations.body: Read the notes from three students and complete the tasks. A. Pre-reading: guess the meaning of the words 病假, 病假条, 便条, 事假（条）, 批准. B. Work in groups of three; each student reads one note, determines what it is about and what is being requested, and writes the answers in the table. C. Exchange your information. D. Each student writes a sick-leave note or a leave note in Chinese and posts it on linoit.com, including reasons and requests. E. Share your note with the class. The three notes (the book prints the dates in digits):

tables.title: Activity 3A: the supplementary words (the book leaves the pinyin and English blank)

rows: 这两天睡得不好，头晕，头疼得特别厉害；要去看医生
孩子发高烧三十九度，咳嗽得很厉害；要带孩子去看病
呕吐、腹痛、发烧，被送进急诊室，得了急性肠胃炎，要住三天院
tables.title: Activity 3B: what each note is about (the book leaves the table blank; this is my filling)

examples.text: 杨老师：您好！我是大卫。今天早上九点十五分我得去看医生，因为这两天我睡得不好，而且头晕、头疼得特别厉害。特向您请假一个半小时（九点十五分至十点十五分），希望您能够批准。谢谢！您的学生：王大卫　二零二零年四月二十八日
examples.translation: yáng lǎo shī nín hǎo wǒ shì dà wèi jīn tiān zǎo shàng jiǔ diǎn shí wǔ fēn wǒ děi qù kàn yī shēng yīn wèi zhè liǎng tiān wǒ shuì de bù hǎo ér qiě tóu yūn tóu téng de tè bié lì hài tè xiàng nín qǐng jià yí gè bàn xiǎo shí jiǔ diǎn shí wǔ fēn zhì shí diǎn shí wǔ fēn xī wàng nín néng gòu pī zhǔn xiè xiè nín de xué shēng wáng dà wèi èr líng èr líng nián sì yuè èr shí bā rì — Teacher Yang: Hello! I am David. This morning at 9:15 I have to see a doctor, because for the past two days I haven’t slept well and I have been dizzy and had a very bad headache. I am asking you for one and a half hours’ leave (9:15 to 10:15) and hope you can approve it. Thank you! Your student: Wang David, April 28, 2020. (a sick-leave note, 病假条; the book writes the times and date in digits)

examples.text: 王老师：您好！刚刚我的太太打来电话，说我的孩子病了，发高烧三十九度，而且咳嗽得非常厉害。需要我回家带孩子去看病，所以今天下午的课我不能上了。特请半天假，希望您能够批准。谢谢！学生：马克　二零二零年五月六日
examples.translation: wáng lǎo shī nín hǎo gāng gāng wǒ de tài tài dǎ lái diàn huà shuō wǒ de hái zi bìng le fā gāo shāo sān shí jiǔ dù ér qiě ké sòu de fēi cháng lì hài xū yào wǒ huí jiā dài hái zi qù kàn bìng suǒ yǐ jīn tiān xià wǔ de kè wǒ bù néng shàng le tè qǐng bàn tiān jià xī wàng nín néng gòu pī zhǔn xiè xiè xué shēng mǎ kè èr líng èr líng nián wǔ yuè liù rì — Teacher Wang: Hello! My wife just phoned to say that my child is ill, with a high fever of 39 degrees and a very bad cough. I need to go home and take the child to see a doctor, so I can’t attend this afternoon’s class. I am asking for half a day’s leave and hope you can approve it. Thank you! Student: Mark, May 6, 2020. (a sick-leave note; the book writes the date in digits)

examples.text: 张老师：您好！昨天晚上十点我因为呕吐、腹痛和发烧，被送进了医院的急诊室。医生说我得了急性肠胃炎，需要住三天院，所以这几天不能到校上课。特向您请三天假（周二至周四），希望您能够批准。谢谢！（假条和医生证明请王兰带给您）您的学生：琳达　二零二零年六月八日
examples.translation: zhāng lǎo shī nín hǎo zuó tiān wǎn shàng shí diǎn wǒ yīn wèi ǒu tù fù tòng hé fā shāo bèi sòng jìn le yī yuàn de jí zhěn shì yī shēng shuō wǒ dé le jí xìng cháng wèi yán xū yào zhù sān tiān yuàn suǒ yǐ zhè jǐ tiān bù néng dào xiào shàng kè tè xiàng nín qǐng sān tiān jià zhōu èr zhì zhōu sì xī wàng nín néng gòu pī zhǔn xiè xiè jià tiáo hé yī shēng zhèng míng qǐng wáng lán dài gěi nín nín de xué shēng lín dá èr líng èr líng nián liù yuè bā rì — Teacher Zhang: Hello! Last night at ten I was taken to the hospital emergency room because of vomiting, stomach pain and fever. The doctor said I have acute gastroenteritis and need to stay in hospital for three days, so I cannot come to school these days. I am asking you for three days’ leave (Tuesday to Thursday) and hope you can approve it. Thank you! (Please ask Wang Lan to bring you the note and the doctor’s certificate.) Your student: Linda, June 8, 2020. (the book writes the date in digits)

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: Read the following passage about a student’s ER experience and complete the tasks. A. Pair up. Each student receives two slips from the teacher, reads two parts of the passage, writes a summary of each part and exchanges the information with the partner. B. Together, order the paragraphs ①–④ into a logical story and share it with the class (Correct Order: _ → _ → _ → _). My order: ③ → ① → ④ → ② (③ the injury and the trip to the ER, ① the ER treatment, ④ leaving with medicine and a note, ② three days at home). C. Translate three sentences from the passage (sample translations below). D. Share your translation with the class. Student 1’s and Student 2’s slips:

examples.text: ① 那天我们到急诊室的时候，因为是早上只有一两个病人，所以很快就有一个女医生过来问我的病情。她先给我量了量血压，听了一下心脏，然后又给我做了一个透视，拍了Ｘ光。等拍的片子出来后，医生告诉我幸亏没有伤到骨头，所以不需要住院治疗，但是得打针、输液治疗。医生先让护士给我打了止痛针，很快我的疼痛开始慢慢减轻。然后护士又给我输液，输了大概两个小时。② 我在家躺了三天，不能坐和走，只能躺着，到了第四天才能站起来。以后锻炼的时候，我一定得多加小心，不能再受伤了。
examples.translation: nà tiān wǒ men dào jí zhěn shì de shí hòu yīn wèi shì zǎo shàng zhǐ yǒu yì liǎng gè bìng rén suǒ yǐ hěn kuài jiù yǒu yí gè nǚ yī shēng guò lái wèn wǒ de bìng qíng tā xiān gěi wǒ liáng le liáng xuè yā tīng le yí xià xīn zàng rán hòu yòu gěi wǒ zuò le yí gè tòu shì pāi le guāng děng pāi de piān zi chū lái hòu yī shēng gào sù wǒ xìng kuī méi yǒu shāng dào gǔ tou suǒ yǐ bù xū yào zhù yuàn zhì liáo dàn shì děi dǎ zhēn shū yè zhì liáo yī shēng xiān ràng hù shì gěi wǒ dǎ le zhǐ tòng zhēn hěn kuài wǒ de téng tòng kāi shǐ màn màn jiǎn qīng rán hòu hù shì yòu gěi wǒ shū yè shū le dà gài liǎng gè xiǎo shí wǒ zài jiā tǎng le sān tiān bù néng zuò hé zǒu zhǐ néng tǎng zhe dào le dì sì tiān cái néng zhàn qǐ lái yǐ hòu duàn liàn de shí hòu wǒ yí dìng děi duō jiā xiǎo xīn bù néng zài shòu shāng le — ① When we got to the emergency room that day, because it was morning and there were only one or two patients, a woman doctor soon came over to ask about my condition. She first measured my blood pressure and listened to my heart, then gave me an X-ray and took an X-ray picture (the book writes “X 光”; I wrote the letter in full-width form). When the picture came out the doctor told me that luckily the bone wasn’t injured, so no hospitalization was needed, but I had to have an injection and an infusion. The doctor first had the nurse give me a painkiller injection, and soon my pain slowly eased. Then the nurse gave me an infusion for about two hours. ② I lay at home for three days, unable to sit or walk, only lie; only on the fourth day could I stand up. When I exercise in the future I must be extra careful and not get hurt again. (Student 1’s two slips; translation mine)

examples.text: ③ 上个星期一在体育馆锻炼的时候，我不小心伤到了后背，休息了几天。后来有一点好转，所以我就试着举起双手，突然后背又疼起来，而且疼痛越来越严重，最后不得不请我的同学送我去了医院的急诊室。④ 离开急诊室以前，医生给我开了两种止痛药，告诉我回家以后一定要按时吃药。最后，医生又给我开了一张医生证明，让我这个星期不要着急去上课，跟老师请几天假，就在家安心养病，多休息，少动。
examples.translation: shàng gè xīng qī yī zài tǐ yù guǎn duàn liàn de shí hòu wǒ bù xiǎo xīn shāng dào le hòu bèi xiū xī le jǐ tiān hòu lái yǒu yì diǎn hǎo zhuǎn suǒ yǐ wǒ jiù shì zhe jǔ qǐ shuāng shǒu tū rán hòu bèi yòu téng qǐ lái ér qiě téng tòng yuè lái yuè yán zhòng zuì hòu bù dé bù qǐng wǒ de tóng xué sòng wǒ qù le yī yuàn de jí zhěn shì lí kāi jí zhěn shì yǐ qián yī shēng gěi wǒ kāi le liǎng zhǒng zhǐ tòng yào gào sù wǒ huí jiā yǐ hòu yí dìng yào àn shí chī yào zuì hòu yī shēng yòu gěi wǒ kāi le yì zhāng yī shēng zhèng míng ràng wǒ zhè ge xīng qī bú yào zháo jí qù shàng kè gēn lǎo shī qǐng jǐ tiān jià jiù zài jiā ān xīn yǎng bìng duō xiū xī shǎo dòng — ③ Last Monday while exercising in the gym I carelessly injured my back and rested a few days. Later it got a little better, so I tried to raise both hands, and suddenly my back hurt again, and the pain got worse and worse; finally I had no choice but to ask my classmate to take me to the hospital emergency room. ④ Before leaving the emergency room the doctor prescribed two kinds of painkillers and told me I must take them on time after getting home. Finally the doctor also gave me a doctor’s certificate and told me not to hurry to class this week, to ask the teacher for a few days’ leave, to recuperate at home with peace of mind, to rest more and move less. (Student 2’s two slips; translation mine)

examples.text: 后来有一点好转，所以我就试着举起双手，突然后背又疼起来，而且疼痛越来越严重，最后不得不请我的同学送我去了医院的急诊室。
examples.translation: hòu lái yǒu yì diǎn hǎo zhuǎn suǒ yǐ wǒ jiù shì zhe jǔ qǐ shuāng shǒu tū rán hòu bèi yòu téng qǐ lái ér qiě téng tòng yuè lái yuè yán zhòng zuì hòu bù dé bù qǐng wǒ de tóng xué sòng wǒ qù le yī yuàn de jí zhěn shì — 1. Later it got a little better, so I tried to raise both hands, and suddenly my back hurt again, and the pain got worse and worse; finally I had no choice but to ask my classmate to take me to the hospital emergency room. (translation mine)

examples.text: 等拍的片子出来后，医生告诉我幸亏没有伤到骨头，所以不需要住院治疗，但是得打针、输液治疗。
examples.translation: děng pāi de piān zi chū lái hòu yī shēng gào sù wǒ xìng kuī méi yǒu shāng dào gǔ tou suǒ yǐ bù xū yào zhù yuàn zhì liáo dàn shì děi dǎ zhēn shū yè zhì liáo — 2. When the picture came out the doctor told me that luckily the bone wasn’t injured, so no hospitalization was needed, but I had to have an injection and an infusion. (mine)

examples.text: 最后，医生又给我开了一张医生证明，让我这个星期不要去上课了，跟老师请几天假，就在家安心养病，多休息，少动。
examples.translation: zuì hòu yī shēng yòu gěi wǒ kāi le yì zhāng yī shēng zhèng míng ràng wǒ zhè ge xīng qī bú yào qù shàng kè le gēn lǎo shī qǐng jǐ tiān jià jiù zài jiā ān xīn yǎng bìng duō xiū xī shǎo dòng — 3. Finally the doctor gave me a doctor’s certificate and told me not to go to class this week, to ask the teacher for a few days’ leave, to recuperate at home with peace of mind, and to rest more and move less. (mine)

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Read the following dialog (a joke about a hospital) and answer the question: Why was the patient scared, initially? What did the doctor really mean?

examples.text: 去医院检查后，医生拿着我的报告单说：“幸亏你来得早……”我吓出了一身冷汗，以为自己得了什么重病，结果医生慢慢地说：“再晚点，我就下班了。”
examples.translation: qù yī yuàn jiǎn chá hòu yī shēng ná zhe wǒ de bào gào dān shuō xìng kuī nǐ lái de zǎo wǒ xià chū le yì shēn lěng hàn yǐ wéi zì jǐ dé le shén me zhòng bìng jié guǒ yī shēng màn màn de shuō zài wǎn diǎn wǒ jiù xià bān le — After the examination at the hospital the doctor held my report and said, “Luckily you came early…” I broke out in a cold sweat, thinking I had some serious illness, and then the doctor slowly said, “A little later and I would have gone off duty.” (the book’s joke; translation mine. Answer: the patient was scared because 幸亏你来得早 sounds as if a serious illness was caught only just in time; the doctor really meant he was about to finish work.)

options: One and a half hours’ leave

exercises.prompt: Why did David need to see a doctor?

exercises.explanation: 睡得不好，头晕、头疼得特别厉害.

options: His child had a high fever and a bad cough

options: She was sent to the ER with gastroenteritis and had to stay three days

lessons.title: 544. Lesson 21 Presentation 3 using Chinese in context: calling 120, an ER story, ERs in China and the U.S.
lessons.subtitle: 看急诊 · 打幺二零 · 病假条 · 急诊室的故事 · 中美看急诊

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Writing, Speaking, Listening and Reading): 看急诊
explanations.body: Scenario: while you and your classmates are studying in Shanghai, one of your housemates has a medical emergency. You and your friend need to call the local emergency center and get your roommate to an emergency room for treatment, then help the roommate ask for sick leave and tell your teacher what happened. A. Work in groups of three. Two members prepare a phone call to the local emergency center; the other acts as the 120 operator and prepares questions to ask the callers; all jot down key words and important information. B. In your group call the emergency hotline 120 and take turns explaining what happened and what help you need; the operator responds. C. Pair up. Text your teacher to ask for sick leave for your housemate and write a draft of the sick-leave note (病假条). D. Find two other students to form a new group of three; your teacher calls you to ask what happened after receiving your message. Include: 1. when, 2. symptoms, 3. what you did, 4. checkups, 5. diagnosis, 6. treatment, 7. estimated recovery time, 8. other information. E. The class reads the sick-leave notes together. My sample call and note:

examples.text: 接线员：您好，这里是幺二零急救中心。请问出什么事了？
examples.translation: jiē xiàn yuán nín hǎo zhè lǐ shì yāo èr líng jí jiù zhōng xīn qǐng wèn chū shén me shì le — Hello, this is the 120 emergency center. What has happened? (sample call, mine)

examples.text: 我：我的室友肚子疼得很厉害，一直呕吐，还发高烧。
examples.translation: wǒ wǒ de shì yǒu dǔ zi téng de hěn lì hài yì zhí ǒu tù hái fā gāo shāo — My roommate has a terrible stomach ache, keeps vomiting and has a high fever. (mine)

examples.text: 接线员：你们在哪儿？请告诉我地址。
examples.translation: jiē xiàn yuán nǐ men zài nǎr qǐng gào sù wǒ dì zhǐ — Where are you? Please tell me the address. (mine)

examples.text: 我：我们在上海复旦大学的二号宿舍楼。
examples.translation: wǒ wǒ men zài shàng hǎi fù dàn dà xué de èr hào sù shè lóu — We are in Dormitory Building 2 at Fudan University in Shanghai. (mine)

examples.text: 接线员：病人多大年纪？他有没有意识？
examples.translation: jiē xiàn yuán bìng rén duō dà nián jì tā yǒu méi yǒu yì shí — How old is the patient? Is he conscious? (mine)

examples.text: 我：二十岁，他有意识，可是疼得说不出话。
examples.translation: wǒ èr shí suì tā yǒu yì shí kě shì téng de shuō bù chū huà — Twenty. He is conscious, but in too much pain to speak. (mine)

examples.text: 接线员：好，救护车马上就到。请不要给他吃东西，也别让他一个人。

lessons.title: 546. Lesson 21 Area Studies: China’s Healthcare Sector, Promising for 2020 and Beyond
lessons.subtitle: 医疗行业 · 医保覆盖 · 健康科技 · 医疗人工智能 · 2020年以后

explanations.title: China’s Healthcare Sector Promising for 2020 and Beyond (1)
explanations.body: In China, many sectors of the healthcare industry are growing rapidly. There are numerous reasons: urbanization, an aging population, a continuous rise in wages and living standards for Chinese citizens, greater innovation in high-tech and broader access to healthcare. China constantly improves its health statistics: per capita healthcare spending in China has risen from $42 in 2000 to $398 in 2016, according to World Bank statistics. China passed Japan in total healthcare spending in 2016 with $574 billion compared to Japan’s $469 billion and passed the U.S. in hospital beds per 1,000 persons, with 3.8 for China and only 2.9 in the U.S., according to OECD data. China is seeing some of the fastest growth in this category, putting it ahead of countries such as Norway, Canada and the UK. This is in part due to Chinese government policies such as increased funding for hospitals.

explanations.title: (2) Doctors, nurses, life expectancy and the reasons for growth
explanations.body: The number of doctors per 1,000 inhabitants has also been continuously rising in China since 2002, from 1.13 to 2.01 in 2017, according to OECD health data, putting it above the East Asian and Pacific average. A similar development is seen in the number of nurses per 1,000 inhabitants, with 1 in 2004 rising to 2.7 in 2017. Life expectancy has also continuously risen in China: according to statistics for the United Nations World Population Prospects the current life expectancy for Chinese citizens is 76.79 years, significantly higher than the world average life expectancy of 72 years. The growing healthcare sector is in many aspects a byproduct of China’s recent economic rise. Several hundred million people were lifted out of poverty in recent decades, which led to overall higher living standards and affordability of healthcare services. This in turn created the continuously rising life expectancy, with more people reaching retirement age than ever before, which further increases the demand for healthcare services. Within the last two decades China has benefited from large-scale reforms in the fields of medical infrastructure and insurance as well as the opening-up of its healthcare market. Focus has been on developing urban areas and continuously making healthcare more accessible in rural China. This has boosted development and the number of hospitals, doctors and medical equipment.

explanations.title: (3) Medical insurance and health tech
explanations.body: The most important contributor might be that, according to the State Council, China has created the world’s largest network for basic medical insurance accessible for all, and formed a healthcare service system encompassing both urban and rural areas. By the end of 2016 basic medical insurance had reached over 1.3 billion citizens nationwide, accounting for more than 95 percent of the total population. Promising industries for 2020 and beyond: health tech and medical AI. To tackle overcrowded hospitals in an innovative way, the government made it clear that health technology is a strategic area of development for China. It features heavily in both the 13th Five-Year Plan (2016–2020) and its Healthy China 2030 strategy. In April 2018 the State Council also issued new guidelines to promote internet-based healthcare, encouraging medical institutions to leverage internet-based technologies to improve the efficiency of medical services. China’s large number of smartphone and internet users (700 million today) provides large potential for more technology use in healthcare subsectors. Everything can be done via apps in the future, also called “fingertip medical treatment”. Data from the National Health Commission showed that in 2017 China’s online healthcare market reached 32.5 billion yuan ($4.6 billion), 45.87 percent higher than that of the previous year. The market will grow to 90 billion yuan by 2020.

explanations.title: (4) WeChat, medical AI and the outlook
explanations.body: Tencent, for example, has already been steadily building up a network of participating hospitals, over 38,000 medical facilities as of 2017, where users can book doctors’ appointments through their WeChat Intelligent Healthcare to avoid long lines at medical facilities. Following their health checkup, patients can also conveniently access their medical reports through WeChat and pay for their medical bills. Also, China is a frontrunner in the field of medical AI. In 2018 Alibaba’s health unit introduced AI software that could help interpret CT scans and an AI medical lab to help doctors make diagnoses. Deep-learning algorithms trained through the data of billions can analyze medical outputs like CT and MRI images with a close to 100 percent accuracy. Tencent established the AI Medical Innovation System or AIMIS, an AI-powered diagnostic medical imaging service, available so far in over 10 hospitals across the country. Images of patient tissue are fed into the AI software, which can then determine in under four seconds whether the body looks normal, inflamed or cancerous. Currently over 130 Chinese companies are working on applying AI in healthcare, with their number expected to grow even further in 2020. Outlook: the healthcare market in China is expected to reach 198 billion yuan ($28.59 billion) in 2026, increasing tenfold from 2016, according to China Briefing. China believes it is the government’s duty to further regulate the market through innovative measures and policies and assure that with the growth of the healthcare sector medical treatment remains affordable for all citizens. The programs of Healthy China 2020 and Healthy China 2030 both outline comprehensive health care reforms which aim to ensure universal healthcare access as well as improve the overall health situation of all Chinese people. China has managed to progress in three fields simultaneously to ensure stable growth of the healthcare sector: reducing overcrowding of hospitals, increasing quality of healthcare, and at the same time keeping healthcare affordable and accessible to all. (References printed in the book: Chinadaily (2020), Michael Santiago (2020), Ali Sheikh (2020).)

explanations.title: Unit 4 overview and Lesson 22 objectives (请问怎么走, Asking for Directions)
explanations.body: Unit 4, Survival Skill and Social Factors. Lesson 22 topic: Ask for directions. Tasks and functions: obtain and provide simple directions; ask and provide directions; understand and explain ways of taking public transportation; describe facilities and provide directions at an airport. Grammar: 还 as a modal adverb; common expressions for taking public transportation; the basic structure of explanatory text; approximate numbers. Area Studies: China’s Tourism. Upon completion of this lesson you will be able to: ask for directions; understand and give directions for driving, walking, and taking public transportation; describe facilities and provide directions at an airport. To do so you must master: new words and phrases for these functions; common expressions used when taking public transportation; the general expressions for giving directions; the basic structure of explanatory text; 还 as a modal adverb; approximate numbers.

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss: A. How do you usually get directions when you go someplace new? B. What is the best way to get directions when taking public transportation? C. Have you ever gotten lost? How did you find directions? D. Has anyone ever asked you for help with directions? How did you help them? E. In the internet era, do you think people can still get lost? Under what circumstances might that happen? (A photograph is not included.)

lessons.title: 549. Lesson 22 Presentation 1 grammar: 还 as a modal adverb
lessons.subtitle: 我还真不知道 · 我还以为…呢 · 还担心…呢 · 还可以 还不错 · 比…还…

explanations.title: 还 Used to Express a Certain Mood or Tone
explanations.body: Aside from its many other meanings and usages, 还 can also be used to express certain moods or tones, depending on the context. Pattern: Subject + 还 + Predicate. In sentences 1 and 2, 还 expresses a surprised tone, indicating something the speaker just realized but thinks he should have known or realized before. In sentence 3, the speaker is surprised that his previous thoughts were wrong. In sentence 4, 还 expresses a tone of relief from original worries. In sentence 5, 还 creates a sense of pride and can be translated as “even” in English. Without 还, these sentences are bland, even though they still convey the same meaning.

examples.text: 美国大使馆？我还真不知道。
examples.translation: měi guó dà shǐ guǎn wǒ hái zhēn bù zhī dào — The book’s example 1: The American Embassy? I really don’t know. (还 expresses surprise: something the speaker just realized he should have known)

examples.text: 我看，你是上网上瘾了。——还真有点儿。
examples.translation: wǒ kàn nǐ shì shàng wǎng shàng yǐn le hái zhēn yǒu diǎnr — 2. I think you’re addicted to the internet. — Yes, a bit actually. (还 again expresses surprise; the book prints 上网瘾了, which I read as 上网上瘾了)

examples.text: 你看起来这么年轻，我还以为你是学生呢！
examples.translation: nǐ kàn qǐ lái zhè me nián qīng wǒ hái yǐ wéi nǐ shì xué shēng ne — 3. You look so young, I thought you were a student! (the speaker is surprised that his earlier thought was wrong)

examples.text: 流感啊？我还担心是肺炎呢。
examples.translation: liú gǎn a wǒ hái dān xīn shì fèi yán ne — 4. The flu? I was afraid it was pneumonia. (还 expresses relief from an original worry)

examples.text: 听起来挺酷的。——那当然，我们的乐队还上过电视呢！
examples.translation: tīng qǐ lái tǐng kù de nà dāng rán wǒ men de yuè duì hái shàng guò diàn shì ne — 5. It sounds pretty cool. — Of course; our band has even been on TV! (还 creates a sense of pride and can be translated “even”)

explanations.title: 还 before a positive adjective
explanations.body: Another common use of 还 is to place it in front of a positive adjective to weaken it, or to make the speaker’s tone less enthusiastic. Pattern: Subject + 还 + Positive Adjective (好 / 行 / 可以 / 不错). Notes: when “还 + adjective” is used in a comparative sentence, it functions as emphasis.

examples.text: 饭厅还可以，厨房好像小了一点儿。
examples.translation: fàn tīng hái kě yǐ chú fáng hǎo xiàng xiǎo le yì diǎnr — 1. The dining room is OK; the kitchen seems a little small.

examples.text: 这次她考得还好。
examples.translation: zhè cì tā kǎo de hái hǎo — 2. She did fairly well on this exam. (the book prints 考的)

examples.text: 这家饭店做的菜还不错。
examples.translation: zhè jiā fàn diàn zuò de cài hái bú cuò — 3. The dishes at this restaurant are pretty good.

examples.text: 这件衣服的颜色还行，就是样式有点老。
examples.translation: zhè jiàn yī fú de yán sè hái xíng jiù shì yàng shì yǒu diǎn lǎo — 4. The color of this garment is all right; the style is just a bit old-fashioned.

examples.text: 他比爸爸还高了！
examples.translation: tā bǐ bà bà hái gāo le — Note: He is even taller than his father! (还 + adjective in a comparative sentence works as emphasis)

examples.text: 我卖的西瓜比篮球还大，比糖还甜。
examples.translation: wǒ mài de xī guā bǐ lán qiú hái dà bǐ táng hái tián — My watermelons are even bigger than a basketball and sweeter than candy.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Read the following sentences and explain the function of each use of 还. Then pair up and check your answer with your partner’s. The book gives the five sentences; the explanations are mine:

examples.text: 这个房子还可以，但是有点儿贵。
examples.translation: zhè ge fáng zi hái kě yǐ dàn shì yǒu diǎnr guì — 1. 还 weakens the positive adjective: This house is OK, but a bit expensive. (key mine)

examples.text: 我还没去过中国的邮局。
examples.translation: wǒ hái méi qù guò zhōng guó de yóu jú — 2. 还没 = not yet (the ordinary meaning, “still/yet”): I haven’t been to a Chinese post office yet.

examples.text: 他唱得比专业歌手还好。
examples.translation: tā chàng de bǐ zhuān yè gē shǒu hái hǎo — 3. 还 in a comparison emphasizes: He sings even better than a professional singer.

examples.text: 晚上一个人走路，还真有点儿害怕。
examples.translation: wǎn shàng yí gè rén zǒu lù hái zhēn yǒu diǎnr hài pà — 4. 还真 expresses surprise at oneself: Walking alone at night, I really am a bit scared.

examples.text: 你还在这儿？我还以为你回家了呢。
examples.translation: nǐ hái zài zhèr wǒ hái yǐ wéi nǐ huí jiā le ne — 5. First 还 = still; second 还以为…呢 expresses surprise that the earlier thought was wrong: You’re still here? I thought you had gone home.

options: Surprise at something the speaker should have known

options: Surprise that the earlier thought was wrong

What does 还 express in 我们的乐队还上过电视呢?

Which adjectives does the weakening pattern use?

大, 小, 多, 少

exercises.prompt: What does 还 do in 他比爸爸还高了?
What does 我还没去过中国的邮局 mean?
options: I haven’t been to a Chinese post office yet

lessons.title: 550. Lesson 22 Presentation 1 grammar: approximate numbers
lessons.subtitle: 几分钟 十几分钟 二十来分钟 二十分钟左右 · 四五分钟 两三个 十七八个 · 两 as 几 · 一望二三里

explanations.title: Approximate Numbers
explanations.body: There are various ways to express an approximate number. Another way to express approximation is by using two numbers together; usually the smaller number is placed before the larger. Pattern: Number + (Number + 1).

tables.title: Approximate numbers

examples.text: 再走四五分钟就到了。
examples.translation: zài zǒu sì wǔ fēn zhōng jiù dào le — The book’s example 1: Walk four or five more minutes and you’ll be there.

examples.text: 教室里只有两三个学生。
examples.translation: jiào shì lǐ zhǐ yǒu liǎng sān gè xué shēng — 2. There are only two or three students in the classroom.

examples.text: 操场上有十七八个学生在锻炼。
examples.translation: cāo chǎng shàng yǒu shí qī bā gè xué shēng zài duàn liàn — 3. There are seventeen or eighteen students exercising on the playground.

examples.text: 他看起来三十五六岁的样子。
examples.translation: tā kàn qǐ lái sān shí wǔ liù suì de yàng zi — 4. He looks about thirty-five or thirty-six.

examples.text: 西安市的人均工资是六七千元人民币。
examples.translation: xī ān shì de rén jūn gōng zī shì liù qī qiān yuán rén mín bì — 5. The average income per person in Xi’an is six or seven thousand yuan.

explanations.title: Notes
explanations.body: 1. When 二 and 三 are used together as single-digit numbers and followed by a measure word, 二 usually is in the form of 两, like 两三个菜, 两三斤苹果. 2. Numbers that end with “0” cannot be used with adjacent numbers, like “9, 10” or “10, 11”. 3. When two-digit numbers are used together, they must be shortened; “16 or 17” would be 十六七, and “30 to 40” would be 三四十. Note that even when used alone, 两 can be an unspecified number. Like the English phrase “a couple of”, 两 is an unspecified number in the sentences below and is equivalent to 几, or “a few.”

examples.text: 我请你喝两杯。
examples.translation: wǒ qǐng nǐ hē liǎng bēi — 1. I’ll treat you to a couple of drinks.

examples.text: 来，下两盘（棋）！
examples.translation: lái xià liǎng pán qí — 2. Come on, let’s play a couple of games (of chess)!

examples.text: 过两天就是爸爸的生日了。
examples.translation: guò liǎng tiān jiù shì bà bà de shēng rì le — 3. In a couple of days it’s Dad’s birthday.

examples.text: 到我这儿来玩儿两天吧。
examples.translation: dào wǒ zhèr lái wánr liǎng tiān ba — 4. Come and stay with me a couple of days.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading)
explanations.body: Pair up. With your partner, discuss what is wrong with the following sentences. The book prints the five wrong sentences (it prints the digit-free forms 十十一, 十五十六, 二三, 六八 and the 过两天 dialog); my corrections and reasons:

examples.text: 我今天买了十一个苹果。
examples.translation: wǒ jīn tiān mǎi le shí yī gè píng guǒ — 1. The book’s wrong sentence: 我今天买了十十一个苹果. Fix (mine): numbers ending in 0 cannot be placed next to another number, so say 十一个 (exactly eleven) or 十几个 (about ten-odd): I bought eleven apples today.

examples.text: 操场上有十五六个学生。
examples.translation: cāo chǎng shàng yǒu shí wǔ liù gè xué shēng — 2. Wrong: 十五十六个. Two-digit numbers used together must be shortened: There are fifteen or sixteen students on the playground. (fix mine)

examples.text: 我认识两三个中国朋友。
examples.translation: wǒ rèn shí liǎng sān gè zhōng guó péng yǒu — 3. Wrong: 二三个. 二 before a measure word is 两: I know two or three Chinese friends. (fix mine)

examples.text: 我吃了六七个饺子。
examples.translation: wǒ chī le liù qī gè jiǎo zi — 4. Wrong: 六八个. Adjacent approximate numbers must be consecutive (六七 or 七八): I ate six or seven dumplings. (fix mine)

examples.text: 张文：过两天咱们去看电影吧。——马克：好的，是后天吗？
examples.translation: zhāng wén guò liǎng tiān zán men qù kàn diàn yǐng ba mǎ kè hǎo de shì hòu tiān ma — 5. Wrong: 过两天 is an unspecified “in a couple of days” (like 几天), not exactly the day after tomorrow, so Mark’s question is a misunderstanding: Zhang Wen: Let’s go to the movies in a couple of days. — Mark: OK, do you mean the day after tomorrow? (key mine)

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Speaking)
explanations.body: Pair up. Read about Mr. Wang and take turns saying the underlined phrases in Chinese: 1. Mr. Wang is 50–60 years old. 2. He has been working at the university for 20–30 years. 3. His salary is around ¥5000–6000 a month. 4. He teaches 25 to 26 students in each class. 5. He teaches 14–15 hours per week. 6. He does not finish work until 11 p.m.–12 a.m. every night. My sentences:

examples.text: 他今年五六十岁了。
examples.translation: tā jīn nián wǔ liù shí suì le — 1. Mr. Wang is fifty to sixty years old. (Activity 3, mine)

examples.text: 他在这所大学工作二三十年了。
examples.translation: tā zài zhè suǒ dà xué gōng zuò èr sān shí nián le — 2. He has been working at the university for twenty to thirty years. (mine)

examples.text: 他的工资每个月五六千元左右。
examples.translation: tā de gōng zī měi gè yuè wǔ liù qiān yuán zuǒ yòu — 3. His salary is around five or six thousand yuan a month. (mine)

examples.text: 他每个班有二十五六个学生。
examples.translation: tā měi gè bān yǒu èr shí wǔ liù gè xué shēng — 4. He has twenty-five or twenty-six students in each class. (mine)

examples.text: 他每个星期上十四五个小时的课。
examples.translation: tā měi gè xīng qī shàng shí sì wǔ gè xiǎo shí de kè — 5. He teaches fourteen or fifteen hours a week. (mine)

examples.text: 他每天晚上十一二点才下班。
examples.translation: tā měi tiān wǎn shàng shí yī èr diǎn cái xià bān — 6. He does not finish work until eleven or twelve every night. (mine)

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading)
explanations.body: Read the poem aloud and note the poetic use of numbers (the book adds a picture, not included).

examples.text: 一望二三里，烟村四五家，门前六七树，八九十枝花。
examples.translation: yí wàng èr sān lǐ yān cūn sì wǔ jiā mén qián liù qī shù bā jiǔ shí zhī huā — Activity 4: the poem of numbers. As far as the eye can see, two or three li; a misty village of four or five homes; before the door six or seven trees; eight, nine, ten sprays of flowers. (translation mine)

options: Numbers that end in 0 cannot be placed next to another number
