lessons.subtitle: 瞧不起 · 解读 · 公众号 · 非要…不可 · 小周的课 · 向九零后学习互联网 · 企业家论坛

explanations.title: Skill Integration, Activity 2 (Reading, Speaking, and Writing)
explanations.body: A. Pair up. Guess the meaning of each underlined expression in each of the sentences. Then consult a dictionary to check your guesses. B. Read the essay. Then mark the statements as either True or False. C. Pair up and discuss your answers. Then work together to translate the sentences into English. D. Pair up. Create a dialog between the author and a friend using the information in the passage. Act out the dialog for the class. The expressions, the sentences, the essay, my key, translations and sample dialog:

tables.title: Activity 2A: the underlined expressions (the underlining is lost in the text; these are the ones I take to be meant)

examples.text: 这些年轻人很聪明，不要瞧不起他们。
examples.translation: zhè xiē nián qīng rén hěn cōng míng bú yào qiáo bù qǐ tā men — Activity 2A, 1: These young people are very smart; don’t look down on them. (translations mine)

examples.text: 这篇文章我们看不太懂，请您解读一下好吗？
examples.translation: zhè piān wén zhāng wǒ men kàn bú tài dǒng qǐng nín jiě dú yí xià hǎo ma — 2: We can’t quite understand this article; could you interpret it for us?

examples.text: 我们一起吃完饭以后，他非要付钱不可。
examples.translation: wǒ men yì qǐ chī wán fàn yǐ hòu tā fēi yào fù qián bù kě — 3: After we ate together, he insisted on paying.

examples.text: 她每个星期在自己的公众号上发表一篇文章。
examples.translation: tā měi gè xīng qī zài zì jǐ de gōng zhòng hào shàng fā biǎo yì piān wén zhāng — 4: Every week she publishes an article on her own official account.

examples.text: 我小时候最不喜欢大人瞧不起我，但等我过了三十岁，也开始觉得二十来岁的人做什么事都不行了。一天，我们单位的小王转给我一个公众号，说是她大学同学小周办的，每星期发一篇关于读书的文章。我想，我都读了三十多年的书了，还需要看年轻人关于读书的文章吗？所以根本就没看。过了几个月，小王又说那个人要在网上上课，教“怎么解读一本书，成为讲书人”，并请她带一个朋友参加。小王非要我跟她一起参加不可，我就只好参加了。没想到，小周的课马上就把我吸引住了，越听越喜欢。后来我试了一下他讲的方法，真的很有效果！过了不久，我自己也开始在网上讲自己看的书，并且越来越受欢迎。后来，我每个月在网上讲课的收入超过了工资。把爱好变成赚钱的方法，这是年轻人教我的！年轻人不是很有经验，但是他们很喜欢创新，所以他们做的很多事情，代表了将来发展的方向。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎo shí hòu zuì bù xǐ huān dà rén qiáo bù qǐ wǒ dàn děng wǒ guò le sān shí suì yě kāi shǐ jué de èr shí lái suì de rén zuò shén me shì dōu bù xíng le yì tiān wǒ men dān wèi de xiǎo wáng zhuǎn gěi wǒ yí gè gōng zhòng hào shuō shì tā dà xué tóng xué xiǎo zhōu bàn de měi xīng qī fā yì piān guān yú dú shū de wén zhāng wǒ xiǎng wǒ dōu dú le sān shí duō nián de shū le hái xū yào kàn nián qīng rén guān yú dú shū de wén zhāng ma suǒ yǐ gēn běn jiù méi kàn guò le jǐ gè yuè xiǎo wáng yòu shuō nà ge rén yào zài wǎng shàng shàng kè jiào zěn me jiě dú yì běn shū chéng wéi jiǎng shū rén bìng qǐng tā dài yí gè péng yǒu cān jiā xiǎo wáng fēi yào wǒ gēn tā yì qǐ cān jiā bù kě wǒ jiù zhǐ hǎo cān jiā le méi xiǎng dào xiǎo zhōu de kè mǎ shàng jiù bǎ wǒ xī yǐn zhù le yuè tīng yuè xǐ huān hòu lái wǒ shì le yí xià tā jiǎng de fāng fǎ zhēn de hěn yǒu xiào guǒ guò le bù jiǔ wǒ zì jǐ yě kāi shǐ zài wǎng shàng jiǎng zì jǐ kàn de shū bìng qiě yuè lái yuè shòu huān yíng hòu lái wǒ měi gè yuè zài wǎng shàng jiǎng kè de shōu rù chāo guò le gōng zī bǎ ài hào biàn chéng zhuàn qián de fāng fǎ zhè shì nián qīng rén jiāo wǒ de nián qīng rén bú shì hěn yǒu jīng yàn dàn shì tā men hěn xǐ huān chuàng xīn suǒ yǐ tā men zuò de hěn duō shì qíng dài biǎo le jiāng lái fā zhǎn de fāng xiàng — When I was little I most disliked adults looking down on me, but after I passed thirty I too began to feel that people in their twenties could do nothing right. One day Xiao Wang at our workplace forwarded me an official account, saying it was run by her university classmate Xiao Zhou, who posted one article a week about reading. I thought, I have read books for more than thirty years; do I still need to read young people’s articles about reading? So I didn’t read it at all. After a few months, Xiao Wang said that person was going to teach online, teaching “how to interpret a book and become a book talker,” and asked her to bring a friend. Xiao Wang insisted I join her, so I had no choice but to attend. Unexpectedly, Xiao Zhou’s class captivated me at once, and the more I listened the more I liked it. Later I tried the method he taught, and it really worked! Not long after, I began to talk online about books I had read, and became more and more popular. Later, my monthly income from teaching online exceeded my salary. Turning a hobby into a way to make money, this is what a young person taught me! Young people are not very experienced, but they love to innovate, so many things they do represent the direction of future development. (Activity 2B, an essay; the book writes 20 and 30 in digits; translation mine)

examples.text: 作者自己是个年轻人，她觉得岁数大的人不应该瞧不起年轻人。
examples.translation: zuò zhě zì jǐ shì gè nián qīng rén tā jué de suì shù dà de rén bù yīng gāi qiáo bù qǐ nián qīng rén — Activity 2B-1 (true or false; my key: False, the author is over thirty): The author is a young person herself and feels that older people should not look down on young people.

examples.text: 小周在网上教怎么给别人讲一本自己看过的书。
examples.translation: xiǎo zhōu zài wǎng shàng jiào zěn me gěi bié rén jiǎng yì běn zì jǐ kàn guò de shū — 2B-2 (my key: True): Xiao Zhou teaches online how to tell others about a book you have read.

examples.text: 作者听说小周要开课，非常高兴，马上就报名参加了。
examples.translation: zuò zhě tīng shuō xiǎo zhōu yào kāi kè fēi cháng gāo xìng mǎ shàng jiù bào míng cān jiā le — 2B-3 (my key: False, Xiao Wang insisted and she attended reluctantly): The author was very happy to hear Xiao Zhou would give a class and signed up right away.

examples.text: 作者从小周讲的课里学到了很多东西。
examples.translation: zuò zhě cóng xiǎo zhōu jiǎng de kè lǐ xué dào le hěn duō dōng xī — 2B-4 (my key: True): The author learned a lot from Xiao Zhou’s class.

examples.text: 作者觉得年轻人又聪明赚钱又多，所以应该向他们学习。
examples.translation: zuò zhě jué de nián qīng rén yòu cōng míng zhuàn qián yòu duō suǒ yǐ yīng gāi xiàng tā men xué xí — 2B-5 (my key: False, the article does not say this; the book prints 先他们学习, apparently 向): The author feels young people are both smart and earn a lot, so we should learn from them.

examples.text: 我小时候最不喜欢大人瞧不起我，但等我过了三十岁，也开始觉得二十来岁的人做什么事都不行了。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎo shí hòu zuì bù xǐ huān dà rén qiáo bù qǐ wǒ dàn děng wǒ guò le sān shí suì yě kāi shǐ jué de èr shí lái suì de rén zuò shén me shì dōu bù xíng le — Activity 2C, 1 (my translation): When I was little I most disliked adults looking down on me, but after I passed thirty I too began to feel that people in their twenties could do nothing right.

examples.text: 我想，我都读了三十多年的书了，还需要看年轻人关于读书的文章吗？所以根本就没看。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎng wǒ dōu dú le sān shí duō nián de shū le hái xū yào kàn nián qīng rén guān yú dú shū de wén zhāng ma suǒ yǐ gēn běn jiù méi kàn — 2: I thought, I have read books for more than thirty years; do I still need to read young people’s articles about reading? So I didn’t read it at all.

examples.text: 没想到，小周的课马上就把我吸引住了，越听越喜欢。后来我试了一下他讲的方法，真的很有效果！
examples.translation: méi xiǎng dào xiǎo zhōu de kè mǎ shàng jiù bǎ wǒ xī yǐn zhù le yuè tīng yuè xǐ huān hòu lái wǒ shì le yí xià tā jiǎng de fāng fǎ zhēn de hěn yǒu xiào guǒ — 3: Unexpectedly, Xiao Zhou’s class captivated me at once, and the more I listened the more I liked it. Later I tried the method he taught, and it really worked!

examples.text: 把爱好变成赚钱的方法，这是年轻人教我的！年轻人不是很有经验，但是他们很喜欢创新，所以他们做的很多事情，代表了将来发展的方向。
examples.translation: bǎ ài hào biàn chéng zhuàn qián de fāng fǎ zhè shì nián qīng rén jiāo wǒ de nián qīng rén bú shì hěn yǒu jīng yàn dàn shì tā men hěn xǐ huān chuàng xīn suǒ yǐ tā men zuò de hěn duō shì qíng dài biǎo le jiāng lái fā zhǎn de fāng xiàng — 4: Turning a hobby into a way to make money, this is what a young person taught me! Young people are not very experienced, but they love to innovate, so many things they do represent the direction of future development.

examples.text: 朋友：你小时候喜欢大人瞧不起你吗？
examples.translation: péng yǒu nǐ xiǎo shí hòu xǐ huān dà rén qiáo bù qǐ nǐ ma — Activity 2D (my sample dialog between the author and a friend, from the passage; translations mine). Friend: When you were little, did you like adults looking down on you?

examples.text: 作者：当然不喜欢，可是过了三十岁，我也开始觉得二十来岁的人做什么事都不行了。
examples.translation: zuò zhě dāng rán bù xǐ huān kě shì guò le sān shí suì wǒ yě kāi shǐ jué de èr shí lái suì de rén zuò shén me shì dōu bù xíng le — Author: Of course not, but after I passed thirty I too began to feel that people in their twenties could do nothing right.

examples.text: 朋友：那你后来为什么参加了小周的课？
examples.translation: péng yǒu nà nǐ hòu lái wèi shén me cān jiā le xiǎo zhōu de kè — Friend: Then why did you later attend Xiao Zhou’s class?

examples.text: 作者：小王转给我一个公众号，是她大学同学小周办的，我根本就没看。过了几个月，小周要在网上上课，小王非要我跟她一起参加不可，我就只好参加了。
examples.translation: zuò zhě xiǎo wáng zhuǎn gěi wǒ yí gè gōng zhòng hào shì tā dà xué tóng xué xiǎo zhōu bàn de wǒ gēn běn jiù méi kàn guò le jǐ gè yuè xiǎo zhōu yào zài wǎng shàng shàng kè xiǎo wáng fēi yào wǒ gēn tā yì qǐ cān jiā bù kě wǒ jiù zhǐ hǎo cān jiā le — Author: Xiao Wang forwarded me an official account run by her university classmate Xiao Zhou and I didn’t read it at all. A few months later Xiao Zhou was going to teach online, Xiao Wang insisted I join her, so I had to attend.

examples.text: 朋友：那课怎么样？
examples.translation: péng yǒu nà kè zěn me yàng — Friend: And how was the class?

examples.text: 作者：没想到，小周的课马上就把我吸引住了。我试了一下他讲的方法，真的很有效果！
examples.translation: zuò zhě méi xiǎng dào xiǎo zhōu de kè mǎ shàng jiù bǎ wǒ xī yǐn zhù le wǒ shì le yí xià tā jiǎng de fāng fǎ zhēn de hěn yǒu xiào guǒ — Author: Unexpectedly, it captivated me at once. I tried his method and it really worked!

examples.text: 朋友：后来呢？
examples.translation: péng yǒu hòu lái ne — Friend: And then?

examples.text: 作者：我自己也开始在网上讲书，越来越受欢迎，每个月在网上讲课的收入超过了工资。
examples.translation: zuò zhě wǒ zì jǐ yě kāi shǐ zài wǎng shàng jiǎng shū yuè lái yuè shòu huān yíng měi gè yuè zài wǎng shàng jiǎng kè de shōu rù chāo guò le gōng zī — Author: I began to talk about books online myself, became more and more popular, and my monthly income from teaching online exceeded my salary.

examples.text: 朋友：你现在怎么看年轻人？
examples.translation: péng yǒu nǐ xiàn zài zěn me kàn nián qīng rén — Friend: How do you see young people now?

examples.text: 作者：年轻人不是很有经验，但是他们很喜欢创新，他们做的很多事情，代表了将来发展的方向。
examples.translation: zuò zhě nián qīng rén bú shì hěn yǒu jīng yàn dàn shì tā men hěn xǐ huān chuàng xīn tā men zuò de hěn duō shì qíng dài biǎo le jiāng lái fā zhǎn de fāng xiàng — Author: Young people are not very experienced, but they love to innovate, and many things they do represent the direction of future development.

explanations.title: Skill Integration, Activity 3 (Reading, Writing, and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Read the authentic material below. Underline any unknown words, and then highlight those words that are critical to your understanding of the passage. Guess what they mean and share your guesses with a classmate. Then consult a dictionary to confirm your guesses. B. Summarize the passage in English. C. Share your summary with your partner. Then, in Chinese, ask each other questions about the passage. (Each partner asks eight questions, two per paragraph.) The passage, a sample summary and my eight questions:

examples.text: 昨天在上海参加了一个企业家论坛，其中有一场的内容是向九零后学习互联网。一大帮七零后、六零后的企业家，坐在那里听着台上五个九零后年轻的创业者，讲解他们创业的心得。
examples.translation: zuó tiān zài shàng hǎi cān jiā le yí gè qǐ yè jiā lùn tán qí zhōng yǒu yì cháng de nèi róng shì xiàng jiǔ líng hòu xué xí hù lián wǎng yí dà bāng qī líng hòu liù líng hòu de qǐ yè jiā zuò zài nà lǐ tīng zhe tái shàng wǔ gè jiǔ líng hòu nián qīng de chuàng yè zhě jiǎng jiě tā men chuàng yè de xīn de — Yesterday I attended an entrepreneurs’ forum in Shanghai, one session of which was about learning the Internet from the post-’90s. A large group of post-’70s and post-’60s entrepreneurs sat there listening to five young post-’90s founders on the stage explain what they had learned from starting their businesses. (Activity 3, an authentic blog post; the book writes 90 后, 70 后, 60 后 in digits and names its source, a blog site; translations mine)

examples.text: 回答问题的时候，他们都回答问题得很简单，也很直接，没有那些客套。一位七零后企业家说：“你们不用考虑各种关系，也很成功。我们这些年天天应酬，酒都白喝了。”
examples.translation: huí dá wèn tí de shí hòu tā men dōu huí dá wèn tí de hěn jiǎn dān yě hěn zhí jiē méi yǒu nà xiē kè tào yí wèi qī líng hòu qǐ yè jiā shuō nǐ men bú yòng kǎo lǜ gè zhǒng guān xì yě hěn chéng gōng wǒ men zhè xiē nián tiān tiān yìng chóu jiǔ dōu bái hē le — When answering questions they all answered very simply and directly, without the pleasantries. A post-’70s entrepreneur said, “You don’t have to consider all kinds of connections, and you are successful all the same. We have been socializing every day these years, and all that drinking was in vain.” (the book prints 他们都回答问题得很简单, apparently 回答得很简单)

examples.text: 听着他们在讲话，我想，台下很多人今天很有钱，但是，他们不懂高科技，过几年他们很可能就不会这么富有。台上的年轻一代有知识，爱学习，虽然他们现在还不富有，但是明天将会是他们的。
examples.translation: tīng zhe tā men zài jiǎng huà wǒ xiǎng tái xià hěn duō rén jīn tiān hěn yǒu qián dàn shì tā men bù dǒng gāo kē jì guò jǐ nián tā men hěn kě néng jiù bú huì zhè me fù yǒu tái shàng de nián qīng yí dài yǒu zhī shí ài xué xí suī rán tā men xiàn zài hái bú fù yǒu dàn shì míng tiān jiāng huì shì tā men de — Listening to them speak, I thought, many people in the audience are very rich today, but they don’t understand high tech and in a few years they may well not be so wealthy. The young generation on the stage have knowledge and love learning; although they are not rich yet, tomorrow will be theirs.

examples.text: 我想起前不久听了一次课，主讲的老师说，他要向自己的子女学习，因为他们常常是对的。这位老师说得有道理。中国有五千年的历史，中国文化强调尊重老人。这并不错，可是，有些东西前辈应该向后辈学习。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎng qǐ qián bù jiǔ tīng le yí cì kè zhǔ jiǎng de lǎo shī shuō tā yào xiàng zì jǐ de zǐ nǚ xué xí yīn wèi tā men cháng cháng shì duì de zhè wèi lǎo shī shuō de yǒu dào lǐ zhōng guó yǒu wǔ qiān nián de lì shǐ zhōng guó wén huà qiáng diào zūn zhòng lǎo rén zhè bìng bú cuò kě shì yǒu xiē dōng xī qián bèi yīng gāi xiàng hòu bèi xué xí — I remembered a lecture I heard not long ago, in which the teacher said he wants to learn from his own children because they are often right. This teacher has a point. China has a history of five thousand years, and Chinese culture stresses respect for the old. This is not wrong, but there are some things that the older generation should learn from the younger. (the book breaks two lines of this paragraph awkwardly; I join them)

examples.text: 昨天作者在上海参加了一个企业家论坛，七零后、六零后的企业家听五个九零后的创业者讲创业的心得。九零后回答问题简单直接，作者觉得台下的人有钱但不懂高科技，年轻一代有知识，爱学习，明天是他们的。作者还说，有些东西前辈应该向后辈学习。
examples.translation: zuó tiān zuò zhě zài shàng hǎi cān jiā le yí gè qǐ yè jiā lùn tán qī líng hòu liù líng hòu de qǐ yè jiā tīng wǔ gè jiǔ líng hòu de chuàng yè zhě jiǎng chuàng yè de xīn de jiǔ líng hòu huí dá wèn tí jiǎn dān zhí jiē zuò zhě jué de tái xià de rén yǒu qián dàn bù dǒng gāo kē jì nián qīng yí dài yǒu zhī shí ài xué xí míng tiān shì tā men de zuò zhě hái shuō yǒu xiē dōng xī qián bèi yīng gāi xiàng hòu bèi xué xí — Activity 3B (my sample summary, in Chinese; the book asks for English): Yesterday the author attended an entrepreneurs’ forum in Shanghai where post-’70s and post-’60s entrepreneurs listened to five post-’90s founders talk about their experiences. The post-’90s answered simply and directly; the author feels the audience are rich but don’t understand high tech, while the young generation have knowledge and love learning and tomorrow is theirs. The author also says that in some things the older generation should learn from the younger.

examples.text: 这是什么论坛？在哪儿开的？
examples.translation: zhè shì shén me lùn tán zài nǎr kāi de — Activity 3C (my eight questions, two per paragraph), paragraph 1: What forum was this? Where was it held?

examples.text: 台上是什么人？台下是什么人？
examples.translation: tái shàng shì shén me rén tái xià shì shén me rén — Who were on the stage? Who were in the audience?

examples.text: 九零后回答问题的时候怎么样？
examples.translation: jiǔ líng hòu huí dá wèn tí de shí hòu zěn me yàng — Paragraph 2: How did the post-’90s answer questions?

examples.text: 那位七零后企业家说了什么？
examples.translation: nà wèi qī líng hòu qǐ yè jiā shuō le shén me — What did the post-’70s entrepreneur say?

examples.text: 作者觉得台下的人有什么问题？
examples.translation: zuò zhě jué de tái xià de rén yǒu shén me wèn tí — Paragraph 3: What problem does the author see in the people in the audience?

examples.text: 为什么说明天是年轻一代的？
examples.translation: wèi shén me shuō míng tiān shì nián qīng yí dài de — Why does the author say tomorrow belongs to the young generation?

examples.text: 那位老师为什么要向自己的子女学习？
examples.translation: nà wèi lǎo shī wèi shén me yào xiàng zì jǐ de zǐ nǚ xué xí — Paragraph 4: Why did the teacher want to learn from his own children?

examples.text: 中国文化强调什么？作者怎么看？
examples.translation: zhōng guó wén huà qiáng diào shén me zuò zhě zěn me kàn — What does Chinese culture stress, and how does the author see it?

lessons.title: 745. Lesson 28 Presentation 3 using Chinese in context: situations, and Rong Mengya who sprays cotton fields with drones
lessons.subtitle: 九零后创业者 · 礼物说有什么特点 · 戎梦雅 · 无人机 · 洒农药 · 棉田 · 新疆 · 哈密

explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context, Activity 1 (Reading, Writing, and Speaking)
explanations.body: Pair up and take turns telling your partner what you would say in each of the situations. Provide as many details as possible. Upon completion, switch roles and repeat the activity. 1. 有人问你，中国的九零后有没有成功的创业者。 (two or more sentences) 2. 听说中国很多年轻人喜欢去“礼物说”网站买礼物。那是一个什么样的网站？ (three or more sentences) 3. 温城辉领导下的“礼物说”有什么特点？ (three or more sentences) 4. 如果你也想创业的话，你会做什么？怎么做？ (three or more sentences) My answers:

examples.text: 有。比如温城辉，他创办了“礼物说”网站，一年销售的礼品有几十亿元。
examples.translation: yǒu bǐ rú wēn chéng huī tā chuàng bàn le lǐ wù shuō wǎng zhàn yì nián xiāo shòu de lǐ pǐn yǒu jǐ shí yì yuán — Using Chinese in Context, Activity 1, 1 (my answer, two sentences): Yes. For example Wen Chenghui founded the “Liwushuo” website, and the gifts it sells in a year amount to several billion yuan.

examples.text: “礼物说”是一个专卖礼品的购物网站。顾客在那儿不但可以买到礼物，而且可以从视频上看到使用礼物的效果。它还给顾客一些好的建议，让顾客买到满意的礼物。
examples.translation: lǐ wù shuō shì yí gè zhuān mài lǐ pǐn de gòu wù wǎng zhàn gù kè zài nàr bú dàn kě yǐ mǎi dào lǐ wù ér qiě kě yǐ cóng shì pín shàng kàn dào shǐ yòng lǐ wù de xiào guǒ tā hái gěi gù kè yì xiē hǎo de jiàn yì ràng gù kè mǎi dào mǎn yì de lǐ wù — 2 (my answer, three sentences): “Liwushuo” is a shopping website that sells only gifts. Customers there can not only buy gifts but also see in videos the effect of using them. It also gives customers good suggestions so they can buy a satisfying gift.

examples.text: “礼物说”有自己的特色，会给顾客好的建议。他们用高科技管理公司，使销售快速增长，买过东西的人还可以向别人介绍礼物，吸引了更多的新顾客。
examples.translation: lǐ wù shuō yǒu zì jǐ de tè sè huì gěi gù kè hǎo de jiàn yì tā men yòng gāo kē jì guǎn lǐ gōng sī shǐ xiāo shòu kuài sù zēng zhǎng mǎi guò dōng xī de rén hái kě yǐ xiàng bié rén jiè shào lǐ wù xī yǐn le gèng duō de xīn gù kè — 3 (my answer, three sentences): “Liwushuo” has its own character and gives customers good suggestions. They use high tech to manage the company, making sales grow fast, and people who have bought things can introduce gifts to others, attracting more new customers.

examples.text: 我会开一个网上的咖啡店。我会先研究顾客喜欢什么，再找人帮我做，最后在网上销售。
examples.translation: wǒ huì kāi yí gè wǎng shàng de kā fēi diàn wǒ huì xiān yán jiū gù kè xǐ huān shén me zài zhǎo rén bāng wǒ zuò zuì hòu zài wǎng shàng xiāo shòu — 4 (a sample answer of mine, three sentences; this is a personal question): I would open an online coffee shop. I would first study what customers like, then find people to help me make it, and finally sell online.

explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context, Activity 2 (Reading, Writing, Listening, and Speaking)
explanations.body: As a UNESCO representative in China working on a study about China’s young people, you find yourself in Xinjiang waiting to interview a young woman named 戎梦雅. A. Read a brief bio about this person; consult a dictionary for the underlined words. B. Pair up and discuss the questions you will ask 戎梦雅. C. Listen to Róng talk about her experiences and fill in the table. Share your work with your partner, then go over the script to refine your work. D. Conduct the interview. Your partner will play the role of 戎梦雅. The bio, the words, the script, my table and my questions:

headers: Meaning (mine; the underlining in the book is lost, so these are the words I take to be meant)
tables.title: Activity 2A: words to look up

headers: 信息 (my sample, from the script)
rows: 戎梦雅的经历和她的家庭
九零后，在新疆的棉田陪着长大；父母种着四千多亩棉田；她在英国学习，玩儿过无人机
看到能撒农药的无人机很感兴趣，去深圳学习了无人机技术，和哥哥一起买了一台；试了很多次，找到效果最好的方法；速度比老方法快了很多倍
成立公司给别人的棉田洒药
当地很多种棉花的人也感兴趣，她和哥哥成立了公司，又买了几台无人机；二零一六年年底在哈密给七万多亩棉田洒药，一次赚了差不多三十万元；现在平均每个月的收入超过十万元
tables.title: Activity 2C: the table (the book leaves the cells empty)

examples.text: 几年前，戎梦雅从英国学习结束回到新疆，帮助父母种棉花。每到洒药的时候，就要花钱找人帮忙，很麻烦，速度也很慢。后来戎梦雅学习无人机技术，并和哥哥买了一架无人机，开始了无人机洒药。二零一六年七月成立了自己的公司，每年给新疆几十万亩棉田洒药，月收入十万多元。
examples.translation: jǐ nián qián róng mèng yǎ cóng yīng guó xué xí jié shù huí dào xīn jiāng bāng zhù fù mǔ zhòng mián huā měi dào sǎ yào de shí hòu jiù yào huā qián zhǎo rén bāng máng hěn má fán sù dù yě hěn màn hòu lái róng mèng yǎ xué xí wú rén jī jì shù bìng hé gē gē mǎi le yí jià wú rén jī kāi shǐ le wú rén jī sǎ yào èr líng yī liù nián qī yuè chéng lì le zì jǐ de gōng sī měi nián gěi xīn jiāng jǐ shí wàn mǔ mián tián sǎ yào yuè shōu rù shí wàn duō yuán — A few years ago, Róng Mèngyǎ returned to Xinjiang from studying in Britain to help her parents grow cotton. Whenever it was time to spray pesticide, they had to pay people to help, which was troublesome and slow. Later Rong Mengya studied drone technology, bought a drone with her older brother and began spraying with a drone. In July 2016 she founded her own company, which sprays several hundred thousand mu of cotton fields in Xinjiang every year, with a monthly income of over a hundred thousand yuan. (Using Chinese, Activity 2A, a brief bio; the book writes 2016 in digits and glosses the name with pinyin; translations mine)

examples.text: 你为什么从英国回到新疆？
examples.translation: nǐ wèi shén me cóng yīng guó huí dào xīn jiāng — Activity 2B (my sample questions for Rong Mengya): Why did you come back to Xinjiang from Britain?

examples.text: 你是怎么想起来用无人机洒药的？
examples.translation: nǐ shì zěn me xiǎng qǐ lái yòng wú rén jī sǎ yào de — How did you come up with using a drone to spray pesticide?

examples.text: 用无人机洒药，效果怎么样？
examples.translation: yòng wú rén jī sǎ yào xiào guǒ zěn me yàng — How well does spraying with a drone work?

examples.text: 你们的公司是什么时候成立的？
examples.translation: nǐ men de gōng sī shì shén me shí hòu chéng lì de — When was your company founded?

examples.text: 现在你们的收入怎么样？
examples.translation: xiàn zài nǐ men de shōu rù zěn me yàng — How is your income now?

examples.text: 各位听众，现在我给大家讲一个九零后开公司，用无人机给棉田洒农药的故事。
examples.translation: gè wèi tīng zhòng xiàn zài wǒ gěi dà jiā jiǎng yí gè jiǔ líng hòu kāi gōng sī yòng wú rén jī gěi mián tián sǎ nóng yào de gù shì — Script (translations mine). Dear listeners, now I will tell you a story of a post-’90s person who started a company and uses drones to spray pesticide on cotton fields.

examples.text: 大家都知道，新疆每年生产很多棉花，它的棉花产量呢，是全国产量的百分之八十还多。和许多新疆孩子一样，九零后的戎梦雅是棉田陪着长大的。她父母三十年来到了新疆，现在种着四千多亩棉田。但是，给棉田撒农药特别辛苦。一般情况下，每年要给棉田要洒六次农药。用老方法洒药，一天只能洒两百亩地，洒完四千亩地得多少天啊！
examples.translation: dà jiā dōu zhī dào xīn jiāng měi nián shēng chǎn hěn duō mián huā tā de mián huā chǎn liàng ne shì quán guó chǎn liàng de bǎi fēn zhī bā shí hái duō hé xǔ duō xīn jiāng hái zi yí yàng jiǔ líng hòu de róng mèng yǎ shì mián tián péi zhe zhǎng dà de tā fù mǔ sān shí nián lái dào le xīn jiāng xiàn zài zhòng zhe sì qiān duō mǔ mián tián dàn shì gěi mián tián sā nóng yào tè bié xīn kǔ yì bān qíng kuàng xià měi nián yào gěi mián tián yào sǎ liù cì nóng yào yòng lǎo fāng fǎ sǎ yào yì tiān zhǐ néng sǎ liǎng bǎi mǔ dì sǎ wán sì qiān mǔ dì děi duō shǎo tiān a — As everyone knows, Xinjiang produces a lot of cotton every year, and its cotton output is more than eighty percent of the national output. Like many Xinjiang children, post-’90s Rong Mengya grew up accompanied by cotton fields. Her parents came to Xinjiang thirty years ago (the book prints 三十年来到了新疆) and now grow more than four thousand mu of cotton. But spraying pesticide on cotton fields is especially hard work. Generally the fields must be sprayed six times a year (the book prints 要给棉田要洒; I keep it as printed). With the old method one can spray only two hundred mu a day, so how many days it takes to spray four thousand mu! (the book writes 4000 and 200 in digits)

examples.text: 在英国学习的时候，戎梦雅玩儿过无人机。后来，她看到一台能撒农药的无人机，很感兴趣，就去深圳学习了无人机技术，回家后和哥哥一起买了一台。有了无人机，怎么洒药的效果最好呢？他们试了很多次，最后找到了效果最好的方法，比如放多少水，多少药，无人机得飞多高多快，等等。接着，他们用无人机把自己家的棉田洒了一遍，和以前的老方法比，速度快了很多倍。
examples.translation: zài yīng guó xué xí de shí hòu róng mèng yǎ wánr guò wú rén jī hòu lái tā kàn dào yì tái néng sā nóng yào de wú rén jī hěn gǎn xìng qù jiù qù shēn zhèn xué xí le wú rén jī jì shù huí jiā hòu hé gē gē yì qǐ mǎi le yì tái yǒu le wú rén jī zěn me sǎ yào de xiào guǒ zuì hǎo ne tā men shì le hěn duō cì zuì hòu zhǎo dào le xiào guǒ zuì hǎo de fāng fǎ bǐ rú fàng duō shǎo shuǐ duō shǎo yào wú rén jī děi fēi duō gāo duō kuài děng děng jiē zhe tā men yòng wú rén jī bǎ zì jǐ jiā de mián tián sǎ le yí biàn hé yǐ qián de lǎo fāng fǎ bǐ sù dù kuài le hěn duō bèi — When she studied in Britain, Rong Mengya had played with drones. Later she saw a drone that could spray pesticide and was very interested, so she went to Shenzhen to study drone technology and, back home, bought one with her older brother. Once they had a drone, how could it spray with the best effect? They tried many times and finally found the method with the best effect, for example how much water and how much medicine to put in, how high and fast the drone must fly, and so on. Then they used the drone to spray their own family’s cotton fields once, and compared with the old method the speed was many times faster.

examples.text: 看到他们用无人机洒农药，当地很多种棉花的人也开始感兴趣了。戎梦雅就和哥哥成立了公司，又买了几台无人机，帮助别人给棉田洒药。二零一六年年底，戎梦雅和哥哥在哈密地区，给七万多亩棉田洒药，一次就赚了差不多三十万元。现在，平均每个月他们的收入都超过十万元。
examples.translation: kàn dào tā men yòng wú rén jī sǎ nóng yào dāng dì hěn duō zhòng mián huā de rén yě kāi shǐ gǎn xìng qù le róng mèng yǎ jiù hé gē gē chéng lì le gōng sī yòu mǎi le jǐ tái wú rén jī bāng zhù bié rén gěi mián tián sǎ yào èr líng yī liù nián nián dǐ róng mèng yǎ hé gē gē zài hā mì dì qū gěi qī wàn duō mǔ mián tián sǎ yào yí cì jiù zhuàn le chà bu duō sān shí wàn yuán xiàn zài píng jūn měi gè yuè tā men de shōu rù dōu chāo guò shí wàn yuán — Seeing them use drones to spray pesticide, many local cotton growers also became interested. Rong Mengya then founded a company with her brother and bought several more drones to help others spray their cotton fields. At the end of 2016, Rong Mengya and her brother sprayed more than seventy thousand mu of cotton fields in the Hami region, earning nearly three hundred thousand yuan in one go. Now their income averages over a hundred thousand yuan every month.

examples.text: 好，故事讲完了。这个故事告诉了我们什么呢？我觉得，它告诉我们，现在的年轻人非常聪明，了解的信息又多，又愿意学习最新的技术，所以他们这一代大有前途，值得我们学习。您说呢？
examples.translation: hǎo gù shì jiǎng wán le zhè ge gù shì gào sù le wǒ men shén me ne wǒ jué de tā gào sù wǒ men xiàn zài de nián qīng rén fēi cháng cōng míng liǎo jiě de xìn xī yòu duō yòu yuàn yì xué xí zuì xīn de jì shù suǒ yǐ tā men zhè yí dài dà yǒu qián tú zhí de wǒ men xué xí nín shuō ne — Well, the story is finished. What does it tell us? I think it tells us that young people today are very smart, know a lot of information and are willing to learn the latest technology, so this generation has a great future and is worth learning from. What do you think?

exercises.prompt: Where did Rong Mengya return after studying abroad?
exercises.explanation: 从英国学习结束回到新疆.

exercises.prompt: What did she help her parents grow?
What did she buy with her brother?
What share of the national cotton output does Xinjiang produce?
exercises.explanation: 全国产量的百分之八十还多.

exercises.prompt: How many times a year must the fields generally be sprayed?
exercises.explanation: 每年要给棉田要洒六次农药.

exercises.prompt: How much could be sprayed in a day with the old method?
Where did Rong Mengya learn drone technology?
exercises.explanation: 就去深圳学习了无人机技术.

exercises.prompt: How much did they earn in one go in Hami at the end of 2016?
exercises.explanation: 一次就赚了差不多三十万元.

exercises.prompt: What does the story tell us about today’s young people?
options: They are smart and worth learning from

exercises.prompt: 她看到一台能撒农药的无人___。
他们试了很多次，最后找到了效果最好的方___。

lessons.title: 746. Lesson 28 Presentation 3 using Chinese in context: nominating young entrepreneurs
lessons.subtitle: 创业明星郭浩 · 聊网创始人张林轩 · 新新小吃 · 一对一 · 精确 · 提名 · 国际青年创业者奖

explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context, Activity 3 (Reading, Writing, and Speaking)
explanations.body: You are part of an international panel that will nominate recipients for the Global Young Entrepreneurs Awards and you are in charge of the China section. A. Divide into groups of three. Members of each group read different passages below and provide a summary in Chinese. B. Share your work in your group. Compare the three cases and decide who to nominate. Rank the other two nominees. C. The whole class then discusses the nominations together. Each group explains how they came to their decision. The class picks a final nominee and decides the ranking of the other two. The three passages and my summaries:

rows: Rank (for the group to decide; no key)
Rank (for the group to decide; no key)
Rank (for the group to decide; no key)
tables.title: Activity 3B and C: choosing the nominee (the book asks the groups and the class to decide, so I give no answer)

examples.text: 郭浩是一九九零年出生的。刚上大学的时候，一天有人问他，大学毕业后你打算做什么？他想也没想就说，我要创业。为了做好创业的准备，上大学时，他利用各种机会练习演讲，提高自己交流的能力。他也努力学习各种知识，差不多每门课都考一百分，多次得到国家奖学金。后来在读研究生期间，他找了十八位同学，成立了一个移动互联网工作室，为一些大公司开发软件。后来大家都去大公司工作，离开了工作室，只有他一个人留下来，坚持创业。
examples.translation: guō hào shì yī jiǔ jiǔ líng nián chū shēng de gāng shàng dà xué de shí hòu yì tiān yǒu rén wèn tā dà xué bì yè hòu nǐ dǎ suàn zuò shén me tā xiǎng yě méi xiǎng jiù shuō wǒ yào chuàng yè wèi le zuò hǎo chuàng yè de zhǔn bèi shàng dà xué shí tā lì yòng gè zhǒng jī huì liàn xí yǎn jiǎng tí gāo zì jǐ jiāo liú de néng lì tā yě nǔ lì xué xí gè zhǒng zhī shí chà bu duō měi mén kè dōu kǎo yì bǎi fēn duō cì dé dào guó jiā jiǎng xué jīn hòu lái zài dú yán jiū shēng qī jiān tā zhǎo le shí bā wèi tóng xué chéng lì le yí gè yí dòng hù lián wǎng gōng zuò shì wèi yì xiē dà gōng sī kāi fā ruǎn jiàn hòu lái dà jiā dōu qù dà gōng sī gōng zuò lí kāi le gōng zuò shì zhǐ yǒu tā yí gè rén liú xià lái jiān chí chuàng yè — Guo Hao was born in 1990. When he had just entered university, one day someone asked him, what do you plan to do after graduating? Without thinking he said, I want to start a business. To prepare well for starting a business, at university he used every opportunity to practice speaking and improved his ability to communicate. He also studied hard in all kinds of subjects, scoring 100 in nearly every course, and received the national scholarship several times. Later, during his graduate studies, he found eighteen classmates and set up a mobile Internet studio that developed software for some big companies. Afterwards everyone went to work in big companies and left the studio; only he stayed on and persisted in his business. (Activity 3A, Passage 1: 创业明星郭浩; the book writes 1990, 100 and 18 in digits; translations mine)

examples.text: 二零一六年，郭浩在西安创建了他自己的公司。同一年，他的公司推出了一个智慧互动服务平台。他们的平台很棒，对一些高科技公司来说十分有用，但开始的时候卖得并不好。他就想办法改变销售渠道，终于让更多人熟悉、了解了他的产品，现在这个平台已经卖到全国两百多个城市，为几万家公司提供服务。几年前，他被评为西安市“创业明星。”
examples.translation: èr líng yī liù nián guō hào zài xī ān chuàng jiàn le tā zì jǐ de gōng sī tóng yì nián tā de gōng sī tuī chū le yí gè zhì huì hù dòng fú wù píng tái tā men de píng tái hěn bàng duì yì xiē gāo kē jì gōng sī lái shuō shí fēn yǒu yòng dàn kāi shǐ de shí hòu mài de bìng bù hǎo tā jiù xiǎng bàn fǎ gǎi biàn xiāo shòu qú dào zhōng yú ràng gèng duō rén shú xī liǎo jiě le tā de chǎn pǐn xiàn zài zhè ge píng tái yǐ jīng mài dào quán guó liǎng bǎi duō gè chéng shì wèi jǐ wàn jiā gōng sī tí gōng fú wù jǐ nián qián tā bèi píng wéi xī ān shì chuàng yè míng xīng — In 2016 Guo Hao founded his own company in Xi’an. In the same year his company launched a smart interactive service platform. Their platform was excellent and very useful to some high-tech companies, but at first it did not sell well. He thought of ways to change the sales channels and finally got more people familiar with and understanding his product; now this platform has sold in more than two hundred cities across the country and serves tens of thousands of companies. A few years ago he was named a “Star of Entrepreneurship” of Xi’an.

examples.text: 张林轩，今年二十岁，是聊网的创始人。他的网站为中国学生提供了一个新的学习英语的平台。现在网站还在测试，没有正式运营。从公司注册到现在半年的时间，他已经得到几百万元的投资，估计公司现在的价值已经超过一千万。
examples.translation: zhāng lín xuān jīn nián èr shí suì shì liáo wǎng de chuàng shǐ rén tā de wǎng zhàn wèi zhōng guó xué shēng tí gōng le yí gè xīn de xué xí yīng yǔ de píng tái xiàn zài wǎng zhàn hái zài cè shì méi yǒu zhèng shì yùn yíng cóng gōng sī zhù cè dào xiàn zài bàn nián de shí jiān tā yǐ jīng dé dào jǐ bǎi wàn yuán de tóu zī gū jì gōng sī xiàn zài de jià zhí yǐ jīng chāo guò yì qiān wàn — Zhang Linxuan, twenty years old this year, is the founder of Liaowang (Talkways). His website provides Chinese students a new platform for learning English. The website is still being tested and has not formally begun operating. In the half year from the company’s registration until now he has already received several million yuan in investment, and the company’s value is estimated to have exceeded ten million. (Passage 2: 聊网创始人张林轩; the book gives the site’s web address, which I leave out; the book writes 20 in digits; translations mine)

examples.text: 在他的网上，美国有名大学的学生或毕业生当老师，一对一和中国学生用英语通过视频聊天，让中国学生学习地道的英语。每次课程结束以后，学生会对老师的教学情况打分，来保证老师上课的质量。由于美国的大学生不是专业老师，他们的收费并不高，一个小时一般二十美元左右。如果是在中国，找一个外国老师上同样的课，价格要高五到十倍。
examples.translation: zài tā de wǎng shàng měi guó yǒu míng dà xué de xué shēng huò bì yè shēng dāng lǎo shī yí duì yì hé zhōng guó xué shēng yòng yīng yǔ tōng guò shì pín liáo tiān ràng zhōng guó xué shēng xué xí dì dào de yīng yǔ měi cì kè chéng jié shù yǐ hòu xué shēng huì duì lǎo shī de jiào xué qíng kuàng dǎ fēn lái bǎo zhèng lǎo shī shàng kè de zhì liàng yóu yú měi guó de dà xué shēng bú shì zhuān yè lǎo shī tā men de shōu fèi bìng bù gāo yí gè xiǎo shí yì bān èr shí měi yuán zuǒ yòu rú guǒ shì zài zhōng guó zhǎo yí gè wài guó lǎo shī shàng tóng yàng de kè jià gé yào gāo wǔ dào shí bèi — On his site, students or graduates of well-known American universities serve as teachers and chat with Chinese students one on one by video in English, letting Chinese students learn authentic English. After each class the student rates the teacher’s teaching, which ensures the quality of the teacher’s classes. Since American university students are not professional teachers, their charges are not high, generally about 20 U.S. dollars an hour. In China, finding a foreign teacher for the same class would cost five to ten times as much.

examples.text: “新新小吃”是一家开发小吃的公司。它的创始人都是九零后网络工程师，他们只懂电脑和网络，不懂小吃，但却可以做最好的小吃。
examples.translation: xīn xīn xiǎo chī shì yì jiā kāi fā xiǎo chī de gōng sī tā de chuàng shǐ rén dōu shì jiǔ líng hòu wǎng luò gōng chéng shī tā men zhǐ dǒng diàn nǎo hé wǎng luò bù dǒng xiǎo chī dàn què kě yǐ zuò zuì hǎo de xiǎo chī — “Xinxin Snacks” is a company that develops snacks. Its founders are all post-’90s network engineers who understand only computers and networks, not snacks, but can still make the best snacks. (Passage 3: 用互联网技术开发小吃的“新新小吃”公司; translations mine)

examples.text: 为了开发一种小吃，他们先分析网上的各种信息，研究小吃的成分和味道，再设计制作的过程。新产品做好以后，他们会请喜欢小吃的朋友尝一尝，他们说好吃，就继续做下去。由于他们用的机器都是用电脑控制，所以很精确，做出来的每个产品的样子和味道都是一样的。
examples.translation: wèi le kāi fā yì zhǒng xiǎo chī tā men xiān fēn xī wǎng shàng de gè zhǒng xìn xī yán jiū xiǎo chī de chéng fèn hé wèi dào zài shè jì zhì zuò de guò chéng xīn chǎn pǐn zuò hǎo yǐ hòu tā men huì qǐng xǐ huān xiǎo chī de péng yǒu cháng yì cháng tā men shuō hǎo chī jiù jì xù zuò xià qù yóu yú tā men yòng de jī qì dōu shì yòng diàn nǎo kòng zhì suǒ yǐ hěn jīng què zuò chū lái de měi gè chǎn pǐn de yàng zi hé wèi dào dōu shì yí yàng de — To develop a snack, they first analyze all kinds of information online, study the snack’s ingredients and flavor, and then design the process of making it. After a new product is made, they invite friends who like snacks to taste it, and if they say it is delicious, they carry on. Since the machines they use are all computer-controlled, they are very precise, and every product made looks and tastes the same.

examples.text: 那些很复杂特别有名的小吃他们也能做。对他们来说，只要花足够的时间，就能做出来，并且做得非常好。老百姓熟悉的一些小吃，几十年没有什么变化，而“新新小吃的”的产品，总是在改进，味道越做越好。
examples.translation: nà xiē hěn fù zá tè bié yǒu míng de xiǎo chī tā men yě néng zuò duì tā men lái shuō zhǐ yào huā zú gòu de shí jiān jiù néng zuò chū lái bìng qiě zuò de fēi cháng hǎo lǎo bǎi xìng shú xī de yì xiē xiǎo chī jǐ shí nián méi yǒu shén me biàn huà ér xīn xīn xiǎo chī de de chǎn pǐn zǒng shì zài gǎi jìn wèi dào yuè zuò yuè hǎo — They can also make those very complicated, especially famous snacks. For them, as long as they spend enough time they can make them, and make them very well. Some snacks ordinary people know have not changed in decades, while the products of “Xinxin Snacks” are always being improved and taste better and better. (the book prints “新新小吃的”的产品 with a stray 的; I print “新新小吃”的产品)

examples.text: 郭浩一九九零年出生，上大学时就想创业，努力学习，练习演讲。读研究生时他和同学成立了工作室，后来只有他留下来。二零一六年他在西安创建了公司，推出了智慧互动服务平台，改变销售渠道后，现在已经卖到全国两百多个城市。

lessons.title: 748. Lesson 28 Area Studies: the Post-’70s, ’80s, ’90s and ’00s Generations and the Eras They Grew Up In
lessons.subtitle: 七零后 · 八零后 · 九零后 · 零零后 · 后浪 · 改革开放 · 独生子女 · 铁饭碗

explanations.title: The Post-’70s Generation (七零后)
explanations.body:
The Post-’70s Generation (七零后, Qīlíng-hòu) is the generation of people born between 1970 and 1979 in Mainland China, during a dramatic transition period, from the Cultural Revolution led by Mao Zedong (1966-1976) to the “Economic Reform” led by Deng Xiaoping in 1978. The 1970s were a time of centralized economy and extreme scarcity. People lived a frugal life. Workers received low wages from the government and shopped for basic daily supplies such as rice, meat and fabric with ration tickets. Many households had access to radio but had no television. Common people had no understanding of the outside world.

Family planning was not fully implemented at this time. Most post-’70s generation have 2–3 siblings. After 1978, universities reopened and accepted students through college entrance exams, and China started to value academics again. At the time, less than 10% of examinees were accepted to colleges. Growing up between the Cultural Revolution and the era of Reform and Opening-Up, the post-’70s generation are half modern and half traditional. They pursue stable work (“iron rice bowl”) and cherish their jobs. They work hard to improve their own lives and the society. They are pragmatic and conservative.

explanations.title: The Post-’80s Generation (八零后)
explanations.body:
The Post-’80s Generation (八零后, Bālíng-hòu) is the generation of people whose members were born between 1980 and 1989 in Mainland China, after the introduction of the one-child policy. They are the first to grow up entirely within the reformist era. They have been characterized by their optimism for the future, excitement for consumerism, entrepreneurship, and acceptance of their historic role in transforming modern China into an economic superpower.

These people are also distinguished by their increased access to digital media such as computers, MP3 players and mobile phones. The post-’80s generation in China often experience a generation gap with their elders. While their parents lived during an era of famine, political instability and lack of proper education because of the Cultural Revolution, they lived in an environment of tremendous economic growth and social change, greater technology, and rigorous educational standards. This gap is noticeable in purchasing habits, career pursuits, and family interactions. Furthermore, these young adults have been indirectly affected by government restrictions to the Internet. They are also affected by China’s large socioeconomic divide between urban and rural residents and societal problems resulting from modernization.

The post-’80s generation experienced the end of government funding of college educations, job assignments for graduates and subsidized housing. Upon entering the workplace, they had to face financial pressures such as marriage and home purchases. The majority of the post-’80s generation were more willing to find jobs that are stable, with strong continuity and matching what they studied in school, and that can satisfy their parents. They believed government agencies, institutions, and state-owned enterprises had more advantages in social resources and development prospects. Many of them have not yet had a strong entrepreneurial impulse.

explanations.title: The Post-’90s Generation (九零后)
explanations.body:
The Post-’90s Generation (九零后, Jiǔlíng-hòu) is the generation of people born between 1990 and 1999. They are the second generation of Chinese people to grow up without siblings and the first generation to be born after the Tiananmen protests. Unlike the post-’80s generation, who witnessed a glimpse of pre-affluent China in the late 1980s and 1990s, they have not experienced historical and political turmoil, and have not experienced major economic fluctuations. The post-’90s generation were born in the era of rapid development of information and innovation, so they pursue individuality and freedom. They grew up being appreciated and encouraged since they were young. They are alleged to have traits that are similar to the post-’80s generation, such as “Little Emperor Syndrome” and a knack for information technology and capitalism, but in a more highly developed way.

In an era where mainstream social thought is more dispersed, factions are more diverse, and ideas are updated more rapidly, they are more focused on their own hobbies in their work and prefer to do what they want to do and what they are good at. They want to find jobs that they like, that are challenging, and where they can realize their self-worth, so they become people who do not like to “put up with” just any job.

The post-’90s generation are also alleged to have less of a sense of hierarchy in the workplace and more of a sense of individuality compared to older generations. With financial support from their parents, the post-’90s generation are more inclined to be able to use their personal skills and talents. They prefer jobs that can satisfy personality development and being appreciated by employers. Even though civil servants and public institutions are still good choices and attract many post-’90s generation applicants, many also choose private enterprise, entrepreneurship, going abroad or working alone. Their advantage lies in their active thinking, natural sensitivity, and dependence on new things, especially the Internet. They don’t like too much restraint, suppression, or repeated mechanized labor, and they respect entrepreneurial heroes. They will freely switch to a new job with a better working environment and room for development or leave to start their own business.

explanations.title: The Post-’00s Generation (零零后)
explanations.body:
The Post-’00s Generation (零零后, Línglíng-hòu) is the generation of people born after the year 2000, in an era that had the highest GDP per capita and lowest birth rate and enjoyed the most abundance in China. They are the “mobile internet generation”. Many of them have opportunities to visit other countries; and they are able to learn about other cultures through the Internet. Mostly born into 421-format families, they may not be a single child anymore.

Surveys indicate that most of them identify their interests and hobbies early and know how to use online resources to deepen their knowledge of a specific field. They value in-depth understanding of a certain field much more than consumption or career growth, which is a departure from naked materialism. They love to connect with peers and are able to respect and adapt to different points of view. Equality is highly important for China’s post-’00s generation. Compared to previous generations, they care much less about what authorities and experts say. They study more hours than all generations before and with a more pragmatic motivation.

They want jobs that can express their personal values, with a high income and a sense of style. They also want a comfortable environment and friendly and simple interpersonal relationships. They will not obey leaders absolutely but like to keep their personal ideas and opinions. They are less concerned about job stability. The job replacement rate and mobility for this group is high.

explanations.title: A Chinese Internet Meme: 后浪 Waves Behind
explanations.body:
A poem quoted from a Song dynasty book said, “As in the Yangtze River, the waves behind ride on the ones before: The new generation replaces the old.” The metaphor of wave has been used to describe the phenomena of how the new generation exceeds the old.

On the May Fourth Youth Day in 2020, Chinese video sharing website Bilibili and a number of mainland Chinese media sites jointly launched a promotional video “Waves Behind 后浪.” The 3 minute and 52 second video shows the actor He Bing expressing envy, recognition, encouragement, and other positive emotions to the younger generation. The video caused controversy after it was aired and became a Chinese internet meme.

Learning Objectives (the overview of the unit follows in the table):

1. Upon completion of this lesson, you will be able to talk about: the rapid growth of hobby classes in China; the value of children’s education in China: its traditions, family investment, and related negative issues; the difficulties in education faced by children left behind in rural areas, and the village children who migrate to cities.

2. To perform the above you must master the following: new words and phrases associated with the above functions; using 当然 as a concession conjunction word; using 吧 to express the indefinite tone; using directional complements 下去 and 下来 to express continuation of an action; complement: Verb + 得 + 过来, 上不起, 比不上; the structure 用在…上; the structure 在…的同时; using 好 to express purpose; structure 再…也… for determination; the 只好 + Verb phrase.

explanations.title: Presentation 1: an interview at the Children’s Palace
explanations.body: A reporter interviews Director Wang about the many children who attend interest classes.

examples.text: 记者：王主任，谢谢您接受我们的采访。现在到少年宫参加兴趣班的孩子有多少？
examples.translation: jì zhě wáng zhǔ rèn xiè xiè nín jiē shòu wǒ men de cǎi fǎng xiàn zài dào shào nián gōng cān jiā xìng qù bān de hái zi yǒu duō shǎo — Reporter: Director Wang, thank you for accepting our interview. How many children now come to the Children’s Palace to attend interest classes? (Presentation 1; translations mine; the traditional-character copy is not repeated)

examples.text: 王主任：平时周末有五千多人，暑假要更多一些。
examples.translation: wáng zhǔ rèn píng shí zhōu mò yǒu wǔ qiān duō rén shǔ jià yào gèng duō yì xiē — Director Wang: Usually on weekends there are over five thousand, and in the summer holidays there are more. (the book writes 5000 in digits)

examples.text: 记者：这么多啊？
examples.translation: jì zhě zhè me duō a — Reporter: That many?

examples.text: 王主任：我们这儿还是少的呢，有些大城市的少年宫，每个周末都有三四万孩子。
examples.translation: wáng zhǔ rèn wǒ men zhèr hái shì shǎo de ne yǒu xiē dà chéng shì de shào nián gōng měi gè zhōu mò dōu yǒu sān sì wàn hái zi — Director Wang: Here it’s still few; at some big cities’ children’s palaces there are thirty or forty thousand children every weekend.

examples.text: 记者：上兴趣班的孩子怎么这么多呢？
examples.translation: jì zhě shàng xìng qù bān de hái zi zěn me zhè me duō ne — Reporter: Why are there so many children attending interest classes?

examples.text: 王主任：我想主要是人们都有钱了，另外也希望孩子有更多的兴趣和爱好。
examples.translation: wáng zhǔ rèn wǒ xiǎng zhǔ yào shì rén men dōu yǒu qián le lìng wài yě xī wàng hái zi yǒu gèng duō de xìng qù hé ài hào — Director Wang: I think mainly it’s that people all have money now, and they also hope their children have more interests and hobbies.

examples.text: 记者：我也觉得，现在的父母不像以前，只关心孩子的学习成绩了。
examples.translation: jì zhě wǒ yě jué de xiàn zài de fù mǔ bú xiàng yǐ qián zhǐ guān xīn hái zi de xué xí chéng jì le — Reporter: I feel so too; today’s parents are not like before, caring only about their children’s grades.

examples.text: 王主任：是啊。培养兴趣对孩子的发展很有好处。而且有了特长，在升学考试的时候还可以加分。
examples.translation: wáng zhǔ rèn shì a péi yǎng xìng qù duì hái zi de fā zhǎn hěn yǒu hǎo chù ér qiě yǒu le tè cháng zài shēng xué kǎo shì de shí hòu hái kě yǐ jiā fēn — Director Wang: Yes. Cultivating interests is very good for a child’s development. Besides, with a special skill, one can also get extra points in the entrance exams.

examples.text: 记者：你们都有些什么样的兴趣班呢？
examples.translation: jì zhě nǐ men dōu yǒu xiē shén me yàng de xìng qù bān ne — Reporter: What kinds of interest classes do you have?

examples.text: 王主任：各种各样的班都有，像音乐、舞蹈、画画、武术什么的。
examples.translation: wáng zhǔ rèn gè zhǒng gè yàng de bān dōu yǒu xiàng yīn yuè wǔ dǎo huà huà wǔ shù shén me de — Director Wang: All kinds of classes, such as music, dance, drawing, martial arts and so on.

examples.text: 记者：你们怎么收费？
examples.translation: jì zhě nǐ men zěn me shōu fèi — Reporter: How do you charge?

examples.text: 王主任：我们收费比外面低得多，上一个班一年三千元左右吧。
examples.translation: wáng zhǔ rèn wǒ men shōu fèi bǐ wài miàn dī de duō shàng yí gè bān yì nián sān qiān yuán zuǒ yòu ba — Director Wang: Our fees are much lower than outside; one class costs about three thousand yuan a year.

examples.translation: jì zhě tīng shuō yǒu xiē jiā zhǎng xǐ huān hé bié rén bǐ huì tóng shí gěi hái zi bào hǎo jǐ gè bān — Reporter: I hear some parents like to compare with others and sign their children up for quite a few classes at the same time.

lessons.title: 750. Lesson 29 Presentation 1 grammar: the concessive use of 当然
lessons.subtitle: 当然 · 后置的当然 · 前置的当然 · 但是/可是/不过 · 当然也可以 · 当然很重要，但是

explanations.title: The concessive use of 当然
explanations.body: In conversation or discourse, the “当然 clause” provides a concessional tone to the main opinion of the speaker. There are two types: 1) post-main clause use, and 2) pre-main clause use. Post-main clause use: this type of 当然 clause offers a secondary choice or opinion to the speaker’s main notion to soften the tone (main clause + 当然 clause). Pre-main clause use: in conversation, the pre-main clause 当然 is often used to acknowledge the other speaker’s opinion or a common opinion first, then offer a contradicting opinion of the main speaker, so as to make this opinion less forceful and offer a concessionary tone (当然 clause + adversative conjunction (但是/可是/不过) + main clause).

examples.text: 买高铁票很方便，你可以在网上或者在手机上预订，当然也可以直接到火车站去买。
examples.translation: mǎi gāo tiě piào hěn fāng biàn nǐ kě yǐ zài wǎng shàng huò zhě zài shǒu jī shàng yù dìng dāng rán yě kě yǐ zhí jiē dào huǒ chē zhàn qù mǎi — Post-main clause use (a 当然 clause that offers a secondary choice to soften the tone: main clause + 当然 clause), 1: Buying high-speed rail tickets is very convenient; you can book online or on your phone, and of course you can also go straight to the train station to buy. (translations mine)

examples.text: 这代年轻人又有知识又有能力，当然，他们也有一些不足的地方，比如生活能力就不太强。
examples.translation: zhè dài nián qīng rén yòu yǒu zhī shí yòu yǒu néng lì dāng rán tā men yě yǒu yì xiē bù zú de dì fāng bǐ rú shēng huó néng lì jiù bú tài qiáng — 2: This generation of young people has both knowledge and ability; of course they also have some shortcomings, for example their ability to take care of themselves is not strong.

examples.text: 家长们通常会给孩子报两三个兴趣班，当然，也有选七八个的。
examples.translation: jiā zhǎng men tōng cháng huì gěi hái zi bào liǎng sān gè xìng qù bān dāng rán yě yǒu xuǎn qī bā gè de — 3: Parents usually sign their children up for two or three interest classes, though of course some choose seven or eight.

examples.text: 钱当然很重要，但我觉得，生活中还应该有些别的什么。
examples.translation: qián dāng rán hěn zhòng yào dàn wǒ jué de shēng huó zhōng hái yīng gāi yǒu xiē bié de shén me — Pre-main clause use (the 当然 clause acknowledges the other’s or a common opinion first, then an adversative conjunction 但是/可是/不过 and the main clause), 1: Money is of course important, but I think life should have something else too.

examples.text: 重视孩子的教育当然是好的，但家长们也应该重视孩子们的身心健康。
examples.translation: zhòng shì hái zi de jiào yù dāng rán shì hǎo de dàn jiā zhǎng men yě yīng gāi zhòng shì hái zi men de shēn xīn jiàn kāng — 2: Valuing children’s education is of course good, but parents should also value their children’s physical and mental health.

explanations.title: Activities 1 to 3
explanations.body: Activity 1 (Reading): Translate the following sentences into English. Note the function of 当然 in each sentence. Activity 2 (Speaking): Create sentences with the concessive 当然, using the pictures for reference (1. Exercise 2. Learning Chinese 3. Join military 4. Order fast food 5. Self-driving car 6. Traveling abroad). Make sure you use both pre-main and post-main clauses in your sentences. Pair up and share your work with your partner. Activity 3 (Speaking): A. Pair up. Student A makes a statement. Student B acknowledges it with 当然, then uses 但是/可是/不过 to add a contradictory idea to it. Then, switch roles. B. Work with your partner to find common ideas, then use 当然 to add secondary thoughts to the ideas. The sentences, my translations and samples:

examples.text: 明天的比赛输赢都没有关系，大家努力就行了。当然，能赢最好。
examples.translation: míng tiān de bǐ sài shū yíng dōu méi yǒu guān xì dà jiā nǔ lì jiù xíng le dāng rán néng yíng zuì hǎo — Activity 1, 1 (translations mine; note the function of 当然, a post-main clause use): Whether we win or lose tomorrow’s match doesn’t matter; it’s enough for everyone to try hard. Of course, winning would be best.

examples.text: 成熟的男人喜欢聪明的女人，当然，如果同时长得也漂亮，就更好了。
examples.translation: chéng shú de nán rén xǐ huān cōng míng de nǚ rén dāng rán rú guǒ tóng shí zhǎng de yě piào liàng jiù gèng hǎo le — 2 (post-main): Mature men like clever women; of course, if she is also good-looking at the same time, so much the better.

examples.text: 我们相信美国会做正确的事，当然，是在她试过别的一切可能以后。
examples.translation: wǒ men xiāng xìn měi guó huì zuò zhèng què de shì dāng rán shì zài tā shì guò bié de yí qiè kě néng yǐ hòu — 3 (post-main): We believe America will do the right thing, of course after she has tried every other possibility.

examples.text: 孩子听话当然是好事，但是你也要看他在听话的同时是不是快乐。
examples.translation: hái zi tīng huà dāng rán shì hǎo shì dàn shì nǐ yě yào kàn tā zài tīng huà de tóng shí shì bú shì kuài lè — 4 (pre-main): A child being obedient is of course a good thing, but you should also see whether he is happy while being obedient.

examples.text: 一个人说什么当然重要，但更重要的是他做什么，怎么做。
examples.translation: yí gè rén shuō shén me dāng rán zhòng yào dàn gèng zhòng yào de shì tā zuò shén me zěn me zuò — 5 (pre-main): What a person says is of course important, but more important is what he does and how.

examples.text: 我每天都锻炼身体，当然，有时候太忙了就不去。
examples.translation: wǒ měi tiān dōu duàn liàn shēn tǐ dāng rán yǒu shí hòu tài máng le jiù bú qù — Activity 2, picture 1 Exercise (my sentence, post-main): I exercise every day, though of course when I’m too busy sometimes I don’t go.

examples.text: 学中文当然很难，但是我觉得很有意思。
examples.translation: xué zhōng wén dāng rán hěn nán dàn shì wǒ jué de hěn yǒu yì si — 2 Learning Chinese (my sentence, pre-main): Learning Chinese is of course hard, but I find it very interesting.

examples.text: 参军很辛苦，当然，也可以学到很多东西。
examples.translation: cān jūn hěn xīn kǔ dāng rán yě kě yǐ xué dào hěn duō dōng xī — 3 Join military (my sentence, post-main): Joining the military is hard work, though of course one can also learn a lot.

examples.text: 快餐当然方便，但是吃得太多对身体不好。
examples.translation: kuài cān dāng rán fāng biàn dàn shì chī de tài duō duì shēn tǐ bù hǎo — 4 Order fast food (my sentence, pre-main): Fast food is of course convenient, but eating too much is bad for the body.

examples.text: 自动驾驶汽车当然很先进，但是我还是有点儿担心。
examples.translation: zì dòng jià shǐ qì chē dāng rán hěn xiān jìn dàn shì wǒ hái shì yǒu diǎnr dān xīn — 5 Self-driving car (my sentence, pre-main): Self-driving cars are of course advanced, but I’m still a bit worried.

examples.text: 出国旅游很有意思，当然，也要花很多钱。
examples.translation: chū guó lǚ yóu hěn yǒu yì si dāng rán yě yào huā hěn duō qián — 6 Traveling abroad (my sentence, post-main): Traveling abroad is a lot of fun, though of course it also costs a lot of money. (the pictures are not included, so these sentences are only my samples)

examples.text: 要学好中文，背生词很重要。
examples.translation: yào xué hǎo zhōng wén bèi shēng cí hěn zhòng yào — Activity 3A, the book’s example. Student A: To learn Chinese well, memorizing new words is very important.

examples.text: 背生词当然很重要，但是，不要忘了多读多听真实语料。
examples.translation: bèi shēng cí dāng rán hěn zhòng yào dàn shì bú yào wàng le duō dú duō tīng zhēn shí yǔ liào — Student B: Memorizing new words is of course very important, but don’t forget to read and listen to a lot of authentic material.

examples.text: 想减肥就要少吃。
examples.translation: xiǎng jiǎn féi jiù yào shǎo chī — Activity 3B, the book’s example. Common idea: If you want to lose weight, you must eat less.

examples.text: 想减肥就要少吃，当然，锻炼也很重要。
examples.translation: xiǎng jiǎn féi jiù yào shǎo chī dāng rán duàn liàn yě hěn zhòng yào — Response: If you want to lose weight you must eat less; of course, exercise is also important.

examples.text: 想减肥就要少吃，当然，吃得太少对身体也不好。
examples.translation: xiǎng jiǎn féi jiù yào shǎo chī dāng rán chī de tài shǎo duì shēn tǐ yě bù hǎo — Or: … of course, eating too little is also bad for the body.

examples.text: 在中国学中文最好，当然，在别的地方也可以。
examples.translation: zài zhōng guó xué zhōng wén zuì hǎo dāng rán zài bié de dì fāng yě kě yǐ — My sample (3A, student A): Studying Chinese in China is best, though of course you can also do it elsewhere.

lessons.title: 751. Lesson 29 Presentation 1 grammar: 过来 as a resultative complement
lessons.subtitle: 走过来 · 改过来 · 学得过来 · 忙不过来 · 明白过来 · 暖和不过来

explanations.title: 过来 as resultative complements
explanations.body: When used as a resultative complement, 过来 has three meanings: (1) movement in a direction, (2) change of state, and (3) degree of feasibility. Activity 4 (Reading): Translate the following sentences into English. Activity 5 (Reading and Speaking): Use the images to complete the sentences. Share your work with the class. The five beginnings are: 1. 天上的星星 2. 你买这么多书, 3. 以后的知识越来越多, 4. 他说了半天, 5. 这么多孩子, The examples, my translations and my completions:

headers: Meaning of 过来 as a resultative complement
rows: Change of state (figurative meaning, usually indicating a return to an original, normal, and typically improved state)
Degree of feasibility (figurative meaning, with sufficiency of time, ability to manage something, usually used in negative or interrogative sentences)
tables.title: 过来 as resultative complements: when used as a resultative complement, 过来 has three meanings

examples.text: 她向我走过来。

examples.translation: gōng zuò zhè me duō yí gè rén gēn běn máng bú guò lái — 2: There is so much work that one person simply can’t manage it all.

examples.translation: děng tā míng bái guò lái yǐ jīng tài wǎn le — 3: By the time he realized (came to understand), it was already too late.

examples.text: 我的手很冷，半天也暖和不过来。
examples.translation: wǒ de shǒu hěn lěng bàn tiān yě nuǎn huo bú guò lái — 4: My hands are very cold and haven’t warmed up for ages.

examples.text: 事情不多，我一个人也忙得过来。

examples.text: 他说了半天，我还没明白过来。

lessons.title: 752. Lesson 29 Presentation 1 grammar: 下来 vs. 下去, and the potential complement 得下去 / 不下去
lessons.subtitle: 坚持下来 · 坚持下去 · 活下来 · 学下去 · 看得下去 · 住不下去了 · 胖下去

explanations.title: 下来 vs. 下去
explanations.body: When 下来 and 下去 are used as directional complements, they can indicate the continuation of an action. “Verb + 下来” means an action was started in the past and continues until the present; it was not easy, but it was completed. “Verb + 下去” means an action has begun and will continue. The verbs commonly used include 坚持, 活, 保存, 学, 跑, etc., usually preceded by a modal auxiliary verb like 要, 想, 能, 一定, 应该, or an adverb that indicates time, like 再, 又, 接着, 继续, etc. Potential complement form of 下去: it means “able to go on” / “can’t go on” (doing something). Affirmative: Verb + 得 + 下去; negative: Verb + 不 + 下去 (+ 了). 了 is often used at the end of the negative sentence.

headers: Potential complement form of 下去 (“able to go on” / “can’t go on”; 了 is often used at the end of the negative sentence)

examples.text: 大卫很喜欢汉语，他还想继续学下去。

examples.text: 甲：这本书这么难，你看得下去吗？

examples.text: 这儿太冷了，我住不下去了。

examples.text: 我跟他过不下去了，我要离婚！

examples.translation: wǒ bù néng zài zhè yàng pàng xià qù le wǒ yào jiǎn féi — Note: “Adjective + 下去” indicates a state that has existed and will continue to develop, usually with a negative connotation. For example: I can’t keep getting fatter like this; I’m going to lose weight!

examples.translation: xiàn zài cái liù yuè tiān qì hái huì rè xià qù — It is only June now, and the weather will keep getting hotter.

lessons.title: 753. Lesson 29 Presentation 1 grammar: 吧 to express an indefinite tone, and the different uses of 吧
lessons.subtitle: 左右吧 · 还可以吧 · 不太好吧 · 我们走吧 · 还是…吧 · 好吧 · 一定…吧？ · 那我…吧

explanations.title: 吧 to express an indefinite tone
explanations.body: The particle 吧 can be used to express an indefinite tone, either to convey a real sense of uncertainty or to soften a comment to make it more polite, gentle, and less forceful. Activity 7 (Speaking): What would you say in the following situations? Share your work with a classmate. 1. Your friend suggests a party with liquor, although there are attendees under 21. 2. Your friend asks how far it is from Monterey to Los Angeles. 3. Your friend asks how much your pay is. 4. Your friend asks if you are stressed from your studies. 5. Your friend asks how many bus stops there are from DLI to Del Monte Shopping Center. The examples and my sample replies:

examples.text: 甲：你们怎么收费？
examples.translation: jiǎ nǐ men zěn me shōu fèi — 1. A: How do you charge? (the particle 吧 expresses an indefinite tone, to convey real uncertainty or to soften a comment; translations mine)

examples.text: 乙：我们收费比外面低得多，上一个班一年三千元左右吧。
examples.translation: yǐ wǒ men shōu fèi bǐ wài miàn dī de duō shàng yí gè bān yì nián sān qiān yuán zuǒ yòu ba — B: Our fees are much lower than outside, about three thousand yuan a year for one class, I’d say.

examples.text: 甲：听说有些家长喜欢和别人比，会同时给孩子报好几个班。
examples.translation: jiǎ tīng shuō yǒu xiē jiā zhǎng xǐ huān hé bié rén bǐ huì tóng shí gěi hái zi bào hǎo jǐ gè bān — 2. A: I hear some parents like to compare with others and sign their children up for quite a few classes at the same time.

examples.text: 乙：一般也就两三个吧。
examples.translation: yǐ yì bān yě jiù liǎng sān gè ba — B: Generally just two or three, I’d say.

examples.text: 甲：他这次考得怎么样？
examples.translation: jiǎ tā zhè cì kǎo de zěn me yàng — 3. A: How did he do on the exam this time?

examples.text: 乙：还可以吧。
examples.translation: yǐ hái kě yǐ ba — B: Not bad, I guess.

examples.text: 甲：那个送快递的晚了五分钟，我要给他差评！
examples.translation: jiǎ nà ge sòng kuài dì de wǎn le wǔ fēn zhōng wǒ yào gěi tā chà píng — 4. A: That delivery man was five minutes late; I’m going to give him a bad review!

examples.text: 乙：这样做不太好吧。
examples.translation: yǐ zhè yàng zuò bú tài hǎo ba — B: Doing that isn’t quite right, is it?

examples.text: 甲：这个题是这样做吗？
examples.translation: jiǎ zhè ge tí shì zhè yàng zuò ma — 5. A: Is this problem done this way?

examples.text: 乙：应该是吧。
examples.translation: yǐ yīng gāi shì ba — B: It should be, I think.

examples.text: 这样做不太好吧。
examples.translation: zhè yàng zuò bú tài hǎo ba — Activity 7, 1 (my sample reply; liquor at a party with guests under 21): That isn’t quite right, is it?

examples.text: 大概五百公里吧。
examples.translation: dà gài wǔ bǎi gōng lǐ ba — 2 (my sample; how far from Monterey to Los Angeles): About five hundred kilometers, I’d say.

examples.text: 不太多，够用吧。
examples.translation: bú tài duō gòu yòng ba — 3 (my sample; how much is your pay): Not much; enough to get by, I guess.

examples.text: 还可以吧。
examples.translation: hái kě yǐ ba — 4 (my sample; are you stressed from your studies): It’s okay, I guess.

examples.text: 我想想，大概两三站吧。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎng xiǎng dà gài liǎng sān zhàn ba — 5 (my sample; how many bus stops from school to the shopping center): Let me think, perhaps two or three stops.

explanations.title: Different uses of 吧
explanations.body: 1. Making suggestions. 2. 还是…吧 indicates a selected choice or a preference. 3. To concede a point. 4. To form an indefinite tone. 5. To seek confirmation of assumed information or thoughts. 6. To respond with a decision after giving thought to the other speaker’s question, request, or proposal. Activity 8 (Listening and Speaking): Listen to a short dialog and explain the function of 吧 in each sentence (six audio items, which are not included, so I give no key). Activity 9 (Reading and Speaking): Complete the sentences using the tone in parentheses. Share your work with your partner. The examples and my completions:

examples.text: 我们走吧！
examples.translation: wǒ men zǒu ba — Different uses of 吧, 1. Making suggestions (吧 makes a suggestion more tentative and polite): Let’s go! (translations mine)

examples.text: 今天天气不太好，我们还是明天去吧。
examples.translation: jīn tiān tiān qì bú tài hǎo wǒ men hái shì míng tiān qù ba — 2. 还是…吧 indicates a selected choice or a preference: The weather isn’t good today; we had better go tomorrow.

examples.text: 甲：这件太贵了！
examples.translation: jiǎ zhè jiàn tài guì le — 3. To concede a point (to accept or agree with something you’re not particularly happy about). A: This one is too expensive!

examples.text: 乙：好吧，那就别买了。
examples.translation: yǐ hǎo ba nà jiù bié mǎi le — B: All right then, let’s not buy it.

examples.text: 我们收费比外面低得多，上一个班一年三千元左右吧。
examples.translation: wǒ men shōu fèi bǐ wài miàn dī de duō shàng yí gè bān yì nián sān qiān yuán zuǒ yòu ba — 4. To form an indefinite tone: Our fees are much lower than outside, about three thousand yuan a year for one class, I’d say.

examples.text: 你的中文说得非常好，一定有很多学习体会吧？
examples.translation: nǐ de zhōng wén shuō de fēi cháng hǎo yí dìng yǒu hěn duō xué xí tǐ huì ba — 5. To seek confirmation of assumed information or thoughts: Your Chinese is excellent; you must have a lot of learning experience, right?

examples.text: 甲：今天美元对人民币的兑换率是一比六点九。
examples.translation: jiǎ jīn tiān měi yuán duì rén mín bì de duì huàn lǜ shì yì bǐ liù diǎn jiǔ — 6. To respond with a decision after giving thought to the other speaker’s question, request or proposal. A: Today’s exchange rate of the U.S. dollar to the renminbi is one to six point nine.

examples.text: 乙：那我换三百美元吧。
examples.translation: yǐ nà wǒ huàn sān bǎi měi yuán ba — B: Then I’ll change three hundred dollars.

examples.text: 甲：我每天早上五点起床。
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ měi tiān zǎo shàng wǔ diǎn qǐ chuáng — 2 (confirm an assumption; my completion). A: I get up at five o’clock every morning.

examples.text: 乙：你一定很早睡觉吧？
examples.translation: yǐ nǐ yí dìng hěn zǎo shuì jiào ba — B: You must go to bed very early, right?

examples.text: 我们的蔬菜很新鲜，你买一点吧。
examples.translation: wǒ men de shū cài hěn xīn xiān nǐ mǎi yì diǎn ba — Activity 9, 1 (suggestion; my completion): Our vegetables are very fresh; why not buy some? (translations mine)

examples.text: 甲：聚会什么时候开始？
examples.translation: jiǎ jù huì shén me shí hòu kāi shǐ — 3 (estimation; my completion). A: When does the party start?

examples.text: 乙：大概七点吧。
examples.translation: yǐ dà gài qī diǎn ba — B: Around seven, I’d say.

examples.text: 甲：你要存定期还是活期？
examples.translation: jiǎ nǐ yào cún dìng qī hái shì huó qī — 4 (come to a decision; my completion). A: Do you want a fixed deposit or a current one?

examples.text: 乙：那我存活期吧。
examples.translation: yǐ nà wǒ cún huó qī ba — B: Then I’ll take a current one.

examples.text: 甲：我在准备考试呢。
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ zài zhǔn bèi kǎo shì ne — 5 (preference; my completion). A: I’m preparing for an exam.

examples.text: 乙：那你还是明天再来吧。
examples.translation: yǐ nà nǐ hái shì míng tiān zài lái ba — B: Then you had better come tomorrow.

examples.text: 甲：我太累了，不想做饭。
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ tài lèi le bù xiǎng zuò fàn — 6 (concession; my completion). A: I’m too tired and don’t want to cook.

examples.text: 乙：好吧，那我们出去吃吧。
examples.translation: yǐ hǎo ba nà wǒ men chū qù chī ba — B: All right, then let’s eat out.

examples.text: 我以前也不想给孩子报那么多兴趣班，只要她健康快乐就行了。但是看看周围同事们的孩子，从小就上各种兴趣班，我就开始担心自己的孩子了，怕她只知道玩儿，别的什么也不会。所以在我女儿两岁半的时候，我给她报了英语班，后来又报了钢琴班和舞蹈班。所有的兴趣班都是我们家长选的，这么小的孩子也不知道喜欢什么不喜欢什么。兴趣爱好都是要培养的，她学着学着就会感兴趣了。
examples.translation: wǒ yǐ qián yě bù xiǎng gěi hái zi bào nà me duō xìng qù bān zhǐ yào tā jiàn kāng kuài lè jiù xíng le dàn shì kàn kàn zhōu wéi tóng shì men de hái zi cóng xiǎo jiù shàng gè zhǒng xìng qù bān wǒ jiù kāi shǐ dān xīn zì jǐ de hái zi le pà tā zhǐ zhī dào wánr bié de shén me yě bú huì suǒ yǐ zài wǒ nǚ ér liǎng suì bàn de shí hòu wǒ gěi tā bào le yīng yǔ bān hòu lái yòu bào le gāng qín bān hé wǔ dǎo bān suǒ yǒu de xìng qù bān dōu shì wǒ men jiā zhǎng xuǎn de zhè me xiǎo de hái zi yě bù zhī dào xǐ huān shén me bù xǐ huān shén me xìng qù ài hào dōu shì yào péi yǎng de tā xué zhe xué zhe jiù huì gǎn xìng qù le — I used not to want to sign my child up for so many interest classes either; it was enough for her to be healthy and happy. But looking at my colleagues’ children, who attended all kinds of interest classes from an early age, I began to worry about my own child, afraid she would only know how to play and nothing else. So when my daughter was two and a half I signed her up for an English class, and later for piano and dance classes. All the interest classes were chosen by us parents; such a small child doesn’t know what she likes or dislikes. Interests and hobbies have to be cultivated; as she keeps studying she will become interested. (Activity 2A, an interview; translation mine)

examples.text: 小孩子放暑假在家里，除了写作业就是上网玩儿游戏。给他们报兴趣班，可以丰富生活。两个孩子都报了音乐班，另外，男孩报了武术，女孩报了舞蹈。他们都很喜欢来这里上课。有时候还会去参加一些演出活动，对小孩子的成长很有好处，增加了他们的学习兴趣，认识了很多新朋友。我们也不会给孩子什么压力，每天练习半个小时左右，作业少的时候就多练一点。
examples.translation: xiǎo hái zi fàng shǔ jià zài jiā lǐ chú le xiě zuò yè jiù shì shàng wǎng wánr yóu xì gěi tā men bào xìng qù bān kě yǐ fēng fù shēng huó liǎng gè hái zi dōu bào le yīn yuè bān lìng wài nán hái bào le wǔ shù nǚ hái bào le wǔ dǎo tā men dōu hěn xǐ huān lái zhè lǐ shàng kè yǒu shí hòu hái huì qù cān jiā yì xiē yǎn chū huó dòng duì xiǎo hái zi de chéng zhǎng hěn yǒu hǎo chù zēng jiā le tā men de xué xí xìng qù rèn shí le hěn duō xīn péng yǒu wǒ men yě bú huì gěi hái zi shén me yā lì měi tiān liàn xí bàn gè xiǎo shí zuǒ yòu zuò yè shǎo de shí hòu jiù duō liàn yì diǎn — When children are at home on summer vacation, besides doing homework they just play games online. Signing them up for interest classes can enrich their lives. Both children signed up for a music class, and in addition the boy signed up for martial arts and the girl for dance. They both like coming here to class. Sometimes they also take part in some performances, which is very good for little children’s growth, increases their interest in learning and lets them meet many new friends. We also don’t put any pressure on the children; they practice about half an hour a day, and more when there is less homework. (Activity 2C; translation mine)

examples.text: 我觉得她这样做有她的道理，但是应该多听听孩子自己的想法。
examples.translation: wǒ jué de tā zhè yàng zuò yǒu tā de dào lǐ dàn shì yīng gāi duō tīng tīng hái zi zì jǐ de xiǎng fǎ — Activity 2A (a sample of what I think of the mother’s decision, my own view; the activity asks for the learner’s opinion): I think she has her reasons, but should listen more to the child’s own ideas.

examples.text: 两个孩子都报了音乐班，男孩还报了武术，女孩还报了舞蹈。
examples.translation: liǎng gè hái zi dōu bào le yīn yuè bān nán hái huán bào le wǔ shù nǚ hái huán bào le wǔ dǎo — Activity 2C-1 (my answer): Both children take music; the boy also takes martial arts and the girl dance.

examples.text: 可以丰富生活，对小孩子的成长很有好处，增加他们的学习兴趣，认识很多新朋友。
examples.translation: kě yǐ fēng fù shēng huó duì xiǎo hái zi de chéng zhǎng hěn yǒu hǎo chù zēng jiā tā men de xué xí xìng qù rèn shí hěn duō xīn péng yǒu — 2C-2 (my answer): It enriches their lives, is good for their growth, increases their interest in learning and lets them meet new friends.

examples.text: 他们都很喜欢，因为他们很喜欢来这里上课，家长也不给他们什么压力。
examples.translation: tā men dōu hěn xǐ huān yīn wèi tā men hěn xǐ huān lái zhè lǐ shàng kè jiā zhǎng yě bù gěi tā men shén me yā lì — 2C-3 (my answer): Yes, they like it, because they like coming to class here and the parents put no pressure on them.

examples.text: 在参访中，我们见到一位父亲，他去年花在孩子兴趣班上的钱有很大一部分是借来的。这位父亲说，孩子喜欢弹钢琴，跟着当地一位非常有名的钢琴大师学习，学费很高。但是这位父亲觉得，衣食住行都可以省，孩子教育不能省，他说：“很多东西比钱更重要，要学就学最好的。”
examples.translation: zài cān fǎng zhōng wǒ men jiàn dào yí wèi fù qīn tā qù nián huā zài hái zi xìng qù bān shàng de qián yǒu hěn dà yí bù fèn shì jiè lái de zhè wèi fù qīn shuō hái zi xǐ huān tán gāng qín gēn zhe dāng dì yí wèi fēi cháng yǒu míng de gāng qín dà shī xué xí xué fèi hěn gāo dàn shì zhè wèi fù qīn jué de yī shí zhù xíng dōu kě yǐ shěng hái zi jiào yù bù néng shěng tā shuō hěn duō dōng xī bǐ qián gèng zhòng yào yào xué jiù xué zuì hǎo de — During our visit we met a father, a large part of the money he spent last year on his child’s interest classes was borrowed. This father said his child likes playing the piano and studies with a very famous local piano master, and the tuition is very high. But this father feels that food, clothing, housing and transport can all be economized on, whereas a child’s education cannot be; he said, “Many things are more important than money; if you study, study with the best.” (Activity 3A; the book numbers and underlines three expressions: 1) 借来的, 2) 大师, 3) 衣食住行; translation mine)

examples.text: 他的态度是：衣食住行都可以省，孩子教育不能省。我同意他，因为教育对孩子的将来很重要；可是，借钱让孩子学钢琴，家里压力也不小。
examples.translation: tā de tài dù shì yī shí zhù xíng dōu kě yǐ shěng hái zi jiào yù bù néng shěng wǒ tóng yì tā yīn wèi jiào yù duì hái zi de jiāng lái hěn zhòng yào kě shì jiè qián ràng hái zi xué gāng qín jiā lǐ yā lì yě bù xiǎo — Activity 3B (a sample of my own view; the activity asks the learner to agree or disagree): His attitude is that food, clothing, housing and transport can be economized on but a child’s education cannot. I agree, because education is important for a child’s future; but borrowing money for piano lessons also puts great pressure on the family.
